<h1 id="hashicorp-vault-api">HashiCorp Vault API v1.15.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

HTTP API that gives you full access to Vault. All API routes are prefixed with `/v1/`.

<h1 id="hashicorp-vault-api-auth">auth</h1>

## List token accessors, which can then be be used to iterate and discover their properties or revoke them. Because this can be used to cause a denial of service, this endpoint requires 'sudo' capability in addition to 'list'.

<a id="opIdtoken-list-accessors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/token/accessors/?list=true' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /auth/token/accessors/`

<h3 id="list-token-accessors-which-can-then-be-be-used-to-iterate-and-discover-their-properties-or-revoke-them-because-this-can-be-used-to-cause-a-denial-of-service-this-endpoint-requires-sudo-capability-in-addition-to-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|list|query|string|true|Must be set to `true`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|list|true|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "keys": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-token-accessors-which-can-then-be-be-used-to-iterate-and-discover-their-properties-or-revoke-them-because-this-can-be-used-to-cause-a-denial-of-service-this-endpoint-requires-sudo-capability-in-addition-to-list-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[StandardListResponse](#schemastandardlistresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## The token create path is used to create new tokens.

<a id="opIdtoken-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/token/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "display_name": "string",
    "entity_alias": "string",
    "explicit_max_ttl": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "lease": "string",
    "meta": {},
    "no_default_policy": true,
    "no_parent": true,
    "num_uses": 0,
    "period": "string",
    "policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "renewable": true,
    "ttl": "string",
    "type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/token/create`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "display_name": "string",
  "entity_alias": "string",
  "explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "lease": "string",
  "meta": {},
  "no_default_policy": true,
  "no_parent": true,
  "num_uses": 0,
  "period": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "renewable": true,
  "ttl": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="the-token-create-path-is-used-to-create-new-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TokenCreateRequest](#schematokencreaterequest)|true|none|
|» display_name|body|string|false|Name to associate with this token|
|» entity_alias|body|string|false|Name of the entity alias to associate with this token|
|» explicit_max_ttl|body|string|false|Explicit Max TTL of this token|
|» id|body|string|false|Value for the token|
|» lease|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Use 'ttl' instead|
|» meta|body|object(kvpairs)|false|Arbitrary key=value metadata to associate with the token|
|» no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|Do not include default policy for this token|
|» no_parent|body|boolean|false|Create the token with no parent|
|» num_uses|body|integer|false|Max number of uses for this token|
|» period|body|string|false|Renew period|
|» policies|body|[string]|false|List of policies for the token|
|» renewable|body|boolean|false|Allow token to be renewed past its initial TTL up to system/mount maximum TTL|
|» ttl|body|string|false|Time to live for this token|
|» type|body|string|false|Token type|

<h3 id="the-token-create-path-is-used-to-create-new-tokens-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
```
```bash
    "increment": 0,
    "token": "string"
```

```json
  "token": "string"
}
```

## token-write-role

<a id="opIdtoken-write-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/token/roles/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "allowed_entity_aliases": [
      "string"
    ],
    "allowed_policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "allowed_policies_glob": [
      "string"
    ],
    "bound_cidrs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "disallowed_policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "disallowed_policies_glob": [
      "string"
    ],
    "explicit_max_ttl": "string",
    "orphan": true,
    "path_suffix": "string",
    "period": "string",
    "renewable": true,
    "token_bound_cidrs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
```

```json
  ],

    "string"
  ],

  ],

  ],

  "period": "string",
  "renewable": true,
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service"
}
```

<h3 id="token-write-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role_name|path|string|true|Name of the role|
|body|body|[TokenWriteRoleRequest](#schematokenwriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» allowed_entity_aliases|body|[string]|false|String or JSON list of allowed entity aliases. If set, specifies the entity aliases which are allowed to be used during token generation. This field supports globbing.|
|» allowed_policies|body|[string]|false|If set, tokens can be created with any subset of the policies in this list, rather than the normal semantics of tokens being a subset of the calling token's policies. The parameter is a comma-delimited string of policy names.|
|» allowed_policies_glob|body|[string]|false|If set, tokens can be created with any subset of glob matched policies in this list, rather than the normal semantics of tokens being a subset of the calling token's policies. The parameter is a comma-delimited string of policy name globs.|
|» bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use 'token_bound_cidrs' instead.|
|» disallowed_policies|body|[string]|false|If set, successful token creation via this role will require that no policies in the given list are requested. The parameter is a comma-delimited string of policy names.|
|» disallowed_policies_glob|body|[string]|false|If set, successful token creation via this role will require that no requested policies glob match any of policies in this list. The parameter is a comma-delimited string of policy name globs.|
|» explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use 'token_explicit_max_ttl' instead.|
|» orphan|body|boolean|false|If true, tokens created via this role will be orphan tokens (have no parent)|
|» path_suffix|body|string|false|If set, tokens created via this role will contain the given suffix as a part of their path. This can be used to assist use of the 'revoke-prefix' endpoint later on. The given suffix must match the regular expression.\w[\w-.]+\w|
|» period|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use 'token_period' instead.|
|» renewable|body|boolean|false|Tokens created via this role will be renewable or not according to this value. Defaults to "true".|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

```bash
  ],

  ],
```

## aws-configure-certificate

<a id="opIdaws-configure-certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/aws/config/certificate/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "aws_public_cert": "string",
    "type": "pkcs7"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{aws_mount_path}/config/certificate/{cert_name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "aws_public_cert": "string",
  "type": "pkcs7"
}
```

<h3 id="aws-configure-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cert_name|path|string|true|Name of the certificate.|
|aws_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[AwsConfigureCertificateRequest](#schemaawsconfigurecertificaterequest)|true|none|
|» aws_public_cert|body|string|false|Base64 encoded AWS Public cert required to verify PKCS7 signature of the EC2 instance metadata.|
|» type|body|string|false|Takes the value of either "pkcs7" or "identity", indicating the type of document which can be verified using the given certificate. The reason is that the PKCS#7 document will have a DSA digest and the identity signature will have an RSA signature, and accordingly the public certificates to verify those also vary. Defaults to "pkcs7".|

<h3 id="aws-configure-certificate-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
    "string"
```
```bash
  ],

  "iam_endpoint": "",
```

## aws-configure-identity-integration

<a id="opIdaws-configure-identity-integration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/aws/config/identity \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ec2_alias": "instance_id",
    "ec2_metadata": [
      "default"
    ],
    "iam_alias": "unique_id",
    "iam_metadata": [
      "default"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{aws_mount_path}/config/identity`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ec2_alias": "instance_id",
  "ec2_metadata": [
    "default"
  ],
  "iam_alias": "unique_id",
  "iam_metadata": [
    "default"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="aws-configure-identity-integration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aws_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[AwsConfigureIdentityIntegrationRequest](#schemaawsconfigureidentityintegrationrequest)|true|none|
|» ec2_alias|body|string|false|Configure how the AWS auth method generates entity alias when using EC2 auth. Valid values are "role_id", "instance_id", and "image_id". Defaults to "role_id".|
|» ec2_metadata|body|[string]|false|The metadata to include on the aliases and audit logs generated by this plugin. When set to 'default', includes: account_id, auth_type. These fields are available to add: ami_id, instance_id, region. Not editing this field means the 'default' fields are included. Explicitly setting this field to empty overrides the 'default' and means no metadata will be included. If not using 'default', explicit fields must be sent like: 'field1,field2'.|
|» iam_alias|body|string|false|Configure how the AWS auth method generates entity aliases when using IAM auth. Valid values are "role_id", "unique_id", and "full_arn". Defaults to "role_id".|
|» iam_metadata|body|[string]|false|The metadata to include on the aliases and audit logs generated by this plugin. When set to 'default', includes: account_id, auth_type. These fields are available to add: canonical_arn, client_arn, client_user_id, inferred_aws_region, inferred_entity_id, inferred_entity_type. Not editing this field means the 'default' fields are included. Explicitly setting this field to empty overrides the 'default' and means no metadata will be included. If not using 'default', explicit fields must be sent like: 'field1,field2'.|

<h3 id="aws-configure-identity-integration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## aws-login

<a id="opIdaws-login"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/aws/login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "iam_http_request_method": "string",
    "iam_request_body": "string",
    "iam_request_headers": "string",
    "iam_request_url": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "nonce": "string",
    "pkcs7": "string",
    "role": "string",
    "signature": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{aws_mount_path}/login`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "iam_http_request_method": "string",
  "iam_request_body": "string",
  "iam_request_headers": "string",
  "iam_request_url": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "nonce": "string",
  "pkcs7": "string",
  "role": "string",
  "signature": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="aws-login-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aws_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[AwsLoginRequest](#schemaawsloginrequest)|true|none|
|» iam_http_request_method|body|string|false|HTTP method to use for the AWS request when auth_type is iam. This must match what has been signed in the presigned request.|
|» iam_request_body|body|string|false|Base64-encoded request body when auth_type is iam. This must match the request body included in the signature.|
|» iam_request_headers|body|string|false|Key/value pairs of headers for use in the sts:GetCallerIdentity HTTP requests headers when auth_type is iam. Can be either a Base64-encoded, JSON-serialized string, or a JSON object of key/value pairs. This must at a minimum include the headers over which AWS has included a signature.|
|» iam_request_url|body|string|false|Base64-encoded full URL against which to make the AWS request when using iam auth_type.|
|» identity|body|string|false|Base64 encoded EC2 instance identity document. This needs to be supplied along with the 'signature' parameter. If using 'curl' for fetching the identity document, consider using the option '-w 0' while piping the output to 'base64' binary.|
|» nonce|body|string|false|The nonce to be used for subsequent login requests when auth_type is ec2. If this parameter is not specified at all and if reauthentication is allowed, then the backend will generate a random nonce, attaches it to the instance's identity access list entry and returns the nonce back as part of auth metadata. This value should be used with further login requests, to establish client authenticity. Clients can choose to set a custom nonce if preferred, in which case, it is recommended that clients provide a strong nonce. If a nonce is provided but with an empty value, it indicates intent to disable reauthentication. Note that, when 'disallow_reauthentication' option is enabled on either the role or the role tag, the 'nonce' holds no significance.|
|» pkcs7|body|string|false|PKCS7 signature of the identity document when using an auth_type of ec2.|
|» role|body|string|false|Name of the role against which the login is being attempted. If 'role' is not specified, then the login endpoint looks for a role bearing the name of the AMI ID of the EC2 instance that is trying to login. If a matching role is not found, login fails.|
|» signature|body|string|false|Base64 encoded SHA256 RSA signature of the instance identity document. This needs to be supplied along with 'identity' parameter.|

<h3 id="aws-login-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
  "inferred_entity_type": "string",
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "period": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "resolve_aws_unique_ids": true,
  "role_tag": "",
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="aws-write-auth-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|path|string|true|Name of the role.|
|aws_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[AwsWriteAuthRoleRequest](#schemaawswriteauthrolerequest)|true|none|
|» allow_instance_migration|body|boolean|false|If set, allows migration of the underlying instance where the client resides. This keys off of pendingTime in the metadata document, so essentially, this disables the client nonce check whenever the instance is migrated to a new host and pendingTime is newer than the previously-remembered time. Use with caution. This is only checked when auth_type is ec2.|
|» auth_type|body|string|false|The auth_type permitted to authenticate to this role. Must be one of iam or ec2 and cannot be changed after role creation.|
|» bound_account_id|body|[string]|false|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances that the account ID in its identity document to match one of the IDs specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|» bound_ami_id|body|[string]|false|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances that they should be using one of the AMI IDs specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|» bound_ec2_instance_id|body|[string]|false|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances to have one of the given instance IDs. Can be a list or comma-separated string of EC2 instance IDs. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|» bound_iam_instance_profile_arn|body|[string]|false|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances to be associated with an IAM instance profile ARN which has a prefix that matches one of the values specified by this parameter. The value is prefix-matched (as though it were a glob ending in '*'). This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|» bound_iam_principal_arn|body|[string]|false|ARN of the IAM principals to bind to this role. Only applicable when auth_type is iam.|
|» bound_iam_role_arn|body|[string]|false|If set, defines a constraint on the authenticating EC2 instance that it must match one of the IAM role ARNs specified by this parameter. The value is prefix-matched (as though it were a glob ending in '*'). The configured IAM user or EC2 instance role must be allowed to execute the 'iam:GetInstanceProfile' action if this is specified. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|» bound_region|body|[string]|false|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances that the region in its identity document match one of the regions specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2.|
|» bound_subnet_id|body|[string]|false|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instance to be associated with the subnet ID that matches one of the values specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|» bound_vpc_id|body|[string]|false|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instance to be associated with a VPC ID that matches one of the value specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|» disallow_reauthentication|body|boolean|false|If set, only allows a single token to be granted per instance ID. In order to perform a fresh login, the entry in the access list for the instance ID needs to be cleared using 'auth/aws-ec2/identity-accesslist/<instance_id>' endpoint. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2.|
|» inferred_aws_region|body|string|false|When auth_type is iam and inferred_entity_type is set, the region to assume the inferred entity exists in.|
|» inferred_entity_type|body|string|false|When auth_type is iam, the AWS entity type to infer from the authenticated principal. The only supported value is ec2_instance, which will extract the EC2 instance ID from the authenticated role and apply the following restrictions specific to EC2 instances: bound_ami_id, bound_account_id, bound_iam_role_arn, bound_iam_instance_profile_arn, bound_vpc_id, bound_subnet_id. The configured EC2 client must be able to find the inferred instance ID in the results, and the instance must be running. If unable to determine the EC2 instance ID or unable to find the EC2 instance ID among running instances, then authentication will fail.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|» period|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|» policies|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|» resolve_aws_unique_ids|body|boolean|false|If set, resolve all AWS IAM ARNs into AWS's internal unique IDs. When an IAM entity (e.g., user, role, or instance profile) is deleted, then all references to it within the role will be invalidated, which prevents a new IAM entity from being created with the same name and matching the role's IAM binds. Once set, this cannot be unset.|
|» role_tag|body|string|false|If set, enables the role tags for this role. The value set for this field should be the 'key' of the tag on the EC2 instance. The 'value' of the tag should be generated using 'role/<role>/tag' endpoint. Defaults to an empty string, meaning that role tags are disabled. This is only allowed if auth_type is ec2.|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|

The metadata key will be the string consisting of the oid numbers separated by a dash (-) instead of a dot (.) to allow usage in ACL templates.|
|» allowed_names|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of names. At least one must exist in either the Common Name or SANs. Supports globbing. This parameter is deprecated, please use allowed_common_names, allowed_dns_sans, allowed_email_sans, allowed_uri_sans.|
|» allowed_organizational_units|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of Organizational Units names. At least one must exist in the OU field.|
|» allowed_uri_sans|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of URIs. At least one must exist in the SANs. Supports globbing.|
|» bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_bound_cidrs" instead. If this and "token_bound_cidrs" are both specified, only "token_bound_cidrs" will be used.|
|» certificate|body|string|false|The public certificate that should be trusted. Must be x509 PEM encoded.|
|» display_name|body|string|false|The display name to use for clients using this certificate.|
|» lease|body|integer|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|» ocsp_ca_certificates|body|string|false|Any additional CA certificates needed to communicate with OCSP servers|
|» ocsp_enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether to attempt OCSP verification of certificates at login|
|» ocsp_fail_open|body|boolean|false|If set to true, if an OCSP revocation cannot be made successfully, login will proceed rather than failing. If false, failing to get an OCSP status fails the request.|
|» ocsp_query_all_servers|body|boolean|false|If set to true, rather than accepting the first successful OCSP response, query all servers and consider the certificate valid only if all servers agree.|
|» ocsp_servers_override|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of OCSP server addresses. If unset, the OCSP server is determined from the AuthorityInformationAccess extension on the certificate being inspected.|
|» period|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|» policies|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|» required_extensions|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated string or array of extensions formatted as "oid:value". Expects the extension value to be some type of ASN1 encoded string. All values much match. Supports globbing on "value".|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

<h3 id="manage-trusted-certificates-used-for-authentication-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

```json
{

  "gce_alias": "role_id",
  "gce_metadata": [
    "default"
  ],
  "google_certs_endpoint": "string",
  "iam_alias": "role_id",
  "iam_metadata": [
    "default"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="google-cloud-configure-auth-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|gcp_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[GoogleCloudConfigureAuthRequest](#schemagooglecloudconfigureauthrequest)|true|none|
|» credentials|body|string|false|Google credentials JSON that Vault will use to verify users against GCP APIs. If not specified, will use application default credentials|
|» custom_endpoint|body|object(kvpairs)|false|Specifies overrides for various Google API Service Endpoints used in requests.|
|» gce_alias|body|string|false|Indicates what value to use when generating an alias for GCE authentications.|
|» gce_metadata|body|[string]|false|The metadata to include on the aliases and audit logs generated by this plugin. When set to 'default', includes: instance_creation_timestamp, instance_id, instance_name, project_id, project_number, role, service_account_id, service_account_email, zone. Not editing this field means the 'default' fields are included. Explicitly setting this field to empty overrides the 'default' and means no metadata will be included. If not using 'default', explicit fields must be sent like: 'field1,field2'.|
|» google_certs_endpoint|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. This field does nothing and be removed in a future release|
|» iam_alias|body|string|false|Indicates what value to use when generating an alias for IAM authentications.|
|» iam_metadata|body|[string]|false|The metadata to include on the aliases and audit logs generated by this plugin. When set to 'default', includes: project_id, role, service_account_id, service_account_email. Not editing this field means the 'default' fields are included. Explicitly setting this field to empty overrides the 'default' and means no metadata will be included. If not using 'default', explicit fields must be sent like: 'field1,field2'.|

<h3 id="create-a-gcp-role-with-associated-policies-and-required-attributes-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the role.|
|gcp_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[GoogleCloudWriteRoleRequest](#schemagooglecloudwriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» add_group_aliases|body|boolean|false|If true, will add group aliases to auth tokens generated under this role. This will add the full list of ancestors (projects, folders, organizations) for the given entity's project. Requires IAM permission `resourcemanager.projects.get` on this project.|
|» allow_gce_inference|body|boolean|false|'iam' roles only. If false, Vault will not not allow GCE instances to login in against this role|
|» bound_instance_group|body|string|false|Deprecated: use "bound_instance_groups" instead.|
|» bound_instance_groups|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of permitted instance groups to which the GCE instance must belong. This option only applies to "gce" roles.|
|» bound_labels|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of GCP labels formatted as"key:value" strings that must be present on the GCE instance in order to authenticate. This option only applies to "gce" roles.|
|» bound_projects|body|[string]|false|GCP Projects that authenticating entities must belong to.|
|» bound_region|body|string|false|Deprecated: use "bound_regions" instead.|
|» bound_regions|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of permitted regions to which the GCE instance must belong. If a group is provided, it is assumed to be a regional group. If "zone" is provided, this option is ignored. This can be a self-link or region name. This option only applies to "gce" roles.|
|» bound_service_accounts|body|[string]|false|Can be set for both 'iam' and 'gce' roles (required for 'iam'). A comma-seperated list of authorized service accounts. If the single value "*" is given, this is assumed to be all service accounts under the role's project. If this is set on a GCE role, the inferred service account from the instance metadata token will be used.|
|» bound_zone|body|string|false|Deprecated: use "bound_zones" instead.|
|» bound_zones|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of permitted zones to which the GCE instance must belong. If a group is provided, it is assumed to be a zonal group. This can be a self-link or zone name. This option only applies to "gce" roles.|
|» max_jwt_exp|body|string(duration)|false|Currently enabled for 'iam' only. Duration in seconds from time of validation that a JWT must expire within.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|» period|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|» policies|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|» project_id|body|string|false|Deprecated: use "bound_projects" instead|
|» service_accounts|body|[string]|false|Deprecated: use "bound_service_accounts" instead.|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the role. Currently supported: iam, gce|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any policies configured for specific users/groups.|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

<h3 id="github-configure-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Configure the JWT authentication backend.

<a id="opIdjwt-configure"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/jwt/config \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "bound_issuer": "string",
    "default_role": "string",
    "jwks_ca_pem": "string",
    "jwks_url": "string",
    "jwt_supported_algs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "jwt_validation_pubkeys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "namespace_in_state": true,
    "oidc_client_id": "string",
    "oidc_client_secret": "string",
    "oidc_discovery_ca_pem": "string",
    "oidc_discovery_url": "string",
    "oidc_response_mode": "string",
    "oidc_response_types": [
      "string"
    ],
    "provider_config": {}
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{jwt_mount_path}/config`

The JWT authentication backend validates JWTs (or OIDC) using the configured
credentials. If using OIDC Discovery, the URL must be provided, along
with (optionally) the CA cert to use for the connection. If performing JWT
validation locally, a set of public keys must be provided.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bound_issuer": "string",
  "default_role": "string",
  "jwks_ca_pem": "string",
  "jwks_url": "string",
  "jwt_supported_algs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "jwt_validation_pubkeys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "namespace_in_state": true,
  "oidc_client_id": "string",
  "oidc_client_secret": "string",
  "oidc_discovery_ca_pem": "string",
  "oidc_discovery_url": "string",
  "oidc_response_mode": "string",
  "oidc_response_types": [
    "string"
  ],
  "provider_config": {}
}
```

<h3 id="configure-the-jwt-authentication-backend-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|jwt_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[JwtConfigureRequest](#schemajwtconfigurerequest)|true|none|
|» bound_issuer|body|string|false|The value against which to match the 'iss' claim in a JWT. Optional.|
|» default_role|body|string(lowercase)|false|The default role to use if none is provided during login. If not set, a role is required during login.|
|» jwks_ca_pem|body|string|false|The CA certificate or chain of certificates, in PEM format, to use to validate connections to the JWKS URL. If not set, system certificates are used.|
|» jwks_url|body|string|false|JWKS URL to use to authenticate signatures. Cannot be used with "oidc_discovery_url" or "jwt_validation_pubkeys".|
|» jwt_supported_algs|body|[string]|false|A list of supported signing algorithms. Defaults to RS256.|
|» jwt_validation_pubkeys|body|[string]|false|A list of PEM-encoded public keys to use to authenticate signatures locally. Cannot be used with "jwks_url" or "oidc_discovery_url".|
|» namespace_in_state|body|boolean|false|Pass namespace in the OIDC state parameter instead of as a separate query parameter. With this setting, the allowed redirect URL(s) in Vault and on the provider side should not contain a namespace query parameter. This means only one redirect URL entry needs to be maintained on the provider side for all vault namespaces that will be authenticating against it. Defaults to true for new configs.|
|» oidc_client_id|body|string|false|The OAuth Client ID configured with your OIDC provider.|
|» oidc_client_secret|body|string|false|The OAuth Client Secret configured with your OIDC provider.|
|» oidc_discovery_ca_pem|body|string|false|The CA certificate or chain of certificates, in PEM format, to use to validate connections to the OIDC Discovery URL. If not set, system certificates are used.|
|» oidc_discovery_url|body|string|false|OIDC Discovery URL, without any .well-known component (base path). Cannot be used with "jwks_url" or "jwt_validation_pubkeys".|
|» oidc_response_mode|body|string|false|The response mode to be used in the OAuth2 request. Allowed values are 'query' and 'form_post'.|
|» oidc_response_types|body|[string]|false|The response types to request. Allowed values are 'code' and 'id_token'. Defaults to 'code'.|
|» provider_config|body|object(map)|false|Provider-specific configuration. Optional.|

<h3 id="configure-the-jwt-authentication-backend-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
    "user_claim": "string",
    "user_claim_json_pointer": true,
    "verbose_oidc_logging": true
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{jwt_mount_path}/role/{name}`

A role is required to authenticate with this backend. The role binds
		JWT token information with token policies and settings.
		The bindings, token polices and token settings can all be configured
		using this endpoint

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowed_redirect_uris": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_audiences": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_claims": {},
  "bound_claims_type": "string",
  "bound_subject": "string",
  "claim_mappings": {},
  "clock_skew_leeway": 60000000000,
  "expiration_leeway": 150,
  "groups_claim": "string",
  "max_age": "string",
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "not_before_leeway": 150,
  "num_uses": 0,
  "oidc_scopes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "period": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "role_type": "string",
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string",
  "user_claim": "string",
  "user_claim_json_pointer": true,
  "verbose_oidc_logging": true
}
```

<h3 id="register-an-role-with-the-backend-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the role.|
|jwt_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[JwtWriteRoleRequest](#schemajwtwriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» allowed_redirect_uris|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of allowed values for redirect_uri|
|» bound_audiences|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of 'aud' claims that are valid for login; any match is sufficient|
|» bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_bound_cidrs" instead. If this and "token_bound_cidrs" are both specified, only "token_bound_cidrs" will be used.|
|» bound_claims|body|object(map)|false|Map of claims/values which must match for login|
|» bound_claims_type|body|string|false|How to interpret values in the map of claims/values (which must match for login): allowed values are 'string' or 'glob'|
|» bound_subject|body|string|false|The 'sub' claim that is valid for login. Optional.|
|» claim_mappings|body|object(kvpairs)|false|Mappings of claims (key) that will be copied to a metadata field (value)|
|» clock_skew_leeway|body|string(duration)|false|Duration in seconds of leeway when validating all claims to account for clock skew. Defaults to 60 (1 minute) if set to 0 and can be disabled if set to -1.|
|» expiration_leeway|body|string(duration)|false|Duration in seconds of leeway when validating expiration of a token to account for clock skew. Defaults to 150 (2.5 minutes) if set to 0 and can be disabled if set to -1.|
|» groups_claim|body|string|false|The claim to use for the Identity group alias names|
|» max_age|body|string(duration)|false|Specifies the allowable elapsed time in seconds since the last time the user was actively authenticated.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|» not_before_leeway|body|string(duration)|false|Duration in seconds of leeway when validating not before values of a token to account for clock skew. Defaults to 150 (2.5 minutes) if set to 0 and can be disabled if set to -1.|
|» num_uses|body|integer|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_num_uses" instead. If this and "token_num_uses" are both specified, only "token_num_uses" will be used.|
|» oidc_scopes|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of OIDC scopes|
|» period|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|» policies|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|» role_type|body|string|false|Type of the role, either 'jwt' or 'oidc'.|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|
|» user_claim|body|string|false|The claim to use for the Identity entity alias name|
|» user_claim_json_pointer|body|boolean|false|If true, the user_claim value will use JSON pointer syntax for referencing claims.|
|» verbose_oidc_logging|body|boolean|false|Log received OIDC tokens and claims when debug-level logging is active. Not recommended in production since sensitive information may be present in OIDC responses.|

<h3 id="register-an-role-with-the-backend-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## kerberos-configure-ldap

<a id="opIdkerberos-configure-ldap"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/kerberos/config/ldap \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "anonymous_group_search": false,
    "binddn": "string",
    "bindpass": "string",
    "case_sensitive_names": true,
    "certificate": "string",
    "client_tls_cert": "string",
    "client_tls_key": "string",
    "connection_timeout": "30s",
    "deny_null_bind": true,
    "dereference_aliases": "never",
    "discoverdn": true,
    "groupattr": "cn",
    "groupdn": "string",
    "groupfilter": "(|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))",
    "insecure_tls": true,
    "max_page_size": 0,
    "request_timeout": "90s",
    "starttls": true,
    "tls_max_version": "tls12",
    "tls_min_version": "tls12",
    "token_bound_cidrs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
    "token_max_ttl": "string",
    "token_no_default_policy": true,
    "token_num_uses": 0,
    "token_period": "string",
    "token_policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_ttl": "string",
    "token_type": "default-service",
    "upndomain": "string",
    "url": "ldap://127.0.0.1",
    "use_pre111_group_cn_behavior": true,
    "use_token_groups": false,
    "userattr": "cn",
    "userdn": "string",
    "userfilter": "({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})",
    "username_as_alias": false
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{kerberos_mount_path}/config/ldap`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "anonymous_group_search": false,
  "binddn": "string",
  "bindpass": "string",
  "case_sensitive_names": true,
  "certificate": "string",
  "client_tls_cert": "string",
  "client_tls_key": "string",
  "connection_timeout": "30s",
  "deny_null_bind": true,
  "dereference_aliases": "never",
  "discoverdn": true,
  "groupattr": "cn",
  "groupdn": "string",
  "groupfilter": "(|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))",
  "insecure_tls": true,
  "max_page_size": 0,
  "request_timeout": "90s",
  "starttls": true,
  "tls_max_version": "tls12",
  "tls_min_version": "tls12",
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",

  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "upndomain": "string",
  "url": "ldap://127.0.0.1",
  "use_pre111_group_cn_behavior": true,
  "use_token_groups": false,
  "userattr": "cn",
  "userdn": "string",
  "userfilter": "({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})",
  "username_as_alias": false
}
```

<h3 id="kerberos-configure-ldap-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|kerberos_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[KerberosConfigureLdapRequest](#schemakerberosconfigureldaprequest)|true|none|
|» anonymous_group_search|body|boolean|false|Use anonymous binds when performing LDAP group searches (if true the initial credentials will still be used for the initial connection test).|
|» binddn|body|string|false|LDAP DN for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|» bindpass|body|string|false|LDAP password for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|» case_sensitive_names|body|boolean|false|If true, case sensitivity will be used when comparing usernames and groups for matching policies.|
|» certificate|body|string|false|CA certificate to use when verifying LDAP server certificate, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» client_tls_cert|body|string|false|Client certificate to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» client_tls_key|body|string|false|Client certificate key to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» connection_timeout|body|string(duration)|false|Timeout, in seconds, when attempting to connect to the LDAP server before trying the next URL in the configuration.|
|» deny_null_bind|body|boolean|false|Denies an unauthenticated LDAP bind request if the user's password is empty; defaults to true|
|» dereference_aliases|body|string|false|When aliases should be dereferenced on search operations. Accepted values are 'never', 'finding', 'searching', 'always'. Defaults to 'never'.|
|» discoverdn|body|boolean|false|Use anonymous bind to discover the bind DN of a user (optional)|
|» groupattr|body|string|false|LDAP attribute to follow on objects returned by <groupfilter> in order to enumerate user group membership. Examples: "cn" or "memberOf", etc. Default: cn|
|» groupdn|body|string|false|LDAP search base to use for group membership search (eg: ou=Groups,dc=example,dc=org)|
|» groupfilter|body|string|false|Go template for querying group membership of user (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserDN, Username Example: (&(objectClass=group)(member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:={{.UserDN}})) Default: (\|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))|
|» insecure_tls|body|boolean|false|Skip LDAP server SSL Certificate verification - VERY insecure (optional)|
|» max_page_size|body|integer|false|If set to a value greater than 0, the LDAP backend will use the LDAP server's paged search control to request pages of up to the given size. This can be used to avoid hitting the LDAP server's maximum result size limit. Otherwise, the LDAP backend will not use the paged search control.|
|» request_timeout|body|string(duration)|false|Timeout, in seconds, for the connection when making requests against the server before returning back an error.|
|» starttls|body|boolean|false|Issue a StartTLS command after establishing unencrypted connection (optional)|
|» tls_max_version|body|string|false|Maximum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|» tls_min_version|body|string|false|Minimum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any configured for specific users/groups.|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» upndomain|body|string|false|Enables userPrincipalDomain login with [username]@UPNDomain (optional)|
|» url|body|string|false|LDAP URL to connect to (default: ldap://127.0.0.1). Multiple URLs can be specified by concatenating them with commas; they will be tried in-order.|
|» use_pre111_group_cn_behavior|body|boolean|false|In Vault 1.1.1 a fix for handling group CN values of different cases unfortunately introduced a regression that could cause previously defined groups to not be found due to a change in the resulting name. If set true, the pre-1.1.1 behavior for matching group CNs will be used. This is only needed in some upgrade scenarios for backwards compatibility. It is enabled by default if the config is upgraded but disabled by default on new configurations.|
|» use_token_groups|body|boolean|false|If true, use the Active Directory tokenGroups constructed attribute of the user to find the group memberships. This will find all security groups including nested ones.|
|» userattr|body|string|false|Attribute used for users (default: cn)|
|» userdn|body|string|false|LDAP domain to use for users (eg: ou=People,dc=example,dc=org)|
|» userfilter|body|string|false|Go template for LDAP user search filer (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserAttr, Username Default: ({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})|
|» username_as_alias|body|boolean|false|If true, sets the alias name to the username|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» dereference_aliases|never|
|» dereference_aliases|finding|
|» dereference_aliases|searching|
|» dereference_aliases|always|
|» tls_max_version|tls10|
|» tls_max_version|tls11|
|» tls_max_version|tls12|
|» tls_max_version|tls13|
|» tls_min_version|tls10|
|» tls_min_version|tls11|
|» tls_min_version|tls12|
|» tls_min_version|tls13|

<h3 id="kerberos-configure-ldap-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

```json
      "string"
```
```bash
    ],
```

```json
  ],
```

```bash
  ],

  ],
```

```json
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="register-an-role-with-the-backend-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the role.|
|kubernetes_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[KubernetesWriteAuthRoleRequest](#schemakuberneteswriteauthrolerequest)|true|none|
|» alias_name_source|body|string|false|Source to use when deriving the Alias name. valid choices: "serviceaccount_uid" : <token.uid> e.g. 474b11b5-0f20-4f9d-8ca5-65715ab325e0 (most secure choice) "serviceaccount_name" : <namespace>/<serviceaccount> e.g. vault/vault-agent default: "serviceaccount_uid"|
|» audience|body|string|false|Optional Audience claim to verify in the jwt.|
|» bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_bound_cidrs" instead. If this and "token_bound_cidrs" are both specified, only "token_bound_cidrs" will be used.|
|» bound_service_account_names|body|[string]|false|List of service account names able to access this role. If set to "*" all names are allowed.|
|» bound_service_account_namespaces|body|[string]|false|List of namespaces allowed to access this role. If set to "*" all namespaces are allowed.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|» num_uses|body|integer|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_num_uses" instead. If this and "token_num_uses" are both specified, only "token_num_uses" will be used.|
|» period|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|» policies|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

```bash
    ],

    "token_type": "default-service",
    "upndomain": "string",
    "url": "ldap://127.0.0.1",
    "use_pre111_group_cn_behavior": true,
    "use_token_groups": false,
```

`POST /auth/{ldap_mount_path}/config`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "anonymous_group_search": false,
  "binddn": "string",
  "bindpass": "string",
  "case_sensitive_names": true,
  "certificate": "string",
  "client_tls_cert": "string",
  "client_tls_key": "string",
  "connection_timeout": "30s",

    "string"
  ],

  "token_type": "default-service",
  "upndomain": "string",
  "url": "ldap://127.0.0.1",
  "use_pre111_group_cn_behavior": true,
  "use_token_groups": false,
  "userattr": "cn",
  "userdn": "string",
  "userfilter": "({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})",
  "username_as_alias": false
}
```

<h3 id="ldap-configure-auth-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ldap_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[LdapConfigureAuthRequest](#schemaldapconfigureauthrequest)|true|none|
|» anonymous_group_search|body|boolean|false|Use anonymous binds when performing LDAP group searches (if true the initial credentials will still be used for the initial connection test).|
|» binddn|body|string|false|LDAP DN for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|» bindpass|body|string|false|LDAP password for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|» case_sensitive_names|body|boolean|false|If true, case sensitivity will be used when comparing usernames and groups for matching policies.|
|» certificate|body|string|false|CA certificate to use when verifying LDAP server certificate, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» client_tls_cert|body|string|false|Client certificate to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» client_tls_key|body|string|false|Client certificate key to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» connection_timeout|body|string(duration)|false|Timeout, in seconds, when attempting to connect to the LDAP server before trying the next URL in the configuration.|
|» deny_null_bind|body|boolean|false|Denies an unauthenticated LDAP bind request if the user's password is empty; defaults to true|
|» dereference_aliases|body|string|false|When aliases should be dereferenced on search operations. Accepted values are 'never', 'finding', 'searching', 'always'. Defaults to 'never'.|
|» discoverdn|body|boolean|false|Use anonymous bind to discover the bind DN of a user (optional)|
|» groupattr|body|string|false|LDAP attribute to follow on objects returned by <groupfilter> in order to enumerate user group membership. Examples: "cn" or "memberOf", etc. Default: cn|
|» groupdn|body|string|false|LDAP search base to use for group membership search (eg: ou=Groups,dc=example,dc=org)|
|» groupfilter|body|string|false|Go template for querying group membership of user (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserDN, Username Example: (&(objectClass=group)(member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:={{.UserDN}})) Default: (\|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))|
|» insecure_tls|body|boolean|false|Skip LDAP server SSL Certificate verification - VERY insecure (optional)|
|» max_page_size|body|integer|false|If set to a value greater than 0, the LDAP backend will use the LDAP server's paged search control to request pages of up to the given size. This can be used to avoid hitting the LDAP server's maximum result size limit. Otherwise, the LDAP backend will not use the paged search control.|
|» request_timeout|body|string(duration)|false|Timeout, in seconds, for the connection when making requests against the server before returning back an error.|
|» starttls|body|boolean|false|Issue a StartTLS command after establishing unencrypted connection (optional)|
|» tls_max_version|body|string|false|Maximum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|» tls_min_version|body|string|false|Minimum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any configured for specific users/groups.|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» upndomain|body|string|false|Enables userPrincipalDomain login with [username]@UPNDomain (optional)|
|» url|body|string|false|LDAP URL to connect to (default: ldap://127.0.0.1). Multiple URLs can be specified by concatenating them with commas; they will be tried in-order.|
|» use_pre111_group_cn_behavior|body|boolean|false|In Vault 1.1.1 a fix for handling group CN values of different cases unfortunately introduced a regression that could cause previously defined groups to not be found due to a change in the resulting name. If set true, the pre-1.1.1 behavior for matching group CNs will be used. This is only needed in some upgrade scenarios for backwards compatibility. It is enabled by default if the config is upgraded but disabled by default on new configurations.|
|» use_token_groups|body|boolean|false|If true, use the Active Directory tokenGroups constructed attribute of the user to find the group memberships. This will find all security groups including nested ones.|
|» userattr|body|string|false|Attribute used for users (default: cn)|
|» userdn|body|string|false|LDAP domain to use for users (eg: ou=People,dc=example,dc=org)|
|» userfilter|body|string|false|Go template for LDAP user search filer (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserAttr, Username Default: ({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})|
|» username_as_alias|body|boolean|false|If true, sets the alias name to the username|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» dereference_aliases|never|
|» dereference_aliases|finding|
|» dereference_aliases|searching|
|» dereference_aliases|always|
|» tls_max_version|tls10|
|» tls_max_version|tls11|
|» tls_max_version|tls12|
|» tls_max_version|tls13|
|» tls_min_version|tls10|
|» tls_min_version|tls11|
|» tls_min_version|tls12|
|» tls_min_version|tls13|

<h3 id="ldap-configure-auth-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

## Create a role and associate policies to it.

<a id="opIdoci-write-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/oci/role/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ocid_list": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_bound_cidrs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
    "token_max_ttl": "string",
    "token_no_default_policy": true,
    "token_num_uses": 0,
    "token_period": "string",
    "token_policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_ttl": "string",
    "token_type": "default-service"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{oci_mount_path}/role/{role}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ocid_list": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-role-and-associate-policies-to-it-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|path|string|true|Name of the role.|
|oci_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[OciWriteRoleRequest](#schemaociwriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» ocid_list|body|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Group or Dynamic Group OCIDs that are allowed to take this role.|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|

<h3 id="create-a-role-and-associate-policies-to-it-4-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## okta-configure

<a id="opIdokta-configure"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/okta/config \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "api_token": "string",
    "base_url": "string",
    "bypass_okta_mfa": true,
    "max_ttl": "string",
    "org_name": "string",
    "organization": "string",
    "production": true,
    "token": "string",
    "token_bound_cidrs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
    "token_max_ttl": "string",
    "token_no_default_policy": true,
    "token_num_uses": 0,
    "token_period": "string",
    "token_policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_ttl": "string",
    "token_type": "default-service",
    "ttl": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{okta_mount_path}/config`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "api_token": "string",
  "base_url": "string",
  "bypass_okta_mfa": true,
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "org_name": "string",
  "organization": "string",
  "production": true,
  "token": "string",
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="okta-configure-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|okta_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[OktaConfigureRequest](#schemaoktaconfigurerequest)|true|none|
|» api_token|body|string|false|Okta API key.|
|» base_url|body|string|false|The base domain to use for the Okta API. When not specified in the configuration, "okta.com" is used.|
|» bypass_okta_mfa|body|boolean|false|When set true, requests by Okta for a MFA check will be bypassed. This also disallows certain status checks on the account, such as whether the password is expired.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|» org_name|body|string|false|Name of the organization to be used in the Okta API.|
|» organization|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Use org_name instead.|
|» production|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Use base_url instead.|
|» token|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Use api_token instead.|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any configured for specific users/groups.|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

<h3 id="okta-configure-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>
