## radius-configure

<a id="opIdradius-configure"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/radius/config \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "dial_timeout": 10,
    "host": "string",
    "nas_identifier": "",
    "nas_port": 10,
    "port": 1812,
    "read_timeout": 10,
    "secret": "string",
    "token_bound_cidrs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
    "token_max_ttl": "string",
    "token_no_default_policy": true,
    "token_num_uses": 0,
    "token_period": "string",
    "token_policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_ttl": "string",
    "token_type": "default-service",
    "unregistered_user_policies": ""
  }'
```

`POST /auth/{radius_mount_path}/config`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dial_timeout": 10,
  "host": "string",
  "nas_identifier": "",
  "nas_port": 10,
  "port": 1812,
  "read_timeout": 10,
  "secret": "string",
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "unregistered_user_policies": ""
}
```

<h3 id="radius-configure-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|radius_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[RadiusConfigureRequest](#schemaradiusconfigurerequest)|true|none|
|» dial_timeout|body|string(duration)|false|Number of seconds before connect times out (default: 10)|
|» host|body|string|false|RADIUS server host|
|» nas_identifier|body|string|false|RADIUS NAS Identifier field (optional)|
|» nas_port|body|integer|false|RADIUS NAS port field (default: 10)|
|» port|body|integer|false|RADIUS server port (default: 1812)|
|» read_timeout|body|string(duration)|false|Number of seconds before response times out (default: 10)|
|» secret|body|string|false|Secret shared with the RADIUS server|
|» token_bound_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|» token_explicit_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|» token_no_default_policy|body|boolean|false|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|» token_num_uses|body|integer|false|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any configured for specific users.|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» unregistered_user_policies|body|string|false|Comma-separated list of policies to grant upon successful RADIUS authentication of an unregistered user (default: empty)|

<h3 id="radius-configure-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|» token_period|body|string(duration)|false|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|» token_policies|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of policies|
|» token_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

<h3 id="manage-users-allowed-to-authenticate-14-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">

```bash
    "iam_groups": [
      "string"
    ],
    "iam_tags": {},
    "max_sts_ttl": "string",
    "permissions_boundary_arn": "string",
    "policy": "string",
    "policy_arns": [
      "string"
    ],
    "policy_document": "string",
    "role_arns": [
      "string"
    ],
    "user_path": "/"
  }'
```

`POST /{aws_mount_path}/roles/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "arn": "string",
  "credential_type": "string",
  "default_sts_ttl": "string",
  "iam_groups": [
    "string"
  ],
  "iam_tags": {},
  "max_sts_ttl": "string",
  "permissions_boundary_arn": "string",
  "policy": "string",
  "policy_arns": [
    "string"
  ],
  "policy_document": "string",
  "role_arns": [
    "string"
  ],
  "user_path": "/"
}
```

<h3 id="read-write-and-reference-iam-policies-that-access-keys-can-be-made-for-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the role|
|aws_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[AwsWriteRoleRequest](#schemaawswriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» arn|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Use role_arns or policy_arns instead.|
|» credential_type|body|string|false|Type of credential to retrieve. Must be one of assumed_role, iam_user, or federation_token|
|» default_sts_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|Default TTL for assumed_role and federation_token credential types when no TTL is explicitly requested with the credentials|
|» iam_groups|body|[string]|false|Names of IAM groups that generated IAM users will be added to. For a credential type of assumed_role or federation_token, the policies sent to the corresponding AWS call (sts:AssumeRole or sts:GetFederation) will be the policies from each group in iam_groups combined with the policy_document and policy_arns parameters.|
|» iam_tags|body|object(kvpairs)|false|IAM tags to be set for any users created by this role. These must be presented as Key-Value pairs. This can be represented as a map or a list of equal sign delimited key pairs.|
|» max_sts_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|Max allowed TTL for assumed_role and federation_token credential types|
|» permissions_boundary_arn|body|string|false|ARN of an IAM policy to attach as a permissions boundary on IAM user credentials; only valid when credential_type isiam_user|
|» policy|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Use policy_document instead.|
|» policy_arns|body|[string]|false|ARNs of AWS policies. Behavior varies by credential_type. When credential_type is iam_user, then it will attach the specified policies to the generated IAM user. When credential_type is assumed_role or federation_token, the policies will be passed as the PolicyArns parameter, acting as a filter on permissions available.|
|» policy_document|body|string|false|JSON-encoded IAM policy document. Behavior varies by credential_type. When credential_type is iam_user, then it will attach the contents of the policy_document to the IAM user generated. When credential_type is assumed_role or federation_token, this will be passed in as the Policy parameter to the AssumeRole or GetFederationToken API call, acting as a filter on permissions available.|
|» role_arns|body|[string]|false|ARNs of AWS roles allowed to be assumed. Only valid when credential_type is assumed_role|
|» user_path|body|string|false|Path for IAM User. Only valid when credential_type is iam_user|

## consul-write-role

<a id="opIdconsul-write-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/consul/roles/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "consul_namespace": "string",
    "consul_policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "consul_roles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "lease": "string",
    "local": true,
    "max_ttl": "string",
    "node_identities": [
      "string"
    ],
    "partition": "string",
    "policies": [
      "string"
    ],
    "policy": "string",
    "service_identities": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_type": "client",
    "ttl": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{consul_mount_path}/roles/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "consul_namespace": "string",
  "consul_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "consul_roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "lease": "string",
  "local": true,
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "node_identities": [
    "string"
  ],
  "partition": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "policy": "string",
  "service_identities": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_type": "client",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="consul-write-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the role.|
|consul_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[ConsulWriteRoleRequest](#schemaconsulwriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» consul_namespace|body|string|false|Indicates which namespace that the token will be created within. Defaults to 'default'. Available in Consul 1.7 and above.|
|» consul_policies|body|[string]|false|List of policies to attach to the token. Either "consul_policies" or "consul_roles" are required for Consul 1.5 and above, or just "consul_policies" if using Consul 1.4.|
|» consul_roles|body|[string]|false|List of Consul roles to attach to the token. Either "policies" or "consul_roles" are required for Consul 1.5 and above.|
|» lease|body|string(duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Use "ttl" instead.|
|» local|body|boolean|false|Indicates that the token should not be replicated globally and instead be local to the current datacenter. Available in Consul 1.4 and above.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|Max TTL for the Consul token created from the role.|
|» node_identities|body|[string]|false|List of Node Identities to attach to the token. Available in Consul 1.8.1 or above.|
|» partition|body|string|false|Indicates which admin partition that the token will be created within. Defaults to 'default'. Available in Consul 1.11 and above.|
|» policies|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Use "consul_policies" instead.|
|» policy|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Policy document, base64 encoded. Required for 'client' tokens. Required for Consul pre-1.4.|
|» service_identities|body|[string]|false|List of Service Identities to attach to the token, separated by semicolons. Available in Consul 1.5 or above.|
|» token_type|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Which type of token to create: 'client' or 'management'. If a 'management' token, the "policy", "policies", and "consul_roles" parameters are not required. Defaults to 'client'.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|TTL for the Consul token created from the role.|

<h3 id="consul-write-role-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/database/config/string \

    "allowed_roles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "password_policy": "string",
    "plugin_name": "string",
    "plugin_version": "string",
    "root_rotation_statements": [
      "string"
    ],
    "verify_connection": true
  }'
```

`POST /{database_mount_path}/config/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowed_roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "password_policy": "string",
  "plugin_name": "string",
  "plugin_version": "string",
  "root_rotation_statements": [
    "string"
  ],
  "verify_connection": true
}
```

<h3 id="database-configure-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of this database connection|
|database_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[DatabaseConfigureConnectionRequest](#schemadatabaseconfigureconnectionrequest)|true|none|
|» allowed_roles|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or array of the role names allowed to get creds from this database connection. If empty no roles are allowed. If "*" all roles are allowed.|
|» password_policy|body|string|false|Password policy to use when generating passwords.|
|» plugin_name|body|string|false|The name of a builtin or previously registered plugin known to vault. This endpoint will create an instance of that plugin type.|
|» plugin_version|body|string|false|The version of the plugin to use.|
|» root_rotation_statements|body|[string]|false|Specifies the database statements to be executed to rotate the root user's credentials. See the plugin's API page for more information on support and formatting for this parameter.|
|» verify_connection|body|boolean|false|If true, the connection details are verified by actually connecting to the database. Defaults to true.|

<a id="opIddatabase-write-static-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/database/static-roles/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "credential_config": {},
    "credential_type": "password",
    "db_name": "string",
    "rotation_period": "string",
    "rotation_schedule": "string",
    "rotation_statements": [
      "string"
    ],
    "rotation_window": "string",
    "username": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{database_mount_path}/static-roles/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "credential_config": {},
  "credential_type": "password",
  "db_name": "string",
  "rotation_period": "string",
  "rotation_schedule": "string",
  "rotation_statements": [
    "string"
  ],
  "rotation_window": "string",
  "username": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="manage-the-static-roles-that-can-be-created-with-this-backend-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the role.|
|database_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[DatabaseWriteStaticRoleRequest](#schemadatabasewritestaticrolerequest)|true|none|
|» credential_config|body|object(kvpairs)|false|The configuration for the given credential_type.|
|» credential_type|body|string|false|The type of credential to manage. Options include: 'password', 'rsa_private_key'. Defaults to 'password'.|
|» db_name|body|string|false|Name of the database this role acts on.|
|» rotation_period|body|string(duration)|false|Period for automatic credential rotation of the given username. Not valid unless used with "username". Mutually exclusive with "rotation_schedule."|
|» rotation_schedule|body|string|false|Schedule for automatic credential rotation of the given username. Mutually exclusive with "rotation_period."|
|» rotation_statements|body|[string]|false|Specifies the database statements to be executed to rotate the accounts credentials. Not every plugin type will support this functionality. See the plugin's API page for more information on support and formatting for this parameter.|
|» rotation_window|body|string(duration)|false|The window of time in which rotations are allowed to occur starting from a given "rotation_schedule". Requires "rotation_schedule" to be specified|
|» username|body|string|false|Name of the static user account for Vault to manage. Requires "rotation_period" to be specified|

<h3 id="manage-the-static-roles-that-can-be-created-with-this-backend-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Decrypt a ciphertext value using a named key

<a id="opIdgoogle-cloud-kms-decrypt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/gcpkms/decrypt/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "additional_authenticated_data": "string",
    "ciphertext": "string",
    "key_version": 0
  }'
```

`POST /{gcpkms_mount_path}/decrypt/{key}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "additional_authenticated_data": "string",
  "ciphertext": "string",
  "key_version": 0
}
```

<h3 id="decrypt-a-ciphertext-value-using-a-named-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|Name of the key in Vault to use for decryption. This key must already exist in Vault and must map back to a Google Cloud KMS key.|
|gcpkms_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[GoogleCloudKmsDecryptRequest](#schemagooglecloudkmsdecryptrequest)|true|none|
|» additional_authenticated_data|body|string|false|Optional data that was specified during encryption of this payload.|
|» ciphertext|body|string|false|Ciphertext to decrypt as previously returned from an encrypt operation. This must be base64-encoded ciphertext as previously returned from an encrypt operation.|
|» key_version|body|integer|false|Integer version of the crypto key version to use for decryption. This is required for asymmetric keys. For symmetric keys, Cloud KMS will choose the correct version automatically.|

<h3 id="decrypt-a-ciphertext-value-using-a-named-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h3 id="google-cloud-kms-configure-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|Name of the key in Vault.|
|gcpkms_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[GoogleCloudKmsConfigureKeyRequest](#schemagooglecloudkmsconfigurekeyrequest)|true|none|
|» max_version|body|integer|false|Maximum allowed crypto key version. If set to a positive value, key versions greater than the given value are not permitted to be used. If set to 0 or a negative value, there is no maximum key version.|
|» min_version|body|integer|false|Minimum allowed crypto key version. If set to a positive value, key versions less than the given value are not permitted to be used. If set to 0 or a negative value, there is no minimum key version. This value only affects encryption/re-encryption, not decryption. To restrict old values from being decrypted, increase this value and then perform a trim operation.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

## Interact with crypto keys in Vault and Google Cloud KMS

<a id="opIdgoogle-cloud-kms-write-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/gcpkms/keys/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "algorithm": "string",
    "crypto_key": "string",
    "key_ring": "string",
    "labels": {},
    "protection_level": "string",
    "purpose": "string",
    "rotation_period": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{gcpkms_mount_path}/keys/{key}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "algorithm": "string",
  "crypto_key": "string",
  "key_ring": "string",
  "labels": {},
  "protection_level": "string",
  "purpose": "string",
  "rotation_period": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="interact-with-crypto-keys-in-vault-and-google-cloud-kms-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|path|string|true|Name of the key in Vault.|
|gcpkms_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[GoogleCloudKmsWriteKeyRequest](#schemagooglecloudkmswritekeyrequest)|true|none|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|Algorithm to use for encryption, decryption, or signing. The value depends on the key purpose. The value cannot be changed after creation. For a key purpose of "encrypt_decrypt", the valid values are: - symmetric_encryption (default) For a key purpose of "asymmetric_sign", valid values are: - rsa_sign_pss_2048_sha256 - rsa_sign_pss_3072_sha256 - rsa_sign_pss_4096_sha256 - rsa_sign_pkcs1_2048_sha256 - rsa_sign_pkcs1_3072_sha256 - rsa_sign_pkcs1_4096_sha256 - ec_sign_p256_sha256 - ec_sign_p384_sha384 For a key purpose of "asymmetric_decrypt", valid values are: - rsa_decrypt_oaep_2048_sha256 - rsa_decrypt_oaep_3072_sha256 - rsa_decrypt_oaep_4096_sha256|
|» crypto_key|body|string|false|Name of the crypto key to use. If the given crypto key does not exist, Vault will try to create it. This defaults to the name of the key given to Vault as the parameter if unspecified.|
|» key_ring|body|string|false|Full Google Cloud resource ID of the key ring with the project and location (e.g. projects/my-project/locations/global/keyRings/my-keyring). If the given key ring does not exist, Vault will try to create it during a create operation.|
|» labels|body|object(kvpairs)|false|Arbitrary key=value label to apply to the crypto key. To specify multiple labels, specify this argument multiple times (e.g. labels="a=b" labels="c=d").|
|» protection_level|body|string|false|Level of protection to use for the key management. Valid values are "software" and "hsm". The default value is "software". The value cannot be changed after creation.|
|» purpose|body|string|false|Purpose of the key. Valid options are "asymmetric_decrypt", "asymmetric_sign", and "encrypt_decrypt". The default value is "encrypt_decrypt". The value cannot be changed after creation.|
|» rotation_period|body|string(duration)|false|Amount of time between crypto key version rotations. This is specified as a time duration value like 72h (72 hours). The smallest possible value is 24h. This value only applies to keys with a purpose of "encrypt_decrypt".|

<h3 id="interact-with-crypto-keys-in-vault-and-google-cloud-kms-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## kubernetes-write-role

<a id="opIdkubernetes-write-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/kubernetes/roles/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "allowed_kubernetes_namespace_selector": "string",
    "allowed_kubernetes_namespaces": [
      "string"
    ],
    "extra_annotations": {},
    "extra_labels": {},
    "generated_role_rules": "string",
    "kubernetes_role_name": "string",
    "kubernetes_role_type": "Role",
    "name_template": "string",
    "service_account_name": "string",
    "token_default_audiences": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_default_ttl": "string",
    "token_max_ttl": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{kubernetes_mount_path}/roles/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowed_kubernetes_namespace_selector": "string",
  "allowed_kubernetes_namespaces": [
    "string"
  ],
  "extra_annotations": {},
  "extra_labels": {},
  "generated_role_rules": "string",
  "kubernetes_role_name": "string",
  "kubernetes_role_type": "Role",
  "name_template": "string",
  "service_account_name": "string",
  "token_default_audiences": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_default_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="kubernetes-write-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the role|
|kubernetes_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[KubernetesWriteRoleRequest](#schemakuberneteswriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» allowed_kubernetes_namespace_selector|body|string|false|A label selector for Kubernetes namespaces in which credentials can be generated. Accepts either a JSON or YAML object. If set with allowed_kubernetes_namespaces, the conditions are conjuncted.|
|» allowed_kubernetes_namespaces|body|[string]|false|A list of the Kubernetes namespaces in which credentials can be generated. If set to "*" all namespaces are allowed.|
|» extra_annotations|body|object(kvpairs)|false|Additional annotations to apply to all generated Kubernetes objects.|
|» extra_labels|body|object(kvpairs)|false|Additional labels to apply to all generated Kubernetes objects.|
|» generated_role_rules|body|string|false|The Role or ClusterRole rules to use when generating a role. Accepts either a JSON or YAML object. If set, the entire chain of Kubernetes objects will be generated.|
|» kubernetes_role_name|body|string|false|The pre-existing Role or ClusterRole to bind a generated service account to. If set, Kubernetes token, service account, and role binding objects will be created.|
|» kubernetes_role_type|body|string|false|Specifies whether the Kubernetes role is a Role or ClusterRole.|
|» name_template|body|string|false|The name template to use when generating service accounts, roles and role bindings. If unset, a default template is used.|
|» service_account_name|body|string|false|The pre-existing service account to generate tokens for. Mutually exclusive with all role parameters. If set, only a Kubernetes service account token will be created.|
|» token_default_audiences|body|[string]|false|The default audiences for generated Kubernetes service account tokens. If not set or set to "", will use k8s cluster default.|
|» token_default_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The default ttl for generated Kubernetes service account tokens. If not set or set to 0, will use system default.|
|» token_max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum ttl for generated Kubernetes service account tokens. If not set or set to 0, will use system default.|

<h3 id="kubernetes-write-role-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
  }'
```

## ldap-configure

<a id="opIdldap-configure"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/ldap/config \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "anonymous_group_search": false,
    "binddn": "string",
    "bindpass": "string",
    "case_sensitive_names": true,
    "certificate": "string",
    "client_tls_cert": "string",
    "client_tls_key": "string",
    "connection_timeout": "30s",
    "deny_null_bind": true,
    "dereference_aliases": "never",
    "discoverdn": true,
    "groupattr": "cn",
    "groupdn": "string",
    "groupfilter": "(|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))",
    "insecure_tls": true,
    "length": 0,
    "max_page_size": 0,
    "max_ttl": "string",
    "password_policy": "string",
    "request_timeout": "90s",
    "schema": "openldap",
    "starttls": true,
    "tls_max_version": "tls12",
    "tls_min_version": "tls12",
    "ttl": "string",
    "upndomain": "string",
    "url": "ldap://127.0.0.1",
    "use_pre111_group_cn_behavior": true,
    "use_token_groups": false,
    "userattr": "cn",
    "userdn": "string",
    "userfilter": "({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})",
    "username_as_alias": false
  }'
```

`POST /{ldap_mount_path}/config`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "anonymous_group_search": false,
  "binddn": "string",
  "bindpass": "string",
  "case_sensitive_names": true,
  "certificate": "string",
  "client_tls_cert": "string",
  "client_tls_key": "string",
  "connection_timeout": "30s",
  "deny_null_bind": true,
  "dereference_aliases": "never",
  "discoverdn": true,
  "groupattr": "cn",
  "groupdn": "string",
  "groupfilter": "(|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))",
  "insecure_tls": true,
  "length": 0,
  "max_page_size": 0,
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "password_policy": "string",
  "request_timeout": "90s",
  "schema": "openldap",
  "starttls": true,
  "tls_max_version": "tls12",
  "tls_min_version": "tls12",
  "ttl": "string",
  "upndomain": "string",
  "url": "ldap://127.0.0.1",
  "use_pre111_group_cn_behavior": true,
  "use_token_groups": false,
  "userattr": "cn",
  "userdn": "string",
  "userfilter": "({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})",
  "username_as_alias": false
}
```

<h3 id="ldap-configure-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ldap_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[LdapConfigureRequest](#schemaldapconfigurerequest)|true|none|
|» anonymous_group_search|body|boolean|false|Use anonymous binds when performing LDAP group searches (if true the initial credentials will still be used for the initial connection test).|
|» binddn|body|string|false|LDAP DN for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|» bindpass|body|string|false|LDAP password for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|» case_sensitive_names|body|boolean|false|If true, case sensitivity will be used when comparing usernames and groups for matching policies.|
|» certificate|body|string|false|CA certificate to use when verifying LDAP server certificate, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» client_tls_cert|body|string|false|Client certificate to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» client_tls_key|body|string|false|Client certificate key to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|» connection_timeout|body|string(duration)|false|Timeout, in seconds, when attempting to connect to the LDAP server before trying the next URL in the configuration.|
|» deny_null_bind|body|boolean|false|Denies an unauthenticated LDAP bind request if the user's password is empty; defaults to true|
|» dereference_aliases|body|string|false|When aliases should be dereferenced on search operations. Accepted values are 'never', 'finding', 'searching', 'always'. Defaults to 'never'.|
|» discoverdn|body|boolean|false|Use anonymous bind to discover the bind DN of a user (optional)|
|» groupattr|body|string|false|LDAP attribute to follow on objects returned by <groupfilter> in order to enumerate user group membership. Examples: "cn" or "memberOf", etc. Default: cn|
|» groupdn|body|string|false|LDAP search base to use for group membership search (eg: ou=Groups,dc=example,dc=org)|
|» groupfilter|body|string|false|Go template for querying group membership of user (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserDN, Username Example: (&(objectClass=group)(member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:={{.UserDN}})) Default: (\|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))|
|» insecure_tls|body|boolean|false|Skip LDAP server SSL Certificate verification - VERY insecure (optional)|
|» length|body|integer|false|**Deprecated.** The desired length of passwords that Vault generates.|
|» max_page_size|body|integer|false|If set to a value greater than 0, the LDAP backend will use the LDAP server's paged search control to request pages of up to the given size. This can be used to avoid hitting the LDAP server's maximum result size limit. Otherwise, the LDAP backend will not use the paged search control.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum password time-to-live.|
|» password_policy|body|string|false|Password policy to use to generate passwords|
|» request_timeout|body|string(duration)|false|Timeout, in seconds, for the connection when making requests against the server before returning back an error.|
|» schema|body|string|false|The desired LDAP schema used when modifying user account passwords.|
|» starttls|body|boolean|false|Issue a StartTLS command after establishing unencrypted connection (optional)|
|» tls_max_version|body|string|false|Maximum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|» tls_min_version|body|string|false|Minimum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The default password time-to-live.|
|» upndomain|body|string|false|Enables userPrincipalDomain login with [username]@UPNDomain (optional)|
|» url|body|string|false|LDAP URL to connect to (default: ldap://127.0.0.1). Multiple URLs can be specified by concatenating them with commas; they will be tried in-order.|
|» use_pre111_group_cn_behavior|body|boolean|false|In Vault 1.1.1 a fix for handling group CN values of different cases unfortunately introduced a regression that could cause previously defined groups to not be found due to a change in the resulting name. If set true, the pre-1.1.1 behavior for matching group CNs will be used. This is only needed in some upgrade scenarios for backwards compatibility. It is enabled by default if the config is upgraded but disabled by default on new configurations.|
|» use_token_groups|body|boolean|false|If true, use the Active Directory tokenGroups constructed attribute of the user to find the group memberships. This will find all security groups including nested ones.|
|» userattr|body|string|false|Attribute used for users (default: cn)|
|» userdn|body|string|false|LDAP domain to use for users (eg: ou=People,dc=example,dc=org)|
|» userfilter|body|string|false|Go template for LDAP user search filer (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserAttr, Username Default: ({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})|
|» username_as_alias|body|boolean|false|If true, sets the alias name to the username|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» dereference_aliases|never|
|» dereference_aliases|finding|
|» dereference_aliases|searching|
|» dereference_aliases|always|
|» tls_max_version|tls10|
|» tls_max_version|tls11|
|» tls_max_version|tls12|
|» tls_max_version|tls13|
|» tls_min_version|tls10|
|» tls_min_version|tls11|
|» tls_min_version|tls12|
|» tls_min_version|tls13|

<h3 id="ldap-configure-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Manage the roles used to generate MongoDB Atlas Programmatic API Keys.

<a id="opIdmongo-db-atlas-write-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/mongodbatlas/roles/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "cidr_blocks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "ip_addresses": [
      "string"
    ],
    "max_ttl": "string",
    "organization_id": "string",
    "project_id": "string",
    "project_roles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "roles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "ttl": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{mongodbatlas_mount_path}/roles/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cidr_blocks": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ip_addresses": [
    "string"
  ],
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "organization_id": "string",
  "project_id": "string",
  "project_roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="manage-the-roles-used-to-generate-mongodb-atlas-programmatic-api-keys-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the Roles|
|mongodbatlas_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[MongoDbAtlasWriteRoleRequest](#schemamongodbatlaswriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» cidr_blocks|body|[string]|false|Access list entry in CIDR notation to be added for the API key. Optional for organization and project keys.|
|» ip_addresses|body|[string]|false|IP address to be added to the access list for the API key. Optional for organization and project keys.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum allowed lifetime of credentials issued using this role.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|Organization ID required for an organization API key|
|» project_id|body|string|false|Project ID the project API key belongs to.|
|» project_roles|body|[string]|false|Roles assigned when an organization API Key is assigned to a project API key|
|» roles|body|[string]|true|List of roles that the API Key should be granted. A minimum of one role must be provided. Any roles provided must be valid for the assigned Project, required for organization and project keys.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|Duration in seconds after which the issued credential should expire. Defaults to 0, in which case the value will fallback to the system/mount defaults.|

<h3 id="manage-the-roles-used-to-generate-mongodb-atlas-programmatic-api-keys-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## pki-configure-acme

<a id="opIdpki-configure-acme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/pki/config/acme \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "allow_role_ext_key_usage": false,
    "allowed_issuers": [
      "*"
    ],
    "allowed_roles": [
      "*"
    ],
    "default_directory_policy": "sign-verbatim",
    "dns_resolver": "",
    "eab_policy": "always-required",
    "enabled": false
  }'
```

`POST /{pki_mount_path}/config/acme`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_role_ext_key_usage": false,
  "allowed_issuers": [
    "*"
  ],
  "allowed_roles": [
    "*"
  ],
  "default_directory_policy": "sign-verbatim",
  "dns_resolver": "",
  "eab_policy": "always-required",
  "enabled": false
}
```

<h3 id="pki-configure-acme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiConfigureAcmeRequest](#schemapkiconfigureacmerequest)|true|none|
|» allow_role_ext_key_usage|body|boolean|false|whether the ExtKeyUsage field from a role is used, defaults to false meaning that certificate will be signed with ServerAuth.|
|» allowed_issuers|body|[string]|false|which issuers are allowed for use with ACME; by default, this will only be the primary (default) issuer|
|» allowed_roles|body|[string]|false|which roles are allowed for use with ACME; by default via '*', these will be all roles including sign-verbatim; when concrete role names are specified, any default_directory_policy role must be included to allow usage of the default acme directories under /pki/acme/directory and /pki/issuer/:issuer_id/acme/directory.|
|» default_directory_policy|body|string|false|the policy to be used for non-role-qualified ACME requests; by default ACME issuance will be otherwise unrestricted, equivalent to the sign-verbatim endpoint; one may also specify a role to use as this policy, as "role:<role_name>", the specified role must be allowed by allowed_roles|
|» dns_resolver|body|string|false|DNS resolver to use for domain resolution on this mount. Defaults to using the default system resolver. Must be in the format <host>:<port>, with both parts mandatory.|
|» eab_policy|body|string|false|Specify the policy to use for external account binding behaviour, 'not-required', 'new-account-required' or 'always-required'|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|whether ACME is enabled, defaults to false meaning that clusters will by default not get ACME support|

<h3 id="pki-configure-acme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## pki-configure-auto-tidy

<a id="opIdpki-configure-auto-tidy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/pki/config/auto-tidy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "acme_account_safety_buffer": 2592000,
    "enabled": true,
    "interval_duration": 43200,
    "issuer_safety_buffer": 31536000,
    "maintain_stored_certificate_counts": false,
    "pause_duration": "0s",
    "publish_stored_certificate_count_metrics": false,
    "revocation_queue_safety_buffer": 172800,
    "safety_buffer": 259200,
    "tidy_acme": false,
    "tidy_cert_store": true,
    "tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs": true,
    "tidy_expired_issuers": true,
    "tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle": true,
    "tidy_revocation_list": true,
    "tidy_revocation_queue": false,
    "tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations": true,
    "tidy_revoked_certs": true
  }'
```

`POST /{pki_mount_path}/config/auto-tidy`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acme_account_safety_buffer": 2592000,
  "enabled": true,
  "interval_duration": 43200,
  "issuer_safety_buffer": 31536000,
  "maintain_stored_certificate_counts": false,
  "pause_duration": "0s",
  "publish_stored_certificate_count_metrics": false,
  "revocation_queue_safety_buffer": 172800,
  "safety_buffer": 259200,
  "tidy_acme": false,
  "tidy_cert_store": true,
  "tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs": true,
  "tidy_expired_issuers": true,
  "tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle": true,
  "tidy_revocation_list": true,
  "tidy_revocation_queue": false,
  "tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations": true,
  "tidy_revoked_certs": true
}
```

<h3 id="pki-configure-auto-tidy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiConfigureAutoTidyRequest](#schemapkiconfigureautotidyrequest)|true|none|
|» acme_account_safety_buffer|body|string(duration)|false|The amount of time that must pass after creation that an account with no orders is marked revoked, and the amount of time after being marked revoked or deactivated.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Set to true to enable automatic tidy operations.|
|» interval_duration|body|string(duration)|false|Interval at which to run an auto-tidy operation. This is the time between tidy invocations (after one finishes to the start of the next). Running a manual tidy will reset this duration.|
|» issuer_safety_buffer|body|string(duration)|false|The amount of extra time that must have passed beyond issuer's expiration before it is removed from the backend storage. Defaults to 8760 hours (1 year).|
|» maintain_stored_certificate_counts|body|boolean|false|This configures whether stored certificates are counted upon initialization of the backend, and whether during normal operation, a running count of certificates stored is maintained.|
|» pause_duration|body|string|false|The amount of time to wait between processing certificates. This allows operators to change the execution profile of tidy to take consume less resources by slowing down how long it takes to run. Note that the entire list of certificates will be stored in memory during the entire tidy operation, but resources to read/process/update existing entries will be spread out over a greater period of time. By default this is zero seconds.|
|» publish_stored_certificate_count_metrics|body|boolean|false|This configures whether the stored certificate count is published to the metrics consumer. It does not affect if the stored certificate count is maintained, and if maintained, it will be available on the tidy-status endpoint.|
|» revocation_queue_safety_buffer|body|string(duration)|false|The amount of time that must pass from the cross-cluster revocation request being initiated to when it will be slated for removal. Setting this too low may remove valid revocation requests before the owning cluster has a chance to process them, especially if the cluster is offline.|
|» safety_buffer|body|string(duration)|false|The amount of extra time that must have passed beyond certificate expiration before it is removed from the backend storage and/or revocation list. Defaults to 72 hours.|
|» tidy_acme|body|boolean|false|Set to true to enable tidying ACME accounts, orders and authorizations. ACME orders are tidied (deleted) safety_buffer after the certificate associated with them expires, or after the order and relevant authorizations have expired if no certificate was produced. Authorizations are tidied with the corresponding order. When a valid ACME Account is at least acme_account_safety_buffer old, and has no remaining orders associated with it, the account is marked as revoked. After another acme_account_safety_buffer has passed from the revocation or deactivation date, a revoked or deactivated ACME account is deleted.|
|» tidy_cert_store|body|boolean|false|Set to true to enable tidying up the certificate store|
|» tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs|body|boolean|false|Set to true to enable tidying up the cross-cluster revoked certificate store. Only runs on the active primary node.|
|» tidy_expired_issuers|body|boolean|false|Set to true to automatically remove expired issuers past the issuer_safety_buffer. No keys will be removed as part of this operation.|
|» tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle|body|boolean|false|Set to true to move the legacy ca_bundle from /config/ca_bundle to /config/ca_bundle.bak. This prevents downgrades to pre-Vault 1.11 versions (as older PKI engines do not know about the new multi-issuer storage layout), but improves the performance on seal wrapped PKI mounts. This will only occur if at least issuer_safety_buffer time has occurred after the initial storage migration. This backup is saved in case of an issue in future migrations. Operators may consider removing it via sys/raw if they desire. The backup will be removed via a DELETE /root call, but note that this removes ALL issuers within the mount (and is thus not desirable in most operational scenarios).|
|» tidy_revocation_list|body|boolean|false|Deprecated; synonym for 'tidy_revoked_certs|
|» tidy_revocation_queue|body|boolean|false|Set to true to remove stale revocation queue entries that haven't been confirmed by any active cluster. Only runs on the active primary node|
|» tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations|body|boolean|false|Set to true to validate issuer associations on revocation entries. This helps increase the performance of CRL building and OCSP responses.|
|» tidy_revoked_certs|body|boolean|false|Set to true to expire all revoked and expired certificates, removing them both from the CRL and from storage. The CRL will be rotated if this causes any values to be removed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acme_account_safety_buffer": 0,
  "enabled": true,
  "interval_duration": 0,
  "issuer_safety_buffer": 0,
  "maintain_stored_certificate_counts": true,
  "pause_duration": "string",
  "publish_stored_certificate_count_metrics": true,
  "revocation_queue_safety_buffer": 0,
  "safety_buffer": 0,
  "tidy_acme": true,
  "tidy_cert_store": true,
  "tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs": true,
  "tidy_expired_issuers": true,
  "tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle": true,
  "tidy_revocation_queue": true,
  "tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations": true,
  "tidy_revoked_certs": true
}
```

<h3 id="pki-configure-auto-tidy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[PkiConfigureAutoTidyResponse](#schemapkiconfigureautotidyresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## pki-configure-crl

<a id="opIdpki-configure-crl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/pki/config/crl \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "auto_rebuild": true,
    "auto_rebuild_grace_period": "12h",
    "cross_cluster_revocation": true,
    "delta_rebuild_interval": "15m",
    "disable": true,
    "enable_delta": true,
    "expiry": "72h",
    "ocsp_disable": true,
    "ocsp_expiry": "1h",
    "unified_crl": "false",
    "unified_crl_on_existing_paths": "false"
  }'
```

`POST /{pki_mount_path}/config/crl`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auto_rebuild": true,
  "auto_rebuild_grace_period": "12h",
  "cross_cluster_revocation": true,
  "delta_rebuild_interval": "15m",
  "disable": true,
  "enable_delta": true,
  "expiry": "72h",
  "ocsp_disable": true,
  "ocsp_expiry": "1h",
  "unified_crl": "false",
  "unified_crl_on_existing_paths": "false"
}
```

<h3 id="pki-configure-crl-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiConfigureCrlRequest](#schemapkiconfigurecrlrequest)|true|none|
|» auto_rebuild|body|boolean|false|If set to true, enables automatic rebuilding of the CRL|
|» auto_rebuild_grace_period|body|string|false|The time before the CRL expires to automatically rebuild it, when enabled. Must be shorter than the CRL expiry. Defaults to 12h.|
|» cross_cluster_revocation|body|boolean|false|Whether to enable a global, cross-cluster revocation queue. Must be used with auto_rebuild=true.|
|» delta_rebuild_interval|body|string|false|The time between delta CRL rebuilds if a new revocation has occurred. Must be shorter than the CRL expiry. Defaults to 15m.|
|» disable|body|boolean|false|If set to true, disables generating the CRL entirely.|
|» enable_delta|body|boolean|false|Whether to enable delta CRLs between authoritative CRL rebuilds|
|» expiry|body|string|false|The amount of time the generated CRL should be valid; defaults to 72 hours|
|» ocsp_disable|body|boolean|false|If set to true, ocsp unauthorized responses will be returned.|
|» ocsp_expiry|body|string|false|The amount of time an OCSP response will be valid (controls the NextUpdate field); defaults to 12 hours|
|» unified_crl|body|boolean|false|If set to true enables global replication of revocation entries, also enabling unified versions of OCSP and CRLs if their respective features are enabled. disable for CRLs and ocsp_disable for OCSP.|
|» unified_crl_on_existing_paths|body|boolean|false|If set to true, existing CRL and OCSP paths will return the unified CRL instead of a response based on cluster-local data|

> Example responses

`POST /{pki_mount_path}/intermediate/cross-sign`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "add_basic_constraints": true,
  "alt_names": "string",
  "common_name": "string",
  "country": [
    "string"
  ],
  "exclude_cn_from_sans": false,
  "exported": "internal",
  "format": "pem",
  "ip_sans": [
    "string"
  ],
  "key_bits": 0,
  "key_name": "string",
  "key_ref": "default",
  "key_type": "rsa",
  "locality": [
    "string"
  ],
  "managed_key_id": "string",
  "managed_key_name": "string",
  "not_after": "string",
  "not_before_duration": 30,
  "organization": [
    "string"
  ],
  "other_sans": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ou": [
    "string"
  ],
  "postal_code": [
    "string"
  ],
  "private_key_format": "der",
  "province": [
    "string"
  ],
  "serial_number": "string",
  "signature_bits": 0,
  "street_address": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ttl": "string",
  "uri_sans": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="pki-cross-sign-intermediate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiCrossSignIntermediateRequest](#schemapkicrosssignintermediaterequest)|true|none|
|» add_basic_constraints|body|boolean|false|Whether to add a Basic Constraints extension with CA: true. Only needed as a workaround in some compatibility scenarios with Active Directory Certificate Services.|
|» alt_names|body|string|false|The requested Subject Alternative Names, if any, in a comma-delimited list. May contain both DNS names and email addresses.|
|» common_name|body|string|false|The requested common name; if you want more than one, specify the alternative names in the alt_names map. If not specified when signing, the common name will be taken from the CSR; other names must still be specified in alt_names or ip_sans.|
|» country|body|[string]|false|If set, Country will be set to this value.|
|» exclude_cn_from_sans|body|boolean|false|If true, the Common Name will not be included in DNS or Email Subject Alternate Names. Defaults to false (CN is included).|
|» exported|body|string|false|Must be "internal", "exported" or "kms". If set to "exported", the generated private key will be returned. This is your *only* chance to retrieve the private key!|
|» format|body|string|false|Format for returned data. Can be "pem", "der", or "pem_bundle". If "pem_bundle", any private key and issuing cert will be appended to the certificate pem. If "der", the value will be base64 encoded. Defaults to "pem".|
|» ip_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested IP SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list|
|» key_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|» key_name|body|string|false|Provide a name to the generated or existing key, the name must be unique across all keys and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|» key_ref|body|string|false|Reference to a existing key; either "default" for the configured default key, an identifier or the name assigned to the key.|
|» key_type|body|string|false|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec" and "ed25519" are the only valid values.|
|» locality|body|[string]|false|If set, Locality will be set to this value.|
|» managed_key_id|body|string|false|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_name is required. Ignored for other types.|
|» managed_key_name|body|string|false|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_id is required. Ignored for other types.|
|» not_after|body|string|false|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|» not_before_duration|body|string(duration)|false|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|» organization|body|[string]|false|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value.|
|» other_sans|body|[string]|false|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|
|» ou|body|[string]|false|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value.|
|» postal_code|body|[string]|false|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value.|
|» private_key_format|body|string|false|Format for the returned private key. Generally the default will be controlled by the "format" parameter as either base64-encoded DER or PEM-encoded DER. However, this can be set to "pkcs8" to have the returned private key contain base64-encoded pkcs8 or PEM-encoded pkcs8 instead. Defaults to "der".|
|» province|body|[string]|false|If set, Province will be set to this value.|
|» serial_number|body|string|false|The Subject's requested serial number, if any. See RFC 4519 Section 2.31 'serialNumber' for a description of this field. If you want more than one, specify alternative names in the alt_names map using OID 2.5.4.5. This has no impact on the final certificate's Serial Number field.|
|» signature_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|» street_address|body|[string]|false|If set, Street Address will be set to this value.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the mount max TTL. Note: this only has an effect when generating a CA cert or signing a CA cert, not when generating a CSR for an intermediate CA.|
|» uri_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested URI SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» exported|internal|
|» exported|external|
|» exported|kms|
|» format|pem|

<h3 id="pki-generate-intermediate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exported|path|string|true|Must be "internal", "exported" or "kms". If set to "exported", the generated private key will be returned. This is your *only* chance to retrieve the private key!|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiGenerateIntermediateRequest](#schemapkigenerateintermediaterequest)|true|none|
|» add_basic_constraints|body|boolean|false|Whether to add a Basic Constraints extension with CA: true. Only needed as a workaround in some compatibility scenarios with Active Directory Certificate Services.|
|» alt_names|body|string|false|The requested Subject Alternative Names, if any, in a comma-delimited list. May contain both DNS names and email addresses.|
|» common_name|body|string|false|The requested common name; if you want more than one, specify the alternative names in the alt_names map. If not specified when signing, the common name will be taken from the CSR; other names must still be specified in alt_names or ip_sans.|
|» country|body|[string]|false|If set, Country will be set to this value.|
|» exclude_cn_from_sans|body|boolean|false|If true, the Common Name will not be included in DNS or Email Subject Alternate Names. Defaults to false (CN is included).|
|» format|body|string|false|Format for returned data. Can be "pem", "der", or "pem_bundle". If "pem_bundle", any private key and issuing cert will be appended to the certificate pem. If "der", the value will be base64 encoded. Defaults to "pem".|
|» ip_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested IP SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list|
|» key_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|» key_name|body|string|false|Provide a name to the generated or existing key, the name must be unique across all keys and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|» key_ref|body|string|false|Reference to a existing key; either "default" for the configured default key, an identifier or the name assigned to the key.|
|» key_type|body|string|false|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec" and "ed25519" are the only valid values.|
|» locality|body|[string]|false|If set, Locality will be set to this value.|
|» managed_key_id|body|string|false|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_name is required. Ignored for other types.|
|» managed_key_name|body|string|false|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_id is required. Ignored for other types.|
|» not_after|body|string|false|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|» not_before_duration|body|string(duration)|false|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|» organization|body|[string]|false|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value.|
|» other_sans|body|[string]|false|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|
|» ou|body|[string]|false|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value.|
|» postal_code|body|[string]|false|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value.|
|» private_key_format|body|string|false|Format for the returned private key. Generally the default will be controlled by the "format" parameter as either base64-encoded DER or PEM-encoded DER. However, this can be set to "pkcs8" to have the returned private key contain base64-encoded pkcs8 or PEM-encoded pkcs8 instead. Defaults to "der".|
|» province|body|[string]|false|If set, Province will be set to this value.|
|» serial_number|body|string|false|The Subject's requested serial number, if any. See RFC 4519 Section 2.31 'serialNumber' for a description of this field. If you want more than one, specify alternative names in the alt_names map using OID 2.5.4.5. This has no impact on the final certificate's Serial Number field.|
|» signature_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|» street_address|body|[string]|false|If set, Street Address will be set to this value.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the mount max TTL. Note: this only has an effect when generating a CA cert or signing a CA cert, not when generating a CSR for an intermediate CA.|
|» uri_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested URI SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list.|

|exported|external|

|» format|der|

|» key_type|ed25519|

|» crl_distribution_points|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of URLs to be used for the CRL distribution points attribute. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.13.|
|» enable_aia_url_templating|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to enabling templating of the above AIA fields. When templating is enabled the special values '{{issuer_id}}', '{{cluster_path}}', '{{cluster_aia_path}}' are available, but the addresses are not checked for URL validity until issuance time. Using '{{cluster_path}}' requires /config/cluster's 'path' member to be set on all PR Secondary clusters and using '{{cluster_aia_path}}' requires /config/cluster's 'aia_path' member to be set on all PR secondary clusters.|
|» issuer_name|body|string|false|Provide a name to the generated or existing issuer, the name must be unique across all issuers and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|» issuing_certificates|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of URLs to be used for the issuing certificate attribute. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.2.1.|
|» leaf_not_after_behavior|body|string|false|Behavior of leaf's NotAfter fields: "err" to error if the computed NotAfter date exceeds that of this issuer; "truncate" to silently truncate to that of this issuer; or "permit" to allow this issuance to succeed (with NotAfter exceeding that of an issuer). Note that not all values will results in certificates that can be validated through the entire validity period. It is suggested to use "truncate" for intermediate CAs and "permit" only for root CAs.|
|» manual_chain|body|[string]|false|Chain of issuer references to use to build this issuer's computed CAChain field, when non-empty.|
|» ocsp_servers|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list of URLs to be used for the OCSP servers attribute. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.2.1.|
|» revocation_signature_algorithm|body|string|false|Which x509.SignatureAlgorithm name to use for signing CRLs. This parameter allows differentiation between PKCS#1v1.5 and PSS keys and choice of signature hash algorithm. The default (empty string) value is for Go to select the signature algorithm. This can fail if the underlying key does not support the requested signature algorithm, which may not be known at modification time (such as with PKCS#11 managed RSA keys).|
|» usage|body|[string]|false|Comma-separated list (or string slice) of usages for this issuer; valid values are "read-only", "issuing-certificates", "crl-signing", and "ocsp-signing". Multiple values may be specified. Read-only is implicit and always set.|

```bash
    "ip_sans": [
      "string"
    ],
    "not_after": "string",
    "other_sans": [
      "string"
    ],
    "private_key_format": "der",
    "remove_roots_from_chain": false,
    "serial_number": "string",
    "ttl": "string",
    "uri_sans": [
      "string"
    ],
    "user_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /{pki_mount_path}/issuer/{issuer_ref}/issue/{role}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alt_names": "string",
  "common_name": "string",
  "exclude_cn_from_sans": false,
  "format": "pem",
  "ip_sans": [
    "string"
  ],
  "not_after": "string",
  "other_sans": [
    "string"
  ],
  "private_key_format": "der",
  "remove_roots_from_chain": false,
  "serial_number": "string",
  "ttl": "string",
  "uri_sans": [
    "string"
  ],
  "user_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="pki-issuer-issue-with-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issuer_ref|path|string|true|Reference to a existing issuer; either "default" for the configured default issuer, an identifier or the name assigned to the issuer.|
|role|path|string|true|The desired role with configuration for this request|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiIssuerIssueWithRoleRequest](#schemapkiissuerissuewithrolerequest)|true|none|
|» alt_names|body|string|false|The requested Subject Alternative Names, if any, in a comma-delimited list. If email protection is enabled for the role, this may contain email addresses.|
|» common_name|body|string|false|The requested common name; if you want more than one, specify the alternative names in the alt_names map. If email protection is enabled in the role, this may be an email address.|
|» exclude_cn_from_sans|body|boolean|false|If true, the Common Name will not be included in DNS or Email Subject Alternate Names. Defaults to false (CN is included).|
|» format|body|string|false|Format for returned data. Can be "pem", "der", or "pem_bundle". If "pem_bundle", any private key and issuing cert will be appended to the certificate pem. If "der", the value will be base64 encoded. Defaults to "pem".|
|» ip_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested IP SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list|
|» not_after|body|string|false|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|» other_sans|body|[string]|false|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|
|» private_key_format|body|string|false|Format for the returned private key. Generally the default will be controlled by the "format" parameter as either base64-encoded DER or PEM-encoded DER. However, this can be set to "pkcs8" to have the returned private key contain base64-encoded pkcs8 or PEM-encoded pkcs8 instead. Defaults to "der".|
|» remove_roots_from_chain|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to remove self-signed CA certificates in the output of the ca_chain field.|
|» serial_number|body|string|false|The Subject's requested serial number, if any. See RFC 4519 Section 2.31 'serialNumber' for a description of this field. If you want more than one, specify alternative names in the alt_names map using OID 2.5.4.5. This has no impact on the final certificate's Serial Number field.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the role max TTL.|
|» uri_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested URI SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list.|
|» user_ids|body|[string]|false|The requested user_ids value to place in the subject, if any, in a comma-delimited list. Restricted by allowed_user_ids. Any values are added with OID 0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.1.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» format|pem|
|» format|der|
|» format|pem_bundle|
|» private_key_format|""|
|» private_key_format|der|
|» private_key_format|pem|
|» private_key_format|pkcs8|

```json
  "ca_chain": [
    "string"
  ],
  "certificate": "string",
  "expiration": 0,
  "issuing_ca": "string",
  "private_key": "string",
  "private_key_type": "string",
  "serial_number": "string"
```
```json
}
```

<h3 id="pki-issuer-sign-intermediate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issuer_ref|path|string|true|Reference to a existing issuer; either "default" for the configured default issuer, an identifier or the name assigned to the issuer.|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiIssuerSignIntermediateRequest](#schemapkiissuersignintermediaterequest)|true|none|
|» alt_names|body|string|false|The requested Subject Alternative Names, if any, in a comma-delimited list. May contain both DNS names and email addresses.|
|» common_name|body|string|false|The requested common name; if you want more than one, specify the alternative names in the alt_names map. If not specified when signing, the common name will be taken from the CSR; other names must still be specified in alt_names or ip_sans.|
|» country|body|[string]|false|If set, Country will be set to this value.|
|» csr|body|string|false|PEM-format CSR to be signed.|
|» exclude_cn_from_sans|body|boolean|false|If true, the Common Name will not be included in DNS or Email Subject Alternate Names. Defaults to false (CN is included).|
|» format|body|string|false|Format for returned data. Can be "pem", "der", or "pem_bundle". If "pem_bundle", any private key and issuing cert will be appended to the certificate pem. If "der", the value will be base64 encoded. Defaults to "pem".|
|» ip_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested IP SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list|
|» issuer_name|body|string|false|Provide a name to the generated or existing issuer, the name must be unique across all issuers and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|» locality|body|[string]|false|If set, Locality will be set to this value.|
|» max_path_length|body|integer|false|The maximum allowable path length|
|» not_after|body|string|false|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|» not_before_duration|body|string(duration)|false|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|» organization|body|[string]|false|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value.|
|» other_sans|body|[string]|false|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|
|» ou|body|[string]|false|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value.|
|» permitted_dns_domains|body|[string]|false|Domains for which this certificate is allowed to sign or issue child certificates. If set, all DNS names (subject and alt) on child certs must be exact matches or subsets of the given domains (see https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.10).|
|» postal_code|body|[string]|false|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value.|
|» private_key_format|body|string|false|Format for the returned private key. Generally the default will be controlled by the "format" parameter as either base64-encoded DER or PEM-encoded DER. However, this can be set to "pkcs8" to have the returned private key contain base64-encoded pkcs8 or PEM-encoded pkcs8 instead. Defaults to "der".|
|» province|body|[string]|false|If set, Province will be set to this value.|
|» serial_number|body|string|false|The Subject's requested serial number, if any. See RFC 4519 Section 2.31 'serialNumber' for a description of this field. If you want more than one, specify alternative names in the alt_names map using OID 2.5.4.5. This has no impact on the final certificate's Serial Number field.|
|» signature_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|» skid|body|string|false|Value for the Subject Key Identifier field (RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.2). This value should ONLY be used when cross-signing to mimic the existing certificate's SKID value; this is necessary to allow certain TLS implementations (such as OpenSSL) which use SKID/AKID matches in chain building to restrict possible valid chains. Specified as a string in hex format. Default is empty, allowing Vault to automatically calculate the SKID according to method one in the above RFC section.|
|» street_address|body|[string]|false|If set, Street Address will be set to this value.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the mount max TTL. Note: this only has an effect when generating a CA cert or signing a CA cert, not when generating a CSR for an intermediate CA.|
|» uri_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested URI SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list.|
|» use_csr_values|body|boolean|false|If true, then: 1) Subject information, including names and alternate names, will be preserved from the CSR rather than using values provided in the other parameters to this path; 2) Any key usages requested in the CSR will be added to the basic set of key usages used for CA certs signed by this path; for instance, the non-repudiation flag; 3) Extensions requested in the CSR will be copied into the issued certificate.|
|» use_pss|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to use PSS signatures when using a RSA key-type issuer. Defaults to false.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» format|pem|
|» format|der|
|» format|pem_bundle|
|» private_key_format|""|
|» private_key_format|der|
|» private_key_format|pem|
|» private_key_format|pkcs8|

> Example responses

```json
    "string"
  ],
  "certificate": "string",
  "expiration": 0,
  "issuing_ca": "string",
  "serial_number": "string"
```
```json
}
```

<h3 id="pki-write-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the role|
