|body|body|[PkiWriteRoleRequest](#schemapkiwriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» allow_any_name|body|boolean|false|If set, clients can request certificates for any domain, regardless of allowed_domains restrictions. See the documentation for more information.|
|» allow_bare_domains|body|boolean|false|If set, clients can request certificates for the base domains themselves, e.g. "example.com" of domains listed in allowed_domains. This is a separate option as in some cases this can be considered a security threat. See the documentation for more information.|
|» allow_glob_domains|body|boolean|false|If set, domains specified in allowed_domains can include shell-style glob patterns, e.g. "ftp*.example.com". See the documentation for more information.|
|» allow_ip_sans|body|boolean|false|If set, IP Subject Alternative Names are allowed. Any valid IP is accepted and No authorization checking is performed.|
|» allow_localhost|body|boolean|false|Whether to allow "localhost" and "localdomain" as a valid common name in a request, independent of allowed_domains value.|
|» allow_subdomains|body|boolean|false|If set, clients can request certificates for subdomains of domains listed in allowed_domains, including wildcard subdomains. See the documentation for more information.|
|» allow_wildcard_certificates|body|boolean|false|If set, allows certificates with wildcards in the common name to be issued, conforming to RFC 6125's Section 6.4.3; e.g., "*.example.net" or "b*z.example.net". See the documentation for more information.|
|» allowed_domains|body|[string]|false|Specifies the domains this role is allowed to issue certificates for. This is used with the allow_bare_domains, allow_subdomains, and allow_glob_domains to determine matches for the common name, DNS-typed SAN entries, and Email-typed SAN entries of certificates. See the documentation for more information. This parameter accepts a comma-separated string or list of domains.|
|» allowed_domains_template|body|boolean|false|If set, Allowed domains can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated domains are also permitted.|
|» allowed_other_sans|body|[string]|false|If set, an array of allowed other names to put in SANs. These values support globbing and must be in the format <oid>;<type>:<value>. Currently only "utf8" is a valid type. All values, including globbing values, must use this syntax, with the exception being a single "*" which allows any OID and any value (but type must still be utf8).|
|» allowed_serial_numbers|body|[string]|false|If set, an array of allowed serial numbers to put in Subject. These values support globbing.|
|» allowed_uri_sans|body|[string]|false|If set, an array of allowed URIs for URI Subject Alternative Names. Any valid URI is accepted, these values support globbing.|
|» allowed_uri_sans_template|body|boolean|false|If set, Allowed URI SANs can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated URI SANs are also permitted.|
|» allowed_user_ids|body|[string]|false|If set, an array of allowed user-ids to put in user system login name specified here: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1274#section-9.3.1|
|» backend|body|string|false|Backend Type|
|» basic_constraints_valid_for_non_ca|body|boolean|false|Mark Basic Constraints valid when issuing non-CA certificates.|
|» client_flag|body|boolean|false|If set, certificates are flagged for client auth use. Defaults to true. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|» cn_validations|body|[string]|false|List of allowed validations to run against the Common Name field. Values can include 'email' to validate the CN is a email address, 'hostname' to validate the CN is a valid hostname (potentially including wildcards). When multiple validations are specified, these take OR semantics (either email OR hostname are allowed). The special value 'disabled' allows disabling all CN name validations, allowing for arbitrary non-Hostname, non-Email address CNs.|
|» code_signing_flag|body|boolean|false|If set, certificates are flagged for code signing use. Defaults to false. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|» country|body|[string]|false|If set, Country will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|» email_protection_flag|body|boolean|false|If set, certificates are flagged for email protection use. Defaults to false. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|» enforce_hostnames|body|boolean|false|If set, only valid host names are allowed for CN and DNS SANs, and the host part of email addresses. Defaults to true.|
|» ext_key_usage|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated string or list of extended key usages. Valid values can be found at https://golang.org/pkg/crypto/x509/#ExtKeyUsage -- simply drop the "ExtKeyUsage" part of the name. To remove all key usages from being set, set this value to an empty list. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|» ext_key_usage_oids|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated string or list of extended key usage oids.|
|» generate_lease|body|boolean|false|If set, certificates issued/signed against this role will have Vault leases attached to them. Defaults to "false". Certificates can be added to the CRL by "vault revoke <lease_id>" when certificates are associated with leases. It can also be done using the "pki/revoke" endpoint. However, when lease generation is disabled, invoking "pki/revoke" would be the only way to add the certificates to the CRL. When large number of certificates are generated with long lifetimes, it is recommended that lease generation be disabled, as large amount of leases adversely affect the startup time of Vault.|
|» issuer_ref|body|string|false|Reference to the issuer used to sign requests serviced by this role.|
|» key_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|» key_type|body|string|false|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec", "ed25519" and "any" are the only valid values.|
|» key_usage|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated string or list of key usages (not extended key usages). Valid values can be found at https://golang.org/pkg/crypto/x509/#KeyUsage -- simply drop the "KeyUsage" part of the name. To remove all key usages from being set, set this value to an empty list. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.3.|
|» locality|body|[string]|false|If set, Locality will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The maximum allowed lease duration. If not set, defaults to the system maximum lease TTL.|
|» no_store|body|boolean|false|If set, certificates issued/signed against this role will not be stored in the storage backend. This can improve performance when issuing large numbers of certificates. However, certificates issued in this way cannot be enumerated or revoked, so this option is recommended only for certificates that are non-sensitive, or extremely short-lived. This option implies a value of "false" for "generate_lease".|
|» not_after|body|string|false|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ.|
|» not_before_duration|body|string(duration)|false|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|» organization|body|[string]|false|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|» ou|body|[string]|false|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|» policy_identifiers|body|[string]|false|A comma-separated string or list of policy OIDs, or a JSON list of qualified policy information, which must include an oid, and may include a notice and/or cps url, using the form [{"oid"="1.3.6.1.4.1.7.8","notice"="I am a user Notice"}, {"oid"="1.3.6.1.4.1.44947.1.2.4 ","cps"="https://example.com"}].|
|» postal_code|body|[string]|false|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|» province|body|[string]|false|If set, Province will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|» require_cn|body|boolean|false|If set to false, makes the 'common_name' field optional while generating a certificate.|
|» server_flag|body|boolean|false|If set, certificates are flagged for server auth use. Defaults to true. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|» signature_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|» street_address|body|[string]|false|If set, Street Address will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The lease duration (validity period of the certificate) if no specific lease duration is requested. The lease duration controls the expiration of certificates issued by this backend. Defaults to the system default value or the value of max_ttl, whichever is shorter.|
|» use_csr_common_name|body|boolean|false|If set, when used with a signing profile, the common name in the CSR will be used. This does *not* include any requested Subject Alternative Names; use use_csr_sans for that. Defaults to true.|
|» use_csr_sans|body|boolean|false|If set, when used with a signing profile, the SANs in the CSR will be used. This does *not* include the Common Name (cn); use use_csr_common_name for that. Defaults to true.|
|» use_pss|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to use PSS signatures when using a RSA key-type issuer. Defaults to false.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» key_type|rsa|
|» key_type|ec|
|» key_type|ed25519|
|» key_type|any|

<h3 id="pki-generate-root-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exported|path|string|true|Must be "internal", "exported" or "kms". If set to "exported", the generated private key will be returned. This is your *only* chance to retrieve the private key!|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiGenerateRootRequest](#schemapkigeneraterootrequest)|true|none|
|» alt_names|body|string|false|The requested Subject Alternative Names, if any, in a comma-delimited list. May contain both DNS names and email addresses.|
|» common_name|body|string|false|The requested common name; if you want more than one, specify the alternative names in the alt_names map. If not specified when signing, the common name will be taken from the CSR; other names must still be specified in alt_names or ip_sans.|
|» country|body|[string]|false|If set, Country will be set to this value.|
|» exclude_cn_from_sans|body|boolean|false|If true, the Common Name will not be included in DNS or Email Subject Alternate Names. Defaults to false (CN is included).|
|» format|body|string|false|Format for returned data. Can be "pem", "der", or "pem_bundle". If "pem_bundle", any private key and issuing cert will be appended to the certificate pem. If "der", the value will be base64 encoded. Defaults to "pem".|
|» ip_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested IP SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list|
|» issuer_name|body|string|false|Provide a name to the generated or existing issuer, the name must be unique across all issuers and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|» key_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|» key_name|body|string|false|Provide a name to the generated or existing key, the name must be unique across all keys and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|» key_ref|body|string|false|Reference to a existing key; either "default" for the configured default key, an identifier or the name assigned to the key.|
|» key_type|body|string|false|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec" and "ed25519" are the only valid values.|
|» locality|body|[string]|false|If set, Locality will be set to this value.|
|» managed_key_id|body|string|false|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_name is required. Ignored for other types.|
|» managed_key_name|body|string|false|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_id is required. Ignored for other types.|
|» max_path_length|body|integer|false|The maximum allowable path length|
|» not_after|body|string|false|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|» not_before_duration|body|string(duration)|false|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|» organization|body|[string]|false|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value.|
|» other_sans|body|[string]|false|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|
|» ou|body|[string]|false|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value.|
|» permitted_dns_domains|body|[string]|false|Domains for which this certificate is allowed to sign or issue child certificates. If set, all DNS names (subject and alt) on child certs must be exact matches or subsets of the given domains (see https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.10).|
|» postal_code|body|[string]|false|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value.|
|» private_key_format|body|string|false|Format for the returned private key. Generally the default will be controlled by the "format" parameter as either base64-encoded DER or PEM-encoded DER. However, this can be set to "pkcs8" to have the returned private key contain base64-encoded pkcs8 or PEM-encoded pkcs8 instead. Defaults to "der".|
|» province|body|[string]|false|If set, Province will be set to this value.|
|» serial_number|body|string|false|The Subject's requested serial number, if any. See RFC 4519 Section 2.31 'serialNumber' for a description of this field. If you want more than one, specify alternative names in the alt_names map using OID 2.5.4.5. This has no impact on the final certificate's Serial Number field.|
|» signature_bits|body|integer|false|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|» street_address|body|[string]|false|If set, Street Address will be set to this value.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the mount max TTL. Note: this only has an effect when generating a CA cert or signing a CA cert, not when generating a CSR for an intermediate CA.|
|» uri_sans|body|[string]|false|The requested URI SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list.|
|» use_pss|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to use PSS signatures when using a RSA key-type issuer. Defaults to false.|

## pki-tidy

<a id="opIdpki-tidy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/pki/tidy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "acme_account_safety_buffer": 2592000,
    "issuer_safety_buffer": 31536000,
    "pause_duration": "0s",
    "revocation_queue_safety_buffer": 172800,
    "safety_buffer": 259200,
    "tidy_acme": false,
    "tidy_cert_store": true,
    "tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs": true,
    "tidy_expired_issuers": true,
    "tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle": true,
    "tidy_revocation_list": true,
    "tidy_revocation_queue": false,
    "tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations": true,
    "tidy_revoked_certs": true
  }'
```

`POST /{pki_mount_path}/tidy`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acme_account_safety_buffer": 2592000,
  "issuer_safety_buffer": 31536000,
  "pause_duration": "0s",
  "revocation_queue_safety_buffer": 172800,
  "safety_buffer": 259200,
  "tidy_acme": false,
  "tidy_cert_store": true,
  "tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs": true,
  "tidy_expired_issuers": true,
  "tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle": true,
  "tidy_revocation_list": true,
  "tidy_revocation_queue": false,
  "tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations": true,
  "tidy_revoked_certs": true
}
```

<h3 id="pki-tidy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pki_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[PkiTidyRequest](#schemapkitidyrequest)|true|none|
|» acme_account_safety_buffer|body|string(duration)|false|The amount of time that must pass after creation that an account with no orders is marked revoked, and the amount of time after being marked revoked or deactivated.|
|» issuer_safety_buffer|body|string(duration)|false|The amount of extra time that must have passed beyond issuer's expiration before it is removed from the backend storage. Defaults to 8760 hours (1 year).|
|» pause_duration|body|string|false|The amount of time to wait between processing certificates. This allows operators to change the execution profile of tidy to take consume less resources by slowing down how long it takes to run. Note that the entire list of certificates will be stored in memory during the entire tidy operation, but resources to read/process/update existing entries will be spread out over a greater period of time. By default this is zero seconds.|
|» revocation_queue_safety_buffer|body|string(duration)|false|The amount of time that must pass from the cross-cluster revocation request being initiated to when it will be slated for removal. Setting this too low may remove valid revocation requests before the owning cluster has a chance to process them, especially if the cluster is offline.|
|» safety_buffer|body|string(duration)|false|The amount of extra time that must have passed beyond certificate expiration before it is removed from the backend storage and/or revocation list. Defaults to 72 hours.|
|» tidy_acme|body|boolean|false|Set to true to enable tidying ACME accounts, orders and authorizations. ACME orders are tidied (deleted) safety_buffer after the certificate associated with them expires, or after the order and relevant authorizations have expired if no certificate was produced. Authorizations are tidied with the corresponding order. When a valid ACME Account is at least acme_account_safety_buffer old, and has no remaining orders associated with it, the account is marked as revoked. After another acme_account_safety_buffer has passed from the revocation or deactivation date, a revoked or deactivated ACME account is deleted.|
|» tidy_cert_store|body|boolean|false|Set to true to enable tidying up the certificate store|
|» tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs|body|boolean|false|Set to true to enable tidying up the cross-cluster revoked certificate store. Only runs on the active primary node.|
|» tidy_expired_issuers|body|boolean|false|Set to true to automatically remove expired issuers past the issuer_safety_buffer. No keys will be removed as part of this operation.|
|» tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle|body|boolean|false|Set to true to move the legacy ca_bundle from /config/ca_bundle to /config/ca_bundle.bak. This prevents downgrades to pre-Vault 1.11 versions (as older PKI engines do not know about the new multi-issuer storage layout), but improves the performance on seal wrapped PKI mounts. This will only occur if at least issuer_safety_buffer time has occurred after the initial storage migration. This backup is saved in case of an issue in future migrations. Operators may consider removing it via sys/raw if they desire. The backup will be removed via a DELETE /root call, but note that this removes ALL issuers within the mount (and is thus not desirable in most operational scenarios).|
|» tidy_revocation_list|body|boolean|false|Deprecated; synonym for 'tidy_revoked_certs|
|» tidy_revocation_queue|body|boolean|false|Set to true to remove stale revocation queue entries that haven't been confirmed by any active cluster. Only runs on the active primary node|
|» tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations|body|boolean|false|Set to true to validate issuer associations on revocation entries. This helps increase the performance of CRL building and OCSP responses.|
|» tidy_revoked_certs|body|boolean|false|Set to true to expire all revoked and expired certificates, removing them both from the CRL and from storage. The CRL will be rotated if this causes any values to be removed.|

<h3 id="pki-tidy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
  }'
```

```bash
  "cert_type": "user",
  "critical_options": {},

  "key_bits": 0,
  "key_id": "string",
  "key_type": "rsa",
  "ttl": "string",
```

```json
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|path|string|true|The desired role with configuration for this request.|

|body|body|[SshIssueCertificateRequest](#schemasshissuecertificaterequest)|true|none|
|» cert_type|body|string|false|Type of certificate to be created; either "user" or "host".|
|» critical_options|body|object(map)|false|Critical options that the certificate should be signed for.|
|» extensions|body|object(map)|false|Extensions that the certificate should be signed for.|
|» key_bits|body|integer|false|Specifies the number of bits to use for the generated keys.|
|» key_id|body|string|false|Key id that the created certificate should have. If not specified, the display name of the token will be used.|
|» key_type|body|string|false|Specifies the desired key type; must be `rsa`, `ed25519` or `ec`|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|The requested Time To Live for the SSH certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be later than the role max TTL.|

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/ssh/roles/string \

  -d '{
    "algorithm_signer": "",

    "allow_host_certificates": false,
    "allow_subdomains": true,
    "allow_user_certificates": false,
    "allow_user_key_ids": true,
    "allowed_critical_options": "string",
    "allowed_domains": "string",
    "allowed_domains_template": false,
    "allowed_extensions": "string",
    "allowed_user_key_lengths": {},
    "allowed_users": "string",
    "allowed_users_template": false,
    "cidr_list": "string",
    "default_critical_options": {},
    "default_extensions": {},
    "default_extensions_template": false,
    "default_user": "string",
    "default_user_template": false,
    "exclude_cidr_list": "string",
    "key_id_format": "string",
    "key_type": "otp",
    "max_ttl": "string",
    "not_before_duration": 30,
    "port": 0,
    "ttl": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{ssh_mount_path}/roles/{role}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "algorithm_signer": "",
  "allow_bare_domains": true,
  "allow_host_certificates": false,
  "allow_subdomains": true,
  "allow_user_certificates": false,
  "allow_user_key_ids": true,
  "allowed_critical_options": "string",
  "allowed_domains": "string",
  "allowed_domains_template": false,
  "allowed_extensions": "string",
  "allowed_user_key_lengths": {},
  "allowed_users": "string",
  "allowed_users_template": false,
  "cidr_list": "string",
  "default_critical_options": {},
  "default_extensions": {},
  "default_extensions_template": false,
  "default_user": "string",
  "default_user_template": false,
  "exclude_cidr_list": "string",
  "key_id_format": "string",
  "key_type": "otp",
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "not_before_duration": 30,
  "port": 0,
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="manage-the-roles-that-can-be-created-with-this-backend-10-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|path|string|true|[Required for all types] Name of the role being created.|
|ssh_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[SshWriteRoleRequest](#schemasshwriterolerequest)|true|none|
|» algorithm_signer|body|string|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] When supplied, this value specifies a signing algorithm for the key. Possible values: ssh-rsa, rsa-sha2-256, rsa-sha2-512, default, or the empty string.|
|» allow_bare_domains|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, host certificates that are requested are allowed to use the base domains listed in "allowed_domains", e.g. "example.com". This is a separate option as in some cases this can be considered a security threat.|
|» allow_host_certificates|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, certificates are allowed to be signed for use as a 'host'.|
|» allow_subdomains|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, host certificates that are requested are allowed to use subdomains of those listed in "allowed_domains".|
|» allow_user_certificates|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, certificates are allowed to be signed for use as a 'user'.|
|» allow_user_key_ids|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If true, users can override the key ID for a signed certificate with the "key_id" field. When false, the key ID will always be the token display name. The key ID is logged by the SSH server and can be useful for auditing.|
|» allowed_critical_options|body|string|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] A comma-separated list of critical options that certificates can have when signed. To allow any critical options, set this to an empty string.|
|» allowed_domains|body|string|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If this option is not specified, client can request for a signed certificate for any valid host. If only certain domains are allowed, then this list enforces it.|
|» allowed_domains_template|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, Allowed domains can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated domains are also permitted.|
|» allowed_extensions|body|string|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] A comma-separated list of extensions that certificates can have when signed. An empty list means that no extension overrides are allowed by an end-user; explicitly specify '*' to allow any extensions to be set.|
|» allowed_user_key_lengths|body|object(map)|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, allows the enforcement of key types and minimum key sizes to be signed.|
|» allowed_users|body|string|false|[Optional for all types] [Works differently for CA type] If this option is not specified, or is '*', client can request a credential for any valid user at the remote host, including the admin user. If only certain usernames are to be allowed, then this list enforces it. If this field is set, then credentials can only be created for default_user and usernames present in this list. Setting this option will enable all the users with access to this role to fetch credentials for all other usernames in this list. Use with caution. N.B.: with the CA type, an empty list means that no users are allowed; explicitly specify '*' to allow any user.|
|» allowed_users_template|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, Allowed users can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated users are also permitted.|
|» cidr_list|body|string|false|[Optional for OTP type] [Not applicable for CA type] Comma separated list of CIDR blocks for which the role is applicable for. CIDR blocks can belong to more than one role.|
|» default_critical_options|body|object(map)|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] Critical options certificates should have if none are provided when signing. This field takes in key value pairs in JSON format. Note that these are not restricted by "allowed_critical_options". Defaults to none.|
|» default_extensions|body|object(map)|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] Extensions certificates should have if none are provided when signing. This field takes in key value pairs in JSON format. Note that these are not restricted by "allowed_extensions". Defaults to none.|
|» default_extensions_template|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, Default extension values can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated extension values are also permitted.|
|» default_user|body|string|false|[Required for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] Default username for which a credential will be generated. When the endpoint 'creds/' is used without a username, this value will be used as default username.|
|» default_user_template|body|boolean|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] If set, Default user can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated users are also permitted.|
|» exclude_cidr_list|body|string|false|[Optional for OTP type] [Not applicable for CA type] Comma separated list of CIDR blocks. IP addresses belonging to these blocks are not accepted by the role. This is particularly useful when big CIDR blocks are being used by the role and certain parts of it needs to be kept out.|
|» key_id_format|body|string|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] When supplied, this value specifies a custom format for the key id of a signed certificate. The following variables are available for use: '{{token_display_name}}' - The display name of the token used to make the request. '{{role_name}}' - The name of the role signing the request. '{{public_key_hash}}' - A SHA256 checksum of the public key that is being signed.|
|» key_type|body|string|false|[Required for all types] Type of key used to login to hosts. It can be either 'otp' or 'ca'. 'otp' type requires agent to be installed in remote hosts.|
|» max_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] The maximum allowed lease duration|
|» not_before_duration|body|string(duration)|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] The duration that the SSH certificate should be backdated by at issuance.|
|» port|body|integer|false|[Optional for OTP type] [Not applicable for CA type] Port number for SSH connection. Default is '22'. Port number does not play any role in creation of OTP. For 'otp' type, this is just a way to inform client about the port number to use. Port number will be returned to client by Vault server along with OTP.|
|» ttl|body|string(duration)|false|[Not applicable for OTP type] [Optional for CA type] The lease duration if no specific lease duration is requested. The lease duration controls the expiration of certificates issued by this backend. Defaults to the value of max_ttl.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» algorithm_signer|""|
|» algorithm_signer|default|
|» algorithm_signer|ssh-rsa|
|» algorithm_signer|rsa-sha2-256|
|» algorithm_signer|rsa-sha2-512|
|» key_type|otp|
|» key_type|ca|

<h3 id="manage-the-roles-that-can-be-created-with-this-backend-10-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

## totp-create-key

<a id="opIdtotp-create-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/totp/keys/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "account_name": "string",
    "algorithm": "SHA1",
    "digits": 6,
    "exported": true,
    "generate": false,
    "issuer": "string",
    "key": "string",
    "key_size": 20,
    "period": 30,
    "qr_size": 200,
    "skew": 1,
    "url": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{totp_mount_path}/keys/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_name": "string",
  "algorithm": "SHA1",
  "digits": 6,
  "exported": true,
  "generate": false,
  "issuer": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "key_size": 20,
  "period": 30,
  "qr_size": 200,
  "skew": 1,
  "url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="totp-create-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the key.|
|totp_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[TotpCreateKeyRequest](#schematotpcreatekeyrequest)|true|none|
|» account_name|body|string|false|The name of the account associated with the key. Required if generate is true.|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|The hashing algorithm used to generate the TOTP token. Options include SHA1, SHA256 and SHA512.|
|» digits|body|integer|false|The number of digits in the generated TOTP token. This value can either be 6 or 8.|
|» exported|body|boolean|false|Determines if a QR code and url are returned upon generating a key. Only used if generate is true.|
|» generate|body|boolean|false|Determines if a key should be generated by Vault or if a key is being passed from another service.|
|» issuer|body|string|false|The name of the key's issuing organization. Required if generate is true.|
|» key|body|string|false|The shared master key used to generate a TOTP token. Only used if generate is false.|
|» key_size|body|integer|false|Determines the size in bytes of the generated key. Only used if generate is true.|
|» period|body|string(duration)|false|The length of time used to generate a counter for the TOTP token calculation.|
|» qr_size|body|integer|false|The pixel size of the generated square QR code. Only used if generate is true and exported is true. If this value is 0, a QR code will not be returned.|
|» skew|body|integer|false|The number of delay periods that are allowed when validating a TOTP token. This value can either be 0 or 1. Only used if generate is true.|
|» url|body|string|false|A TOTP url string containing all of the parameters for key setup. Only used if generate is false.|

<h3 id="totp-create-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/transit/datakey/string/string \
  -X POST \

  }'
```

```json
  "context": "string",
  "key_version": 0,
  "nonce": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-data-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|The backend key used for encrypting the data key|
|plaintext|path|string|true|"plaintext" will return the key in both plaintext and ciphertext; "wrapped" will return the ciphertext only.|
|transit_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[TransitGenerateDataKeyRequest](#schematransitgeneratedatakeyrequest)|true|none|
|» bits|body|integer|false|Number of bits for the key; currently 128, 256, and 512 bits are supported. Defaults to 256.|
|» context|body|string|false|Context for key derivation. Required for derived keys.|
|» key_version|body|integer|false|The version of the Vault key to use for encryption of the data key. Must be 0 (for latest) or a value greater than or equal to the min_encryption_version configured on the key.|
|» nonce|body|string|false|Nonce for when convergent encryption v1 is used (only in Vault 0.6.1)|

## Decrypt a ciphertext value using a named key

<a id="opIdtransit-decrypt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/transit/decrypt/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "associated_data": "string",
    "batch_input": [
      {}
    ],
    "ciphertext": "string",
    "context": "string",
    "nonce": "string",
    "partial_failure_response_code": 0
  }'
```

`POST /{transit_mount_path}/decrypt/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "associated_data": "string",
  "batch_input": [
    {}
  ],
  "ciphertext": "string",
  "context": "string",
  "nonce": "string",
  "partial_failure_response_code": 0
}
```

<h3 id="decrypt-a-ciphertext-value-using-a-named-key-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the key|
|transit_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[TransitDecryptRequest](#schematransitdecryptrequest)|true|none|
|» associated_data|body|string|false|When using an AEAD cipher mode, such as AES-GCM, this parameter allows passing associated data (AD/AAD) into the encryption function; this data must be passed on subsequent decryption requests but can be transited in plaintext. On successful decryption, both the ciphertext and the associated data are attested not to have been tampered with.|
|» batch_input|body|[object]|false|Specifies a list of items to be decrypted in a single batch. When this parameter is set, if the parameters 'ciphertext', 'context' and 'nonce' are also set, they will be ignored. Any batch output will preserve the order of the batch input.|
|» ciphertext|body|string|false|The ciphertext to decrypt, provided as returned by encrypt.|
|» context|body|string|false|Base64 encoded context for key derivation. Required if key derivation is enabled.|
|» nonce|body|string|false|Base64 encoded nonce value used during encryption. Must be provided if convergent encryption is enabled for this key and the key was generated with Vault 0.6.1. Not required for keys created in 0.6.2+.|
|» partial_failure_response_code|body|integer|false|Ordinarily, if a batch item fails to decrypt due to a bad input, but other batch items succeed, the HTTP response code is 400 (Bad Request). Some applications may want to treat partial failures differently. Providing the parameter returns the given response code integer instead of a 400 in this case. If all values fail HTTP 400 is still returned.|

<h3 id="decrypt-a-ciphertext-value-using-a-named-key-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Encrypt a plaintext value or a batch of plaintext blocks using a named key

<a id="opIdtransit-encrypt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/transit/encrypt/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "associated_data": "string",
    "batch_input": [
      {}
    ],
    "context": "string",
    "convergent_encryption": true,
    "key_version": 0,
    "nonce": "string",
    "partial_failure_response_code": 0,
    "plaintext": "string",
    "type": "aes256-gcm96"
  }'
```

`POST /{transit_mount_path}/encrypt/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "associated_data": "string",
  "batch_input": [
    {}
  ],
  "context": "string",
  "convergent_encryption": true,
  "key_version": 0,
  "nonce": "string",
  "partial_failure_response_code": 0,
  "plaintext": "string",
  "type": "aes256-gcm96"
}
```

<h3 id="encrypt-a-plaintext-value-or-a-batch-of-plaintext-blocks-using-a-named-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the key|
|transit_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[TransitEncryptRequest](#schematransitencryptrequest)|true|none|
|» associated_data|body|string|false|When using an AEAD cipher mode, such as AES-GCM, this parameter allows passing associated data (AD/AAD) into the encryption function; this data must be passed on subsequent decryption requests but can be transited in plaintext. On successful decryption, both the ciphertext and the associated data are attested not to have been tampered with.|
|» batch_input|body|[object]|false|Specifies a list of items to be encrypted in a single batch. When this parameter is set, if the parameters 'plaintext', 'context' and 'nonce' are also set, they will be ignored. Any batch output will preserve the order of the batch input.|
|» context|body|string|false|Base64 encoded context for key derivation. Required if key derivation is enabled|
|» convergent_encryption|body|boolean|false|This parameter will only be used when a key is expected to be created. Whether to support convergent encryption. This is only supported when using a key with key derivation enabled and will require all requests to carry both a context and 96-bit (12-byte) nonce. The given nonce will be used in place of a randomly generated nonce. As a result, when the same context and nonce are supplied, the same ciphertext is generated. It is *very important* when using this mode that you ensure that all nonces are unique for a given context. Failing to do so will severely impact the ciphertext's security.|
|» key_version|body|integer|false|The version of the key to use for encryption. Must be 0 (for latest) or a value greater than or equal to the min_encryption_version configured on the key.|
|» nonce|body|string|false|Base64 encoded nonce value. Must be provided if convergent encryption is enabled for this key and the key was generated with Vault 0.6.1. Not required for keys created in 0.6.2+. The value must be exactly 96 bits (12 bytes) long and the user must ensure that for any given context (and thus, any given encryption key) this nonce value is **never reused**.|
|» partial_failure_response_code|body|integer|false|Ordinarily, if a batch item fails to encrypt due to a bad input, but other batch items succeed, the HTTP response code is 400 (Bad Request). Some applications may want to treat partial failures differently. Providing the parameter returns the given response code integer instead of a 400 in this case. If all values fail HTTP 400 is still returned.|
|» plaintext|body|string|false|Base64 encoded plaintext value to be encrypted|
|» type|body|string|false|This parameter is required when encryption key is expected to be created. When performing an upsert operation, the type of key to create. Currently, "aes128-gcm96" (symmetric) and "aes256-gcm96" (symmetric) are the only types supported. Defaults to "aes256-gcm96".|

<h3 id="encrypt-a-plaintext-value-or-a-batch-of-plaintext-blocks-using-a-named-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## transit-create-key

<a id="opIdtransit-create-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/transit/keys/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "allow_plaintext_backup": true,
    "auto_rotate_period": 0,
    "context": "string",
    "convergent_encryption": true,
    "derived": true,
    "exportable": true,
    "key_size": 0,
    "managed_key_id": "string",
    "managed_key_name": "string",
    "type": "aes256-gcm96"
  }'
```

`POST /{transit_mount_path}/keys/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_plaintext_backup": true,
  "auto_rotate_period": 0,
  "context": "string",
  "convergent_encryption": true,
  "derived": true,
  "exportable": true,
  "key_size": 0,
  "managed_key_id": "string",
  "managed_key_name": "string",
  "type": "aes256-gcm96"
}
```

<h3 id="transit-create-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the key|
|transit_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[TransitCreateKeyRequest](#schematransitcreatekeyrequest)|true|none|
|» allow_plaintext_backup|body|boolean|false|Enables taking a backup of the named key in plaintext format. Once set, this cannot be disabled.|
|» auto_rotate_period|body|string(duration)|false|Amount of time the key should live before being automatically rotated. A value of 0 (default) disables automatic rotation for the key.|
|» context|body|string|false|Base64 encoded context for key derivation. When reading a key with key derivation enabled, if the key type supports public keys, this will return the public key for the given context.|
|» convergent_encryption|body|boolean|false|Whether to support convergent encryption. This is only supported when using a key with key derivation enabled and will require all requests to carry both a context and 96-bit (12-byte) nonce. The given nonce will be used in place of a randomly generated nonce. As a result, when the same context and nonce are supplied, the same ciphertext is generated. It is *very important* when using this mode that you ensure that all nonces are unique for a given context. Failing to do so will severely impact the ciphertext's security.|
|» derived|body|boolean|false|Enables key derivation mode. This allows for per-transaction unique keys for encryption operations.|
|» exportable|body|boolean|false|Enables keys to be exportable. This allows for all the valid keys in the key ring to be exported.|
|» key_size|body|integer|false|The key size in bytes for the algorithm. Only applies to HMAC and must be no fewer than 32 bytes and no more than 512|
|» managed_key_id|body|string|false|The UUID of the managed key to use for this transit key|
|» managed_key_name|body|string|false|The name of the managed key to use for this transit key|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of key to create. Currently, "aes128-gcm96" (symmetric), "aes256-gcm96" (symmetric), "ecdsa-p256" (asymmetric), "ecdsa-p384" (asymmetric), "ecdsa-p521" (asymmetric), "ed25519" (asymmetric), "rsa-2048" (asymmetric), "rsa-3072" (asymmetric), "rsa-4096" (asymmetric) are supported. Defaults to "aes256-gcm96".|

<h3 id="transit-create-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
  "allow_plaintext_backup": true,
```
```bash
  "allow_rotation": true,
  "auto_rotate_period": 0,
  "ciphertext": "string",
  "context": "string",
  "derived": true,
```

<h3 id="imports-an-externally-generated-key-into-a-new-transit-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|The name of the key|

|body|body|[TransitImportKeyRequest](#schematransitimportkeyrequest)|true|none|
|» allow_plaintext_backup|body|boolean|false|Enables taking a backup of the named key in plaintext format. Once set, this cannot be disabled.|
|» allow_rotation|body|boolean|false|True if the imported key may be rotated within Vault; false otherwise.|
|» auto_rotate_period|body|string(duration)|false|Amount of time the key should live before being automatically rotated. A value of 0 (default) disables automatic rotation for the key.|
|» ciphertext|body|string|false|The base64-encoded ciphertext of the keys. The AES key should be encrypted using OAEP with the wrapping key and then concatenated with the import key, wrapped by the AES key.|
|» context|body|string|false|Base64 encoded context for key derivation. When reading a key with key derivation enabled, if the key type supports public keys, this will return the public key for the given context.|
|» derived|body|boolean|false|Enables key derivation mode. This allows for per-transaction unique keys for encryption operations.|
|» exportable|body|boolean|false|Enables keys to be exportable. This allows for all the valid keys in the key ring to be exported.|
|» hash_function|body|string|false|The hash function used as a random oracle in the OAEP wrapping of the user-generated, ephemeral AES key. Can be one of "SHA1", "SHA224", "SHA256" (default), "SHA384", or "SHA512"|
|» public_key|body|string|false|The plaintext PEM public key to be imported. If "ciphertext" is set, this field is ignored.|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of key being imported. Currently, "aes128-gcm96" (symmetric), "aes256-gcm96" (symmetric), "ecdsa-p256" (asymmetric), "ecdsa-p384" (asymmetric), "ecdsa-p521" (asymmetric), "ed25519" (asymmetric), "rsa-2048" (asymmetric), "rsa-3072" (asymmetric), "rsa-4096" (asymmetric) are supported. Defaults to "aes256-gcm96".|

<h3 id="imports-an-externally-generated-key-into-a-new-transit-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Generate a signature for input data using the named key

<a id="opIdtransit-sign"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/transit/sign/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "algorithm": "sha2-256",
    "batch_input": [
      {}
    ],
    "context": "string",
    "hash_algorithm": "sha2-256",
    "input": "string",
    "key_version": 0,
    "marshaling_algorithm": "asn1",
    "prehashed": true,
    "salt_length": "auto",
    "signature_algorithm": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{transit_mount_path}/sign/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "algorithm": "sha2-256",
  "batch_input": [
    {}
  ],
  "context": "string",
  "hash_algorithm": "sha2-256",
  "input": "string",
  "key_version": 0,
  "marshaling_algorithm": "asn1",
  "prehashed": true,
  "salt_length": "auto",
  "signature_algorithm": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-signature-for-input-data-using-the-named-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|The key to use|
|transit_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[TransitSignRequest](#schematransitsignrequest)|true|none|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|Deprecated: use "hash_algorithm" instead.|
|» batch_input|body|[object]|false|Specifies a list of items for processing. When this parameter is set, any supplied 'input' or 'context' parameters will be ignored. Responses are returned in the 'batch_results' array component of the 'data' element of the response. Any batch output will preserve the order of the batch input|
|» context|body|string|false|Base64 encoded context for key derivation. Required if key derivation is enabled; currently only available with ed25519 keys.|
|» hash_algorithm|body|string|false|Hash algorithm to use (POST body parameter). Valid values are: * sha1 * sha2-224 * sha2-256 * sha2-384 * sha2-512 * sha3-224 * sha3-256 * sha3-384 * sha3-512 * none Defaults to "sha2-256". Not valid for all key types, including ed25519. Using none requires setting prehashed=true and signature_algorithm=pkcs1v15, yielding a PKCSv1_5_NoOID instead of the usual PKCSv1_5_DERnull signature.|
|» input|body|string|false|The base64-encoded input data|
|» key_version|body|integer|false|The version of the key to use for signing. Must be 0 (for latest) or a value greater than or equal to the min_encryption_version configured on the key.|
|» marshaling_algorithm|body|string|false|The method by which to marshal the signature. The default is 'asn1' which is used by openssl and X.509. It can also be set to 'jws' which is used for JWT signatures; setting it to this will also cause the encoding of the signature to be url-safe base64 instead of using standard base64 encoding. Currently only valid for ECDSA P-256 key types".|
|» prehashed|body|boolean|false|Set to 'true' when the input is already hashed. If the key type is 'rsa-2048', 'rsa-3072' or 'rsa-4096', then the algorithm used to hash the input should be indicated by the 'algorithm' parameter.|
|» salt_length|body|string|false|The salt length used to sign. Currently only applies to the RSA PSS signature scheme. Options are 'auto' (the default used by Golang, causing the salt to be as large as possible when signing), 'hash' (causes the salt length to equal the length of the hash used in the signature), or an integer between the minimum and the maximum permissible salt lengths for the given RSA key size. Defaults to 'auto'.|
|» signature_algorithm|body|string|false|The signature algorithm to use for signing. Currently only applies to RSA key types. Options are 'pss' or 'pkcs1v15'. Defaults to 'pss'|

<h3 id="generate-a-signature-for-input-data-using-the-named-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Verify a signature or HMAC for input data created using the named key

<a id="opIdtransit-verify"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/transit/verify/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "algorithm": "sha2-256",
    "batch_input": [
      {}
    ],
    "context": "string",
    "hash_algorithm": "sha2-256",
    "hmac": "string",
    "input": "string",
    "marshaling_algorithm": "asn1",
    "prehashed": true,
    "salt_length": "auto",
    "signature": "string",
    "signature_algorithm": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /{transit_mount_path}/verify/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "algorithm": "sha2-256",
  "batch_input": [
    {}
  ],
  "context": "string",
  "hash_algorithm": "sha2-256",
  "hmac": "string",
  "input": "string",
  "marshaling_algorithm": "asn1",
  "prehashed": true,
  "salt_length": "auto",
  "signature": "string",
  "signature_algorithm": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-a-signature-or-hmac-for-input-data-created-using-the-named-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|The key to use|
|transit_mount_path|path|string|true|Path that the backend was mounted at|
|body|body|[TransitVerifyRequest](#schematransitverifyrequest)|true|none|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|Deprecated: use "hash_algorithm" instead.|
|» batch_input|body|[object]|false|Specifies a list of items for processing. When this parameter is set, any supplied 'input', 'hmac' or 'signature' parameters will be ignored. Responses are returned in the 'batch_results' array component of the 'data' element of the response. Any batch output will preserve the order of the batch input|
|» context|body|string|false|Base64 encoded context for key derivation. Required if key derivation is enabled; currently only available with ed25519 keys.|
|» hash_algorithm|body|string|false|Hash algorithm to use (POST body parameter). Valid values are: * sha1 * sha2-224 * sha2-256 * sha2-384 * sha2-512 * sha3-224 * sha3-256 * sha3-384 * sha3-512 * none Defaults to "sha2-256". Not valid for all key types. See note about none on signing path.|
|» hmac|body|string|false|The HMAC, including vault header/key version|
|» input|body|string|false|The base64-encoded input data to verify|
|» marshaling_algorithm|body|string|false|The method by which to unmarshal the signature when verifying. The default is 'asn1' which is used by openssl and X.509; can also be set to 'jws' which is used for JWT signatures in which case the signature is also expected to be url-safe base64 encoding instead of standard base64 encoding. Currently only valid for ECDSA P-256 key types".|
|» prehashed|body|boolean|false|Set to 'true' when the input is already hashed. If the key type is 'rsa-2048', 'rsa-3072' or 'rsa-4096', then the algorithm used to hash the input should be indicated by the 'algorithm' parameter.|
|» salt_length|body|string|false|The salt length used to sign. Currently only applies to the RSA PSS signature scheme. Options are 'auto' (the default used by Golang, causing the salt to be as large as possible when signing), 'hash' (causes the salt length to equal the length of the hash used in the signature), or an integer between the minimum and the maximum permissible salt lengths for the given RSA key size. Defaults to 'auto'.|
|» signature|body|string|false|The signature, including vault header/key version|
|» signature_algorithm|body|string|false|The signature algorithm to use for signature verification. Currently only applies to RSA key types. Options are 'pss' or 'pkcs1v15'. Defaults to 'pss'|

<h3 id="verify-a-signature-or-hmac-for-input-data-created-using-the-named-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|» policies|body|[string]|false|Policies to be tied to the entity.|

```json
{
  "conflicting_alias_ids_to_keep": [
    "string"
  ],
  "force": true,
  "from_entity_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "to_entity_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="merge-two-or-more-entities-together-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[EntityMergeRequest](#schemaentitymergerequest)|true|none|

|» force|body|boolean|false|Setting this will follow the 'mine' strategy for merging MFA secrets. If there are secrets of the same type both in entities that are merged from and in entity into which all others are getting merged, secrets in the destination will be unaltered. If not set, this API will throw an error containing all the conflicts.|
|» from_entity_ids|body|[string]|false|Entity IDs which need to get merged|
|» to_entity_id|body|string|false|Entity ID into which all the other entities need to get merged|

```bash
    "qr_size": 200,
    "skew": 1
  }'
```

`POST /identity/mfa/method/totp`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "algorithm": "SHA1",
  "digits": 6,
  "issuer": "string",
  "key_size": 20,
  "max_validation_attempts": 0,
  "method_name": "string",
  "period": 30,
  "qr_size": 200,
  "skew": 1
}
```

<h3 id="create-the-given-mfa-method-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[MfaCreateTotpMethodRequest](#schemamfacreatetotpmethodrequest)|true|none|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|The hashing algorithm used to generate the TOTP token. Options include SHA1, SHA256 and SHA512.|
|» digits|body|integer|false|The number of digits in the generated TOTP token. This value can either be 6 or 8.|
|» issuer|body|string|false|The name of the key's issuing organization.|
|» key_size|body|integer|false|Determines the size in bytes of the generated key.|
|» max_validation_attempts|body|integer|false|Max number of allowed validation attempts.|
|» method_name|body|string|false|The unique name identifier for this MFA method.|
|» period|body|string(duration)|false|The length of time used to generate a counter for the TOTP token calculation.|
|» qr_size|body|integer|false|The pixel size of the generated square QR code.|
|» skew|body|integer|false|The number of delay periods that are allowed when validating a TOTP token. This value can either be 0 or 1.|

## CRUD operations for OIDC keys.

<a id="opIdoidc-write-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/identity/oidc/key/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "algorithm": "RS256",
    "allowed_client_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "rotation_period": "24h",
    "verification_ttl": "24h"
  }'
```

`POST /identity/oidc/key/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "algorithm": "RS256",
  "allowed_client_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "rotation_period": "24h",
  "verification_ttl": "24h"
}
```

<h3 id="crud-operations-for-oidc-keys-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the key|
|body|body|[OidcWriteKeyRequest](#schemaoidcwritekeyrequest)|true|none|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|Signing algorithm to use. This will default to RS256.|
|» allowed_client_ids|body|[string]|false|Comma separated string or array of role client ids allowed to use this key for signing. If empty no roles are allowed. If "*" all roles are allowed.|
|» rotation_period|body|string(duration)|false|How often to generate a new keypair.|
|» verification_ttl|body|string(duration)|false|Controls how long the public portion of a key will be available for verification after being rotated.|

<h3 id="crud-operations-for-oidc-keys-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|max_age|query|integer|false|The allowable elapsed time in seconds since the last time the end-user was actively authenticated.|
|nonce|query|string|false|The value that will be returned in the ID token nonce claim after a token exchange.|
|redirect_uri|query|string|false|The redirection URI to which the response will be sent.|
|response_type|query|string|false|The OIDC authentication flow to be used. The following response types are supported: 'code'|
|scope|query|string|false|A space-delimited, case-sensitive list of scopes to be requested. The 'openid' scope is required.|
|state|query|string|false|The value used to maintain state between the authentication request and client.|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the provider|

<h3 id="oidc-provider-authorize-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

## Enables a new auth method.

<a id="opIdauth-enable-method"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/auth/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "config": {},
    "description": "string",
    "external_entropy_access": false,
    "local": false,
    "options": {},
    "plugin_name": "string",
    "plugin_version": "string",
    "seal_wrap": false,
    "type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sys/auth/{path}`

After enabling, the auth method can be accessed and configured via the auth path specified as part of the URL. This auth path will be nested under the auth prefix.

For example, enable the "foo" auth method will make it accessible at /auth/foo.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "config": {},
  "description": "string",
  "external_entropy_access": false,
  "local": false,
  "options": {},
  "plugin_name": "string",
  "plugin_version": "string",
  "seal_wrap": false,
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="enables-a-new-auth-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|path|string|true|The path to mount to. Cannot be delimited. Example: "user"|
|body|body|[AuthEnableMethodRequest](#schemaauthenablemethodrequest)|true|none|
|» config|body|object(map)|false|Configuration for this mount, such as plugin_name.|
|» description|body|string|false|User-friendly description for this credential backend.|
|» external_entropy_access|body|boolean|false|Whether to give the mount access to Vault's external entropy.|
|» local|body|boolean|false|Mark the mount as a local mount, which is not replicated and is unaffected by replication.|
|» options|body|object(kvpairs)|false|The options to pass into the backend. Should be a json object with string keys and values.|
|» plugin_name|body|string|false|Name of the auth plugin to use based from the name in the plugin catalog.|
|» plugin_version|body|string|false|The semantic version of the plugin to use, or image tag if oci_image is provided.|
|» seal_wrap|body|boolean|false|Whether to turn on seal wrapping for the mount.|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of the backend. Example: "userpass"|

<h3 id="enables-a-new-auth-method-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
  "allowed_managed_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_response_headers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "audit_non_hmac_request_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "audit_non_hmac_response_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "default_lease_ttl": 0,
  "description": "string",
  "external_entropy_access": true,
  "force_no_cache": true,
  "listing_visibility": "string",
  "max_lease_ttl": 0,
  "options": {},
  "passthrough_request_headers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "plugin_version": "string",
  "token_type": "string",
  "user_lockout_counter_reset_duration": 0,
  "user_lockout_disable": true,
  "user_lockout_duration": 0,
  "user_lockout_threshold": 0
}
```

<h3 id="reads-the-given-auth-paths-configuration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AuthReadTuningInformationResponse](#schemaauthreadtuninginformationresponse)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Tune configuration parameters for a given auth path.

<a id="opIdauth-tune-configuration-parameters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/auth/string/tune \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "allowed_response_headers": [
      "string"
    ],
    "audit_non_hmac_request_keys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "audit_non_hmac_response_keys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "default_lease_ttl": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "listing_visibility": "string",
    "max_lease_ttl": "string",
    "options": {},
    "passthrough_request_headers": [
      "string"
    ],
    "plugin_version": "string",
    "token_type": "string",
    "user_lockout_config": {}
  }'
```

`POST /sys/auth/{path}/tune`

This endpoint requires sudo capability on the final path, but the same functionality can be achieved without sudo via `sys/mounts/auth/[auth-path]/tune`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowed_response_headers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "audit_non_hmac_request_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "audit_non_hmac_response_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "default_lease_ttl": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "listing_visibility": "string",
  "max_lease_ttl": "string",
  "options": {},
  "passthrough_request_headers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "plugin_version": "string",
  "token_type": "string",
  "user_lockout_config": {}
}
```

<h3 id="tune-configuration-parameters-for-a-given-auth-path-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|path|string|true|Tune the configuration parameters for an auth path.|
|body|body|[AuthTuneConfigurationParametersRequest](#schemaauthtuneconfigurationparametersrequest)|true|none|
|» allowed_response_headers|body|[string]|false|A list of headers to whitelist and allow a plugin to set on responses.|
|» audit_non_hmac_request_keys|body|[string]|false|The list of keys in the request data object that will not be HMAC'ed by audit devices.|
|» audit_non_hmac_response_keys|body|[string]|false|The list of keys in the response data object that will not be HMAC'ed by audit devices.|
|» default_lease_ttl|body|string|false|The default lease TTL for this mount.|
|» description|body|string|false|User-friendly description for this credential backend.|
|» listing_visibility|body|string|false|Determines the visibility of the mount in the UI-specific listing endpoint. Accepted value are 'unauth' and 'hidden', with the empty default ('') behaving like 'hidden'.|
|» max_lease_ttl|body|string|false|The max lease TTL for this mount.|
|» options|body|object(kvpairs)|false|The options to pass into the backend. Should be a json object with string keys and values.|
|» passthrough_request_headers|body|[string]|false|A list of headers to whitelist and pass from the request to the plugin.|
|» plugin_version|body|string|false|The semantic version of the plugin to use, or image tag if oci_image is provided.|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to issue (service or batch).|
|» user_lockout_config|body|object(map)|false|The user lockout configuration to pass into the backend. Should be a json object with string keys and values.|

<h3 id="tune-configuration-parameters-for-a-given-auth-path-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Enter a single unseal key share to progress the root generation attempt.

<a id="opIdroot-token-generation-update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/generate-root/update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "key": "string",
    "nonce": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sys/generate-root/update`

If the threshold number of unseal key shares is reached, Vault will complete the root generation and issue the new token. Otherwise, this API must be called multiple times until that threshold is met. The attempt nonce must be provided with each call.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "key": "string",
  "nonce": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="enter-a-single-unseal-key-share-to-progress-the-root-generation-attempt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RootTokenGenerationUpdateRequest](#schemaroottokengenerationupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» key|body|string|false|Specifies a single unseal key share.|
|» nonce|body|string|false|Specifies the nonce of the attempt.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "complete": true,
  "encoded_root_token": "string",
  "encoded_token": "string",
  "nonce": "string",
  "otp": "string",
  "otp_length": 0,
  "pgp_fingerprint": "string",
  "progress": 0,
  "required": 0,
  "started": true
}
```

<h3 id="enter-a-single-unseal-key-share-to-progress-the-root-generation-attempt-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

## Initialize a new Vault.

<a id="opIdinitialize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/init \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "pgp_keys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "recovery_pgp_keys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "recovery_shares": 0,
    "recovery_threshold": 0,
    "root_token_pgp_key": "string",
    "secret_shares": 0,
    "secret_threshold": 0,
    "stored_shares": 0
  }'
```

`POST /sys/init`

The Vault must not have been previously initialized. The recovery options, as well as the stored shares option, are only available when using Vault HSM.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pgp_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "recovery_pgp_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "recovery_shares": 0,
  "recovery_threshold": 0,
  "root_token_pgp_key": "string",
  "secret_shares": 0,
  "secret_threshold": 0,
  "stored_shares": 0
}
```

<h3 id="initialize-a-new-vault-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InitializeRequest](#schemainitializerequest)|true|none|
|» pgp_keys|body|[string]|false|Specifies an array of PGP public keys used to encrypt the output unseal keys. Ordering is preserved. The keys must be base64-encoded from their original binary representation. The size of this array must be the same as `secret_shares`.|
|» recovery_pgp_keys|body|[string]|false|Specifies an array of PGP public keys used to encrypt the output recovery keys. Ordering is preserved. The keys must be base64-encoded from their original binary representation. The size of this array must be the same as `recovery_shares`.|
|» recovery_shares|body|integer|false|Specifies the number of shares to split the recovery key into.|
|» recovery_threshold|body|integer|false|Specifies the number of shares required to reconstruct the recovery key. This must be less than or equal to `recovery_shares`.|
|» root_token_pgp_key|body|string|false|Specifies a PGP public key used to encrypt the initial root token. The key must be base64-encoded from its original binary representation.|
|» secret_shares|body|integer|false|Specifies the number of shares to split the unseal key into.|
|» secret_threshold|body|integer|false|Specifies the number of shares required to reconstruct the unseal key. This must be less than or equal secret_shares. If using Vault HSM with auto-unsealing, this value must be the same as `secret_shares`.|
|» stored_shares|body|integer|false|Specifies the number of shares that should be encrypted by the HSM and stored for auto-unsealing. Currently must be the same as `secret_shares`.|

<h3 id="initialize-a-new-vault-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Revokes all secrets or tokens generated under a given prefix immediately

<a id="opIdleases-force-revoke-lease-with-prefix"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/leases/revoke-force/string \
  -X POST
```

`POST /sys/leases/revoke-force/{prefix}`

Unlike `/sys/leases/revoke-prefix`, this path ignores backend errors encountered during revocation. This is potentially very dangerous and should only be used in specific emergency situations where errors in the backend or the connected backend service prevent normal revocation.

By ignoring these errors, Vault abdicates responsibility for ensuring that the issued credentials or secrets are properly revoked and/or cleaned up. Access to this endpoint should be tightly controlled.

<h3 id="revokes-all-secrets-or-tokens-generated-under-a-given-prefix-immediately-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|prefix|path|string|true|The path to revoke keys under. Example: "prod/aws/ops"|

<h3 id="revokes-all-secrets-or-tokens-generated-under-a-given-prefix-immediately-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Enable a new secrets engine at the given path.

<a id="opIdmounts-enable-secrets-engine"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/mounts/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "config": {},
    "description": "string",
    "external_entropy_access": false,
    "local": false,
    "options": {},
    "plugin_name": "string",
    "plugin_version": "string",
    "seal_wrap": false,
    "type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sys/mounts/{path}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "config": {},
  "description": "string",
  "external_entropy_access": false,
  "local": false,
  "options": {},
  "plugin_name": "string",
  "plugin_version": "string",
  "seal_wrap": false,
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="enable-a-new-secrets-engine-at-the-given-path-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|path|string|true|The path to mount to. Example: "aws/east"|
|body|body|[MountsEnableSecretsEngineRequest](#schemamountsenablesecretsenginerequest)|true|none|
|» config|body|object(map)|false|Configuration for this mount, such as default_lease_ttl and max_lease_ttl.|
|» description|body|string|false|User-friendly description for this mount.|
|» external_entropy_access|body|boolean|false|Whether to give the mount access to Vault's external entropy.|
|» local|body|boolean|false|Mark the mount as a local mount, which is not replicated and is unaffected by replication.|
|» options|body|object(kvpairs)|false|The options to pass into the backend. Should be a json object with string keys and values.|
|» plugin_name|body|string|false|Name of the plugin to mount based from the name registered in the plugin catalog.|
|» plugin_version|body|string|false|The semantic version of the plugin to use, or image tag if oci_image is provided.|
|» seal_wrap|body|boolean|false|Whether to turn on seal wrapping for the mount.|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of the backend. Example: "passthrough"|

<h3 id="enable-a-new-secrets-engine-at-the-given-path-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<a id="opIdmounts-tune-configuration-parameters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/mounts/string/tune \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "allowed_managed_keys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "allowed_response_headers": [
      "string"
    ],
    "audit_non_hmac_request_keys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "audit_non_hmac_response_keys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "default_lease_ttl": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "listing_visibility": "string",
    "max_lease_ttl": "string",
    "options": {},
    "passthrough_request_headers": [
      "string"
    ],
    "plugin_version": "string",
    "token_type": "string",
    "user_lockout_config": {}
  }'
```

`POST /sys/mounts/{path}/tune`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowed_managed_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_response_headers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "audit_non_hmac_request_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "audit_non_hmac_response_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "default_lease_ttl": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "listing_visibility": "string",
  "max_lease_ttl": "string",
  "options": {},
  "passthrough_request_headers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "plugin_version": "string",
  "token_type": "string",
  "user_lockout_config": {}
}
```

<h3 id="mounts-tune-configuration-parameters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|path|string|true|The path to mount to. Example: "aws/east"|
|body|body|[MountsTuneConfigurationParametersRequest](#schemamountstuneconfigurationparametersrequest)|true|none|
|» allowed_managed_keys|body|[string]|false|none|
|» allowed_response_headers|body|[string]|false|A list of headers to whitelist and allow a plugin to set on responses.|
|» audit_non_hmac_request_keys|body|[string]|false|The list of keys in the request data object that will not be HMAC'ed by audit devices.|
|» audit_non_hmac_response_keys|body|[string]|false|The list of keys in the response data object that will not be HMAC'ed by audit devices.|
|» default_lease_ttl|body|string|false|The default lease TTL for this mount.|
|» description|body|string|false|User-friendly description for this credential backend.|
|» listing_visibility|body|string|false|Determines the visibility of the mount in the UI-specific listing endpoint. Accepted value are 'unauth' and 'hidden', with the empty default ('') behaving like 'hidden'.|
|» max_lease_ttl|body|string|false|The max lease TTL for this mount.|
|» options|body|object(kvpairs)|false|The options to pass into the backend. Should be a json object with string keys and values.|
|» passthrough_request_headers|body|[string]|false|A list of headers to whitelist and pass from the request to the plugin.|
|» plugin_version|body|string|false|The semantic version of the plugin to use, or image tag if oci_image is provided.|
|» token_type|body|string|false|The type of token to issue (service or batch).|
|» user_lockout_config|body|object(map)|false|The user lockout configuration to pass into the backend. Should be a json object with string keys and values.|

<h3 id="mounts-tune-configuration-parameters-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
    "args": [
      "string"
    ],
    "command": "string",
```

```bash
      "string"
    ],

  }'
```

```json
{
  "args": [
    "string"
  ],
  "command": "string",
  "env": [
    "string"
  ],
  "oci_image": "string",
  "sha256": "string",
  "version": "string"
}
```

|body|body|[PluginsCatalogRegisterPluginRequest](#schemapluginscatalogregisterpluginrequest)|true|none|
|» args|body|[string]|false|The args passed to plugin command.|
