## Reload mounted plugin backends.

<a id="opIdplugins-reload-backends"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/plugins/reload/backend \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "mounts": [
      "string"
    ],
    "plugin": "string",
    "scope": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sys/plugins/reload/backend`

Either the plugin name (`plugin`) or the desired plugin backend mounts (`mounts`) must be provided, but not both. In the case that the plugin name is provided, all mounted paths that use that plugin backend will be reloaded.  If (`scope`) is provided and is (`global`), the plugin(s) are reloaded globally.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mounts": [
    "string"
  ],
  "plugin": "string",
  "scope": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="reload-mounted-plugin-backends-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PluginsReloadBackendsRequest](#schemapluginsreloadbackendsrequest)|true|none|
|» mounts|body|[string]|false|The mount paths of the plugin backends to reload.|
|» plugin|body|string|false|The name of the plugin to reload, as registered in the plugin catalog.|
|» scope|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "reload_id": "string"
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "reload_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="reload-mounted-plugin-backends-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[PluginsReloadBackendsResponse](#schemapluginsreloadbackendsresponse)|
|202|Accepted|OK|[PluginsReloadBackendsResponse](#schemapluginsreloadbackendsresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## rate-limit-quotas-write

<a id="opIdrate-limit-quotas-write"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/quotas/rate-limit/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "block_interval": "string",
    "inheritable": true,
    "interval": "string",
    "path": "string",
    "rate": 0,
    "role": "string",
    "type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sys/quotas/rate-limit/{name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "block_interval": "string",
  "inheritable": true,
  "interval": "string",
  "path": "string",
  "rate": 0,
  "role": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="rate-limit-quotas-write-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the quota rule.|
|body|body|[RateLimitQuotasWriteRequest](#schemaratelimitquotaswriterequest)|true|none|
|» block_interval|body|string(duration)|false|If set, when a client reaches a rate limit threshold, the client will be prohibited from any further requests until after the 'block_interval' has elapsed.|
|» inheritable|body|boolean|false|Whether all child namespaces can inherit this namespace quota.|
|» interval|body|string(duration)|false|The duration to enforce rate limiting for (default '1s').|
|» path|body|string|false|Path of the mount or namespace to apply the quota. A blank path configures a global quota. For example namespace1/ adds a quota to a full namespace, namespace1/auth/userpass adds a quota to userpass in namespace1.|
|» rate|body|number(float)|false|The maximum number of requests in a given interval to be allowed by the quota rule. The 'rate' must be positive.|
|» role|body|string|false|Login role to apply this quota to. Note that when set, path must be configured to a valid auth method with a concept of roles.|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the quota rule.|

<h3 id="rate-limit-quotas-write-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Initializes a new rekey attempt.

<a id="opIdrekey-attempt-initialize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/rekey/init \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "backup": true,
    "pgp_keys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "require_verification": true,
    "secret_shares": 0,
    "secret_threshold": 0
  }'
```

`POST /sys/rekey/init`

Only a single rekey attempt can take place at a time, and changing the parameters of a rekey requires canceling and starting a new rekey, which will also provide a new nonce.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "backup": true,
  "pgp_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "require_verification": true,
  "secret_shares": 0,
  "secret_threshold": 0
}
```

<h3 id="initializes-a-new-rekey-attempt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RekeyAttemptInitializeRequest](#schemarekeyattemptinitializerequest)|true|none|
|» backup|body|boolean|false|Specifies if using PGP-encrypted keys, whether Vault should also store a plaintext backup of the PGP-encrypted keys.|
|» pgp_keys|body|[string]|false|Specifies an array of PGP public keys used to encrypt the output unseal keys. Ordering is preserved. The keys must be base64-encoded from their original binary representation. The size of this array must be the same as secret_shares.|
|» require_verification|body|boolean|false|Turns on verification functionality|
|» secret_shares|body|integer|false|Specifies the number of shares to split the unseal key into.|
|» secret_threshold|body|integer|false|Specifies the number of shares required to reconstruct the unseal key. This must be less than or equal secret_shares. If using Vault HSM with auto-unsealing, this value must be the same as secret_shares.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "backup": true,
  "n": 0,
  "nounce": "string",
  "pgp_fingerprints": [
    "string"
  ],
  "progress": 0,
  "required": 0,
  "started": "string",
  "t": 0,
  "verification_nonce": "string",
  "verification_required": true
}
```

<h3 id="initializes-a-new-rekey-attempt-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[RekeyAttemptInitializeResponse](#schemarekeyattemptinitializeresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Cancels any in-progress rekey.

<a id="opIdrekey-attempt-cancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/rekey/init \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /sys/rekey/init`

This clears the rekey settings as well as any progress made. This must be called to change the parameters of the rekey. Note: verification is still a part of a rekey. If rekeying is canceled during the verification flow, the current unseal keys remain valid.

<h3 id="cancels-any-in-progress-rekey-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

> Code samples

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /sys/rekey/verify`

```bash
  -d '{
```

```bash
    "lease_id": "string"
  }'
```

## Revokes all secrets or tokens generated under a given prefix immediately

<a id="opIdleases-force-revoke-lease-with-prefix2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/revoke-force/string \
  -X POST
```

`POST /sys/revoke-force/{prefix}`

Unlike `/sys/leases/revoke-prefix`, this path ignores backend errors encountered during revocation. This is potentially very dangerous and should only be used in specific emergency situations where errors in the backend or the connected backend service prevent normal revocation.

By ignoring these errors, Vault abdicates responsibility for ensuring that the issued credentials or secrets are properly revoked and/or cleaned up. Access to this endpoint should be tightly controlled.

<h3 id="revokes-all-secrets-or-tokens-generated-under-a-given-prefix-immediately-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|prefix|path|string|true|The path to revoke keys under. Example: "prod/aws/ops"|

<h3 id="revokes-all-secrets-or-tokens-generated-under-a-given-prefix-immediately-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Cause the node to give up active status.

<a id="opIdstep-down-leader"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/step-down \
  -X POST
```

`POST /sys/step-down`

This endpoint forces the node to give up active status. If the node does not have active status, this endpoint does nothing. Note that the node will sleep for ten seconds before attempting to grab the active lock again, but if no standby nodes grab the active lock in the interim, the same node may become the active node again.

<h3 id="cause-the-node-to-give-up-active-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|empty body|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identity_request_headers|string|false|none|The request headers. This must include the headers over which AliCloud has included a signature.|
|identity_request_url|string|false|none|Base64-encoded full URL against which to make the AliCloud request.|

<h2 id="tocS_AliCloudWriteAuthRoleRequest">AliCloudWriteAuthRoleRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaalicloudwriteauthrolerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_AliCloudWriteAuthRoleRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSalicloudwriteauthrolerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsalicloudwriteauthrolerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "arn": "string",
  "bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "period": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|arn|string|false|none|ARN of the RAM to bind to this role.|
|bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_bound_cidrs" instead. If this and "token_bound_cidrs" are both specified, only "token_bound_cidrs" will be used.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|period|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|policies|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

```json
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum allowed lifetime of tokens issued using this role.|
|remote_policies|[string]|false|none|The name and type of each remote policy to be applied. Example: "name:AliyunRDSReadOnlyAccess,type:System".|
|role_arn|string|false|none|ARN of the role to be assumed. If provided, inline_policies and remote_policies should be blank. At creation time, this role must have configured trusted actors, and the access key and secret that will be used to assume the role (in /config) must qualify as a trusted actor.|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|Duration in seconds after which the issued token should expire. Defaults to 0, in which case the value will fallback to the system/mount defaults.|

|aws_public_cert|string|false|none|Base64 encoded AWS Public cert required to verify PKCS7 signature of the EC2 instance metadata.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ec2_alias|string|false|none|Configure how the AWS auth method generates entity alias when using EC2 auth. Valid values are "role_id", "instance_id", and "image_id". Defaults to "role_id".|
|ec2_metadata|[string]|false|none|The metadata to include on the aliases and audit logs generated by this plugin. When set to 'default', includes: account_id, auth_type. These fields are available to add: ami_id, instance_id, region. Not editing this field means the 'default' fields are included. Explicitly setting this field to empty overrides the 'default' and means no metadata will be included. If not using 'default', explicit fields must be sent like: 'field1,field2'.|
|iam_alias|string|false|none|Configure how the AWS auth method generates entity aliases when using IAM auth. Valid values are "role_id", "unique_id", and "full_arn". Defaults to "role_id".|
|iam_metadata|[string]|false|none|The metadata to include on the aliases and audit logs generated by this plugin. When set to 'default', includes: account_id, auth_type. These fields are available to add: canonical_arn, client_arn, client_user_id, inferred_aws_region, inferred_entity_id, inferred_entity_type. Not editing this field means the 'default' fields are included. Explicitly setting this field to empty overrides the 'default' and means no metadata will be included. If not using 'default', explicit fields must be sent like: 'field1,field2'.|

```json
  "pkcs7": "string",
  "role": "string",
  "signature": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|iam_http_request_method|string|false|none|HTTP method to use for the AWS request when auth_type is iam. This must match what has been signed in the presigned request.|
|iam_request_body|string|false|none|Base64-encoded request body when auth_type is iam. This must match the request body included in the signature.|
|iam_request_headers|string|false|none|Key/value pairs of headers for use in the sts:GetCallerIdentity HTTP requests headers when auth_type is iam. Can be either a Base64-encoded, JSON-serialized string, or a JSON object of key/value pairs. This must at a minimum include the headers over which AWS has included a signature.|
|iam_request_url|string|false|none|Base64-encoded full URL against which to make the AWS request when using iam auth_type.|
|identity|string|false|none|Base64 encoded EC2 instance identity document. This needs to be supplied along with the 'signature' parameter. If using 'curl' for fetching the identity document, consider using the option '-w 0' while piping the output to 'base64' binary.|
|nonce|string|false|none|The nonce to be used for subsequent login requests when auth_type is ec2. If this parameter is not specified at all and if reauthentication is allowed, then the backend will generate a random nonce, attaches it to the instance's identity access list entry and returns the nonce back as part of auth metadata. This value should be used with further login requests, to establish client authenticity. Clients can choose to set a custom nonce if preferred, in which case, it is recommended that clients provide a strong nonce. If a nonce is provided but with an empty value, it indicates intent to disable reauthentication. Note that, when 'disallow_reauthentication' option is enabled on either the role or the role tag, the 'nonce' holds no significance.|
|pkcs7|string|false|none|PKCS7 signature of the identity document when using an auth_type of ec2.|
|role|string|false|none|Name of the role against which the login is being attempted. If 'role' is not specified, then the login endpoint looks for a role bearing the name of the AMI ID of the EC2 instance that is trying to login. If a matching role is not found, login fails.|
|signature|string|false|none|Base64 encoded SHA256 RSA signature of the instance identity document. This needs to be supplied along with 'identity' parameter.|

```json
{
  "allow_instance_migration": false,
  "auth_type": "string",
  "bound_account_id": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_ami_id": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_ec2_instance_id": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_iam_instance_profile_arn": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_iam_principal_arn": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_iam_role_arn": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_region": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_subnet_id": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_vpc_id": [
    "string"
  ],
  "disallow_reauthentication": false,
  "inferred_aws_region": "string",
  "inferred_entity_type": "string",
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "period": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "resolve_aws_unique_ids": true,
  "role_tag": "",
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_instance_migration|boolean|false|none|If set, allows migration of the underlying instance where the client resides. This keys off of pendingTime in the metadata document, so essentially, this disables the client nonce check whenever the instance is migrated to a new host and pendingTime is newer than the previously-remembered time. Use with caution. This is only checked when auth_type is ec2.|
|auth_type|string|false|none|The auth_type permitted to authenticate to this role. Must be one of iam or ec2 and cannot be changed after role creation.|
|bound_account_id|[string]|false|none|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances that the account ID in its identity document to match one of the IDs specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|bound_ami_id|[string]|false|none|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances that they should be using one of the AMI IDs specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|bound_ec2_instance_id|[string]|false|none|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances to have one of the given instance IDs. Can be a list or comma-separated string of EC2 instance IDs. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|bound_iam_instance_profile_arn|[string]|false|none|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances to be associated with an IAM instance profile ARN which has a prefix that matches one of the values specified by this parameter. The value is prefix-matched (as though it were a glob ending in '*'). This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|bound_iam_principal_arn|[string]|false|none|ARN of the IAM principals to bind to this role. Only applicable when auth_type is iam.|
|bound_iam_role_arn|[string]|false|none|If set, defines a constraint on the authenticating EC2 instance that it must match one of the IAM role ARNs specified by this parameter. The value is prefix-matched (as though it were a glob ending in '*'). The configured IAM user or EC2 instance role must be allowed to execute the 'iam:GetInstanceProfile' action if this is specified. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|bound_region|[string]|false|none|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instances that the region in its identity document match one of the regions specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2.|
|bound_subnet_id|[string]|false|none|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instance to be associated with the subnet ID that matches one of the values specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|bound_vpc_id|[string]|false|none|If set, defines a constraint on the EC2 instance to be associated with a VPC ID that matches one of the value specified by this parameter. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2 or inferred_entity_type is ec2_instance.|
|disallow_reauthentication|boolean|false|none|If set, only allows a single token to be granted per instance ID. In order to perform a fresh login, the entry in the access list for the instance ID needs to be cleared using 'auth/aws-ec2/identity-accesslist/<instance_id>' endpoint. This is only applicable when auth_type is ec2.|
|inferred_aws_region|string|false|none|When auth_type is iam and inferred_entity_type is set, the region to assume the inferred entity exists in.|
|inferred_entity_type|string|false|none|When auth_type is iam, the AWS entity type to infer from the authenticated principal. The only supported value is ec2_instance, which will extract the EC2 instance ID from the authenticated role and apply the following restrictions specific to EC2 instances: bound_ami_id, bound_account_id, bound_iam_role_arn, bound_iam_instance_profile_arn, bound_vpc_id, bound_subnet_id. The configured EC2 client must be able to find the inferred instance ID in the results, and the instance must be running. If unable to determine the EC2 instance ID or unable to find the EC2 instance ID among running instances, then authentication will fail.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|period|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|policies|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|resolve_aws_unique_ids|boolean|false|none|If set, resolve all AWS IAM ARNs into AWS's internal unique IDs. When an IAM entity (e.g., user, role, or instance profile) is deleted, then all references to it within the role will be invalidated, which prevents a new IAM entity from being created with the same name and matching the role's IAM binds. Once set, this cannot be unset.|
|role_tag|string|false|none|If set, enables the role tags for this role. The value set for this field should be the 'key' of the tag on the EC2 instance. The 'value' of the tag should be generated using 'role/<role>/tag' endpoint. Defaults to an empty string, meaning that role tags are disabled. This is only allowed if auth_type is ec2.|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

For a credential type of assumed_role or federation_token, the policies sent to the corresponding AWS call (sts:AssumeRole or sts:GetFederation) will be the policies from each group in iam_groups combined with the policy_document and policy_arns parameters.|
|iam_tags|object(kvpairs)|false|none|IAM tags to be set for any users created by this role. These must be presented as Key-Value pairs. This can be represented as a map or a list of equal sign delimited key pairs.|
|max_sts_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|Max allowed TTL for assumed_role and federation_token credential types|

|policy_arns|[string]|false|none|ARNs of AWS policies. Behavior varies by credential_type. When credential_type is iam_user, then it will attach the specified policies to the generated IAM user. When credential_type is assumed_role or federation_token, the policies will be passed as the PolicyArns parameter, acting as a filter on permissions available.|
|policy_document|string|false|none|JSON-encoded IAM policy document. Behavior varies by credential_type. When credential_type is iam_user, then it will attach the contents of the policy_document to the IAM user generated. When credential_type is assumed_role or federation_token, this will be passed in as the Policy parameter to the AssumeRole or GetFederationToken API call, acting as a filter on permissions available.|
|role_arns|[string]|false|none|ARNs of AWS roles allowed to be assumed. Only valid when credential_type is assumed_role|
|user_path|string|false|none|Path for IAM User. Only valid when credential_type is iam_user|

<a id="schemaazureloginrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_AzureLoginRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSazureloginrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsazureloginrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "jwt": "string",
  "resource_group_name": "string",
  "resource_id": "string",
  "role": "string",
  "subscription_id": "string",
  "vm_name": "string",
  "vmss_name": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|jwt|string|false|none|A signed JWT|
|resource_group_name|string|false|none|The resource group from the instance.|
|resource_id|string|false|none|The fully qualified ID of the resource, includingthe resource name and resource type. Use the format, /subscriptions/{guid}/resourceGroups/{resource-group-name}/{resource-provider-namespace}/{resource-type}/{resource-name}. This value is ignored if vm_name or vmss_name is specified.|
|role|string|false|none|The token role.|
|subscription_id|string|false|none|The subscription id for the instance.|
|vm_name|string|false|none|The name of the virtual machine. This value is ignored if vmss_name is specified.|
|vmss_name|string|false|none|The name of the virtual machine scale set the instance is in.|

<h2 id="tocS_AzureWriteAuthRoleRequest">AzureWriteAuthRoleRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaazurewriteauthrolerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_AzureWriteAuthRoleRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSazurewriteauthrolerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsazurewriteauthrolerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "bound_group_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_locations": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_resource_groups": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_scale_sets": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_service_principal_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_subscription_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "num_uses": 0,
  "period": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bound_group_ids|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of group ids that login is restricted to.|
|bound_locations|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of locations that login is restricted to.|
|bound_resource_groups|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of resource groups that login is restricted to.|
|bound_scale_sets|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of scale sets that login is restricted to.|
|bound_service_principal_ids|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of service principal ids that login is restricted to.|
|bound_subscription_ids|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of subscription ids that login is restricted to.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|num_uses|integer|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_num_uses" instead. If this and "token_num_uses" are both specified, only "token_num_uses" will be used.|
|period|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|policies|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

<h2 id="tocS_AzureWriteRoleRequest">AzureWriteRoleRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaazurewriterolerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_AzureWriteRoleRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSazurewriterolerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsazurewriterolerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "application_object_id": "string",
  "azure_groups": "string",
  "azure_roles": "string",
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "permanently_delete": false,
  "persist_app": false,
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application_object_id|string|false|none|Application Object ID to use for static service principal credentials.|
|azure_groups|string|false|none|JSON list of Azure groups to add the service principal to.|
|azure_roles|string|false|none|JSON list of Azure roles to assign.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|Maximum time a service principal. If not set or set to 0, will use system default.|
|permanently_delete|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether new application objects should be permanently deleted. If not set, objects will not be permanently deleted.|
|persist_app|boolean|false|none|Persist the app between generated credentials. Useful if the app needs to maintain owner ship of resources it creates|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|Default lease for generated credentials. If not set or set to 0, will use system default.|

|policies|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|scope|string|false|none|OAuth2 App Scope|
|service_url|string|false|none|Service URL (https://<tenant>.my.centrify.com)|

<h2 id="tocS_CertConfigureRequest">CertConfigureRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacertconfigurerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CertConfigureRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScertconfigurerequest"></a>
<a id="tocscertconfigurerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "disable_binding": false,
  "enable_identity_alias_metadata": false,
  "ocsp_cache_size": 100
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|disable_binding|boolean|false|none|If set, during renewal, skips the matching of presented client identity with the client identity used during login. Defaults to false.|
|enable_identity_alias_metadata|boolean|false|none|If set, metadata of the certificate including the metadata corresponding to allowed_metadata_extensions will be stored in the alias. Defaults to false.|
|ocsp_cache_size|integer|false|none|The size of the in memory OCSP response cache, shared by all configured certs|

<h2 id="tocS_CertWriteCertificateRequest">CertWriteCertificateRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacertwritecertificaterequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CertWriteCertificateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScertwritecertificaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocscertwritecertificaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "allowed_common_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_dns_sans": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_email_sans": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_metadata_extensions": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_organizational_units": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_uri_sans": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "certificate": "string",
  "display_name": "string",
  "lease": 0,
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "ocsp_ca_certificates": "string",
  "ocsp_enabled": true,
  "ocsp_fail_open": false,
  "ocsp_query_all_servers": false,
  "ocsp_servers_override": [
    "string"
  ],
  "period": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "required_extensions": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_common_names|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated list of names. At least one must exist in the Common Name. Supports globbing.|
|allowed_dns_sans|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated list of DNS names. At least one must exist in the SANs. Supports globbing.|
|allowed_email_sans|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated list of Email Addresses. At least one must exist in the SANs. Supports globbing.|
|allowed_metadata_extensions|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or array of oid extensions. Upon successful authentication, these extensions will be added as metadata if they are present in the certificate. The metadata key will be the string consisting of the oid numbers separated by a dash (-) instead of a dot (.) to allow usage in ACL templates.|
|allowed_names|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated list of names. At least one must exist in either the Common Name or SANs. Supports globbing. This parameter is deprecated, please use allowed_common_names, allowed_dns_sans, allowed_email_sans, allowed_uri_sans.|
|allowed_organizational_units|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated list of Organizational Units names. At least one must exist in the OU field.|
|allowed_uri_sans|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated list of URIs. At least one must exist in the SANs. Supports globbing.|
|bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_bound_cidrs" instead. If this and "token_bound_cidrs" are both specified, only "token_bound_cidrs" will be used.|
|certificate|string|false|none|The public certificate that should be trusted. Must be x509 PEM encoded.|
|display_name|string|false|none|The display name to use for clients using this certificate.|
|lease|integer|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|ocsp_ca_certificates|string|false|none|Any additional CA certificates needed to communicate with OCSP servers|
|ocsp_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to attempt OCSP verification of certificates at login|
|ocsp_fail_open|boolean|false|none|If set to true, if an OCSP revocation cannot be made successfully, login will proceed rather than failing. If false, failing to get an OCSP status fails the request.|
|ocsp_query_all_servers|boolean|false|none|If set to true, rather than accepting the first successful OCSP response, query all servers and consider the certificate valid only if all servers agree.|
|ocsp_servers_override|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated list of OCSP server addresses. If unset, the OCSP server is determined from the AuthorityInformationAccess extension on the certificate being inspected.|
|period|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|policies|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|required_extensions|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or array of extensions formatted as "oid:value". Expects the extension value to be some type of ASN1 encoded string. All values much match. Supports globbing on "value".|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

```json

  "crl": "string",
  "url": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|crl|string|false|none|The public CRL that should be trusted to attest to certificates' validity statuses. May be DER or PEM encoded. Note: the expiration time is ignored; if the CRL is no longer valid, delete it using the same name as specified here.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL of a CRL distribution point. Only one of 'crl' or 'url' parameters should be specified.|

<h2 id="tocS_CloudFoundryConfigureRequest">CloudFoundryConfigureRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacloudfoundryconfigurerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CloudFoundryConfigureRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScloudfoundryconfigurerequest"></a>
<a id="tocscloudfoundryconfigurerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "cf_api_addr": "string",
  "cf_api_mutual_tls_certificate": "string",
  "cf_api_mutual_tls_key": "string",
  "cf_api_trusted_certificates": [
    "string"
  ],
  "cf_client_id": "string",
  "cf_client_secret": "string",
  "cf_password": "string",
  "cf_username": "string",
  "identity_ca_certificates": [
    "string"
  ],
  "login_max_seconds_not_after": 60,
  "login_max_seconds_not_before": 300,
  "pcf_api_addr": "string",
  "pcf_api_trusted_certificates": [
    "string"
  ],
  "pcf_password": "string",
  "pcf_username": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cf_api_addr|string|false|none|CF’s API address.|
|cf_api_mutual_tls_certificate|string|false|none|The PEM-format certificates that are presented for mutual TLS with the CloudFoundry API. If not set, mutual TLS is not used|
|cf_api_mutual_tls_key|string|false|none|The PEM-format private key that are used for mutual TLS with the CloudFoundry API. If not set, mutual TLS is not used|
|cf_api_trusted_certificates|[string]|false|none|The PEM-format CA certificates that are acceptable for the CF API to present.|
|cf_client_id|string|false|none|The client id for CF’s API.|
|cf_client_secret|string|false|none|The client secret for CF’s API.|
|cf_password|string|false|none|The password for CF’s API.|
|cf_username|string|false|none|The username for CF’s API.|
|identity_ca_certificates|[string]|false|none|The PEM-format CA certificates that are required to have issued the instance certificates presented for logging in.|
|login_max_seconds_not_after|integer|false|none|Duration in seconds for the maximum acceptable length in the future a "signing_time" can be. Useful for clock drift. Set low to reduce the opportunity for replay attacks.|
|login_max_seconds_not_before|string(duration)|false|none|Duration in seconds for the maximum acceptable age of a "signing_time". Useful for clock drift. Set low to reduce the opportunity for replay attacks.|
|pcf_api_addr|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Please use "cf_api_addr".|
|pcf_api_trusted_certificates|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Please use "cf_api_trusted_certificates".|
|pcf_password|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Please use "cf_password".|
|pcf_username|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Please use "cf_username".|

<h2 id="tocS_ConsulWriteRoleRequest">ConsulWriteRoleRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconsulwriterolerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_ConsulWriteRoleRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSconsulwriterolerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsconsulwriterolerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "consul_namespace": "string",
  "consul_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "consul_roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "lease": "string",
  "local": true,
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "node_identities": [
    "string"
  ],
  "partition": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "policy": "string",
  "service_identities": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_type": "client",
  "ttl": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consul_namespace|string|false|none|Indicates which namespace that the token will be created within. Defaults to 'default'. Available in Consul 1.7 and above.|
|consul_policies|[string]|false|none|List of policies to attach to the token. Either "consul_policies" or "consul_roles" are required for Consul 1.5 and above, or just "consul_policies" if using Consul 1.4.|
|consul_roles|[string]|false|none|List of Consul roles to attach to the token. Either "policies" or "consul_roles" are required for Consul 1.5 and above.|
|lease|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "ttl" instead.|
|local|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the token should not be replicated globally and instead be local to the current datacenter. Available in Consul 1.4 and above.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|Max TTL for the Consul token created from the role.|
|node_identities|[string]|false|none|List of Node Identities to attach to the token. Available in Consul 1.8.1 or above.|
|partition|string|false|none|Indicates which admin partition that the token will be created within. Defaults to 'default'. Available in Consul 1.11 and above.|
|policies|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "consul_policies" instead.|
|policy|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Policy document, base64 encoded. Required for 'client' tokens. Required for Consul pre-1.4.|
|service_identities|[string]|false|none|List of Service Identities to attach to the token, separated by semicolons. Available in Consul 1.5 or above.|
|token_type|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Which type of token to create: 'client' or 'management'. If a 'management' token, the "policy", "policies", and "consul_roles" parameters are not required. Defaults to 'client'.|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|TTL for the Consul token created from the role.|

```json
  ],
```

```json
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|creation_statements|[string]|false|none|Specifies the database statements executed to create and configure a user. See the plugin's API page for more information on support and formatting for this parameter.|
|credential_config|object(kvpairs)|false|none|The configuration for the given credential_type.|
|credential_type|string|false|none|The type of credential to manage. Options include: 'password', 'rsa_private_key'. Defaults to 'password'.|
|db_name|string|false|none|Name of the database this role acts on.|
|default_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|Default ttl for role.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|Maximum time a credential is valid for|
|renew_statements|[string]|false|none|Specifies the database statements to be executed to renew a user. Not every plugin type will support this functionality. See the plugin's API page for more information on support and formatting for this parameter.|
|revocation_statements|[string]|false|none|Specifies the database statements to be executed to revoke a user. See the plugin's API page for more information on support and formatting for this parameter.|
|rollback_statements|[string]|false|none|Specifies the database statements to be executed rollback a create operation in the event of an error. Not every plugin type will support this functionality. See the plugin's API page for more information on support and formatting for this parameter.|

```json
  ],
```

```json
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|base_url|string|false|none|The API endpoint to use. Useful if you are running GitHub Enterprise or an API-compatible authentication server.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|organization|string|true|none|The organization users must be part of|
|organization_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the organization users must be part of|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any policies configured for specific users/groups.|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|

<h2 id="tocS_GoogleCloudKmsWriteKeyRequest">GoogleCloudKmsWriteKeyRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemagooglecloudkmswritekeyrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_GoogleCloudKmsWriteKeyRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSgooglecloudkmswritekeyrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsgooglecloudkmswritekeyrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "algorithm": "string",
  "crypto_key": "string",
  "key_ring": "string",
  "labels": {},
  "protection_level": "string",
  "purpose": "string",
  "rotation_period": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|algorithm|string|false|none|Algorithm to use for encryption, decryption, or signing. The value depends on the key purpose. The value cannot be changed after creation. For a key purpose of "encrypt_decrypt", the valid values are: - symmetric_encryption (default) For a key purpose of "asymmetric_sign", valid values are: - rsa_sign_pss_2048_sha256 - rsa_sign_pss_3072_sha256 - rsa_sign_pss_4096_sha256 - rsa_sign_pkcs1_2048_sha256 - rsa_sign_pkcs1_3072_sha256 - rsa_sign_pkcs1_4096_sha256 - ec_sign_p256_sha256 - ec_sign_p384_sha384 For a key purpose of "asymmetric_decrypt", valid values are: - rsa_decrypt_oaep_2048_sha256 - rsa_decrypt_oaep_3072_sha256 - rsa_decrypt_oaep_4096_sha256|
|crypto_key|string|false|none|Name of the crypto key to use. If the given crypto key does not exist, Vault will try to create it. This defaults to the name of the key given to Vault as the parameter if unspecified.|
|key_ring|string|false|none|Full Google Cloud resource ID of the key ring with the project and location (e.g. projects/my-project/locations/global/keyRings/my-keyring). If the given key ring does not exist, Vault will try to create it during a create operation.|
|labels|object(kvpairs)|false|none|Arbitrary key=value label to apply to the crypto key. To specify multiple labels, specify this argument multiple times (e.g. labels="a=b" labels="c=d").|
|protection_level|string|false|none|Level of protection to use for the key management. Valid values are "software" and "hsm". The default value is "software". The value cannot be changed after creation.|
|purpose|string|false|none|Purpose of the key. Valid options are "asymmetric_decrypt", "asymmetric_sign", and "encrypt_decrypt". The default value is "encrypt_decrypt". The value cannot be changed after creation.|
|rotation_period|string(duration)|false|none|Amount of time between crypto key version rotations. This is specified as a time duration value like 72h (72 hours). The smallest possible value is 24h. This value only applies to keys with a purpose of "encrypt_decrypt".|

<a id="tocSgooglecloudwriterolerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsgooglecloudwriterolerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "add_group_aliases": false,
  "allow_gce_inference": true,
  "bound_instance_group": "string",
  "bound_instance_groups": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_labels": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_region": "string",
  "bound_regions": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_service_accounts": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bound_zone": "string",
  "bound_zones": [
    "string"
  ],
  "max_jwt_exp": 900,
  "max_ttl": "string",
  "period": "string",
  "policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "project_id": "string",
  "service_accounts": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "ttl": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|add_group_aliases|boolean|false|none|If true, will add group aliases to auth tokens generated under this role. This will add the full list of ancestors (projects, folders, organizations) for the given entity's project. Requires IAM permission `resourcemanager.projects.get` on this project.|
|allow_gce_inference|boolean|false|none|'iam' roles only. If false, Vault will not not allow GCE instances to login in against this role|
|bound_instance_group|string|false|none|Deprecated: use "bound_instance_groups" instead.|
|bound_instance_groups|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of permitted instance groups to which the GCE instance must belong. This option only applies to "gce" roles.|
|bound_labels|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of GCP labels formatted as"key:value" strings that must be present on the GCE instance in order to authenticate. This option only applies to "gce" roles.|
|bound_projects|[string]|false|none|GCP Projects that authenticating entities must belong to.|
|bound_region|string|false|none|Deprecated: use "bound_regions" instead.|
|bound_regions|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of permitted regions to which the GCE instance must belong. If a group is provided, it is assumed to be a regional group. If "zone" is provided, this option is ignored. This can be a self-link or region name. This option only applies to "gce" roles.|
|bound_service_accounts|[string]|false|none|Can be set for both 'iam' and 'gce' roles (required for 'iam'). A comma-seperated list of authorized service accounts. If the single value "*" is given, this is assumed to be all service accounts under the role's project. If this is set on a GCE role, the inferred service account from the instance metadata token will be used.|
|bound_zone|string|false|none|Deprecated: use "bound_zones" instead.|
|bound_zones|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of permitted zones to which the GCE instance must belong. If a group is provided, it is assumed to be a zonal group. This can be a self-link or zone name. This option only applies to "gce" roles.|
|max_jwt_exp|string(duration)|false|none|Currently enabled for 'iam' only. Duration in seconds from time of validation that a JWT must expire within.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|period|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|policies|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|project_id|string|false|none|Deprecated: use "bound_projects" instead|
|service_accounts|[string]|false|none|Deprecated: use "bound_service_accounts" instead.|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|
|type|string|false|none|Type of the role. Currently supported: iam, gce|

<h2 id="tocS_InitializeRequest">InitializeRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainitializerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_InitializeRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSinitializerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsinitializerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "pgp_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "recovery_pgp_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "recovery_shares": 0,
  "recovery_threshold": 0,
  "root_token_pgp_key": "string",
  "secret_shares": 0,
  "secret_threshold": 0,
  "stored_shares": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pgp_keys|[string]|false|none|Specifies an array of PGP public keys used to encrypt the output unseal keys. Ordering is preserved. The keys must be base64-encoded from their original binary representation. The size of this array must be the same as `secret_shares`.|
|recovery_pgp_keys|[string]|false|none|Specifies an array of PGP public keys used to encrypt the output recovery keys. Ordering is preserved. The keys must be base64-encoded from their original binary representation. The size of this array must be the same as `recovery_shares`.|
|recovery_shares|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of shares to split the recovery key into.|
|recovery_threshold|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of shares required to reconstruct the recovery key. This must be less than or equal to `recovery_shares`.|
|root_token_pgp_key|string|false|none|Specifies a PGP public key used to encrypt the initial root token. The key must be base64-encoded from its original binary representation.|
|secret_shares|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of shares to split the unseal key into.|
|secret_threshold|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of shares required to reconstruct the unseal key. This must be less than or equal secret_shares. If using Vault HSM with auto-unsealing, this value must be the same as `secret_shares`.|
|stored_shares|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of shares that should be encrypted by the HSM and stored for auto-unsealing. Currently must be the same as `secret_shares`.|

<h2 id="tocS_JwtConfigureRequest">JwtConfigureRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajwtconfigurerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_JwtConfigureRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSjwtconfigurerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsjwtconfigurerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "bound_issuer": "string",
  "default_role": "string",
  "jwks_ca_pem": "string",
  "jwks_url": "string",
  "jwt_supported_algs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "jwt_validation_pubkeys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "namespace_in_state": true,
  "oidc_client_id": "string",
  "oidc_client_secret": "string",
  "oidc_discovery_ca_pem": "string",
  "oidc_discovery_url": "string",
  "oidc_response_mode": "string",
  "oidc_response_types": [
    "string"
  ],
  "provider_config": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bound_issuer|string|false|none|The value against which to match the 'iss' claim in a JWT. Optional.|
|default_role|string(lowercase)|false|none|The default role to use if none is provided during login. If not set, a role is required during login.|
|jwks_ca_pem|string|false|none|The CA certificate or chain of certificates, in PEM format, to use to validate connections to the JWKS URL. If not set, system certificates are used.|
|jwks_url|string|false|none|JWKS URL to use to authenticate signatures. Cannot be used with "oidc_discovery_url" or "jwt_validation_pubkeys".|
|jwt_supported_algs|[string]|false|none|A list of supported signing algorithms. Defaults to RS256.|
|jwt_validation_pubkeys|[string]|false|none|A list of PEM-encoded public keys to use to authenticate signatures locally. Cannot be used with "jwks_url" or "oidc_discovery_url".|
|namespace_in_state|boolean|false|none|Pass namespace in the OIDC state parameter instead of as a separate query parameter. With this setting, the allowed redirect URL(s) in Vault and on the provider side should not contain a namespace query parameter. This means only one redirect URL entry needs to be maintained on the provider side for all vault namespaces that will be authenticating against it. Defaults to true for new configs.|
|oidc_client_id|string|false|none|The OAuth Client ID configured with your OIDC provider.|
|oidc_client_secret|string|false|none|The OAuth Client Secret configured with your OIDC provider.|
|oidc_discovery_ca_pem|string|false|none|The CA certificate or chain of certificates, in PEM format, to use to validate connections to the OIDC Discovery URL. If not set, system certificates are used.|
|oidc_discovery_url|string|false|none|OIDC Discovery URL, without any .well-known component (base path). Cannot be used with "jwks_url" or "jwt_validation_pubkeys".|
|oidc_response_mode|string|false|none|The response mode to be used in the OAuth2 request. Allowed values are 'query' and 'form_post'.|
|oidc_response_types|[string]|false|none|The response types to request. Allowed values are 'code' and 'id_token'. Defaults to 'code'.|
|provider_config|object(map)|false|none|Provider-specific configuration. Optional.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_redirect_uris|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of allowed values for redirect_uri|
|bound_audiences|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of 'aud' claims that are valid for login; any match is sufficient|
|bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_bound_cidrs" instead. If this and "token_bound_cidrs" are both specified, only "token_bound_cidrs" will be used.|
|bound_claims|object(map)|false|none|Map of claims/values which must match for login|
|bound_claims_type|string|false|none|How to interpret values in the map of claims/values (which must match for login): allowed values are 'string' or 'glob'|
|bound_subject|string|false|none|The 'sub' claim that is valid for login. Optional.|
|claim_mappings|object(kvpairs)|false|none|Mappings of claims (key) that will be copied to a metadata field (value)|
|clock_skew_leeway|string(duration)|false|none|Duration in seconds of leeway when validating all claims to account for clock skew. Defaults to 60 (1 minute) if set to 0 and can be disabled if set to -1.|
|expiration_leeway|string(duration)|false|none|Duration in seconds of leeway when validating expiration of a token to account for clock skew. Defaults to 150 (2.5 minutes) if set to 0 and can be disabled if set to -1.|
|groups_claim|string|false|none|The claim to use for the Identity group alias names|
|max_age|string(duration)|false|none|Specifies the allowable elapsed time in seconds since the last time the user was actively authenticated.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_max_ttl" instead. If this and "token_max_ttl" are both specified, only "token_max_ttl" will be used.|
|not_before_leeway|string(duration)|false|none|Duration in seconds of leeway when validating not before values of a token to account for clock skew. Defaults to 150 (2.5 minutes) if set to 0 and can be disabled if set to -1.|
|num_uses|integer|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_num_uses" instead. If this and "token_num_uses" are both specified, only "token_num_uses" will be used.|
|oidc_scopes|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of OIDC scopes|
|period|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_period" instead. If this and "token_period" are both specified, only "token_period" will be used.|
|policies|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_policies" instead. If this and "token_policies" are both specified, only "token_policies" will be used.|
|role_type|string|false|none|Type of the role, either 'jwt' or 'oidc'.|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Use "token_ttl" instead. If this and "token_ttl" are both specified, only "token_ttl" will be used.|
|user_claim|string|false|none|The claim to use for the Identity entity alias name|
|user_claim_json_pointer|boolean|false|none|If true, the user_claim value will use JSON pointer syntax for referencing claims.|
|verbose_oidc_logging|boolean|false|none|Log received OIDC tokens and claims when debug-level logging is active. Not recommended in production since sensitive information may be present in OIDC responses.|

<h2 id="tocS_KerberosConfigureLdapRequest">KerberosConfigureLdapRequest</h2>

<a id="schema_KerberosConfigureLdapRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSkerberosconfigureldaprequest"></a>
<a id="tocskerberosconfigureldaprequest"></a>

```json
{
  "anonymous_group_search": false,
  "binddn": "string",
  "bindpass": "string",
  "case_sensitive_names": true,
  "certificate": "string",
  "client_tls_cert": "string",
  "client_tls_key": "string",
  "connection_timeout": "30s",
  "deny_null_bind": true,
  "dereference_aliases": "never",
  "discoverdn": true,
  "groupattr": "cn",
  "groupdn": "string",
  "groupfilter": "(|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))",
  "insecure_tls": true,
  "max_page_size": 0,
  "request_timeout": "90s",
  "starttls": true,
  "tls_max_version": "tls12",
  "tls_min_version": "tls12",
  "token_bound_cidrs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_explicit_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_max_ttl": "string",
  "token_no_default_policy": true,
  "token_num_uses": 0,
  "token_period": "string",
  "token_policies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "token_ttl": "string",
  "token_type": "default-service",
  "upndomain": "string",
  "url": "ldap://127.0.0.1",
  "use_pre111_group_cn_behavior": true,
  "use_token_groups": false,
  "userattr": "cn",
  "userdn": "string",
  "userfilter": "({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})",
  "username_as_alias": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|anonymous_group_search|boolean|false|none|Use anonymous binds when performing LDAP group searches (if true the initial credentials will still be used for the initial connection test).|
|binddn|string|false|none|LDAP DN for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|bindpass|string|false|none|LDAP password for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|case_sensitive_names|boolean|false|none|If true, case sensitivity will be used when comparing usernames and groups for matching policies.|
|certificate|string|false|none|CA certificate to use when verifying LDAP server certificate, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|client_tls_cert|string|false|none|Client certificate to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|client_tls_key|string|false|none|Client certificate key to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|connection_timeout|string(duration)|false|none|Timeout, in seconds, when attempting to connect to the LDAP server before trying the next URL in the configuration.|
|deny_null_bind|boolean|false|none|Denies an unauthenticated LDAP bind request if the user's password is empty; defaults to true|
|dereference_aliases|string|false|none|When aliases should be dereferenced on search operations. Accepted values are 'never', 'finding', 'searching', 'always'. Defaults to 'never'.|
|discoverdn|boolean|false|none|Use anonymous bind to discover the bind DN of a user (optional)|
|groupattr|string|false|none|LDAP attribute to follow on objects returned by <groupfilter> in order to enumerate user group membership. Examples: "cn" or "memberOf", etc. Default: cn|
|groupdn|string|false|none|LDAP search base to use for group membership search (eg: ou=Groups,dc=example,dc=org)|
|groupfilter|string|false|none|Go template for querying group membership of user (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserDN, Username Example: (&(objectClass=group)(member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:={{.UserDN}})) Default: (\|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))|
|insecure_tls|boolean|false|none|Skip LDAP server SSL Certificate verification - VERY insecure (optional)|
|max_page_size|integer|false|none|If set to a value greater than 0, the LDAP backend will use the LDAP server's paged search control to request pages of up to the given size. This can be used to avoid hitting the LDAP server's maximum result size limit. Otherwise, the LDAP backend will not use the paged search control.|
|request_timeout|string(duration)|false|none|Timeout, in seconds, for the connection when making requests against the server before returning back an error.|
|starttls|boolean|false|none|Issue a StartTLS command after establishing unencrypted connection (optional)|
|tls_max_version|string|false|none|Maximum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|tls_min_version|string|false|none|Minimum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any configured for specific users/groups.|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|upndomain|string|false|none|Enables userPrincipalDomain login with [username]@UPNDomain (optional)|
|url|string|false|none|LDAP URL to connect to (default: ldap://127.0.0.1). Multiple URLs can be specified by concatenating them with commas; they will be tried in-order.|
|use_pre111_group_cn_behavior|boolean|false|none|In Vault 1.1.1 a fix for handling group CN values of different cases unfortunately introduced a regression that could cause previously defined groups to not be found due to a change in the resulting name. If set true, the pre-1.1.1 behavior for matching group CNs will be used. This is only needed in some upgrade scenarios for backwards compatibility. It is enabled by default if the config is upgraded but disabled by default on new configurations.|
|use_token_groups|boolean|false|none|If true, use the Active Directory tokenGroups constructed attribute of the user to find the group memberships. This will find all security groups including nested ones.|
|userattr|string|false|none|Attribute used for users (default: cn)|
|userdn|string|false|none|LDAP domain to use for users (eg: ou=People,dc=example,dc=org)|
|userfilter|string|false|none|Go template for LDAP user search filer (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserAttr, Username Default: ({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})|
|username_as_alias|boolean|false|none|If true, sets the alias name to the username|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|dereference_aliases|never|
|dereference_aliases|finding|
|dereference_aliases|searching|
|dereference_aliases|always|
|tls_max_version|tls10|
|tls_max_version|tls11|
|tls_max_version|tls12|
|tls_max_version|tls13|
|tls_min_version|tls10|
|tls_min_version|tls11|
|tls_min_version|tls12|
|tls_min_version|tls13|

```json
    "string"
```
```json
  ],
```
```json
  "token_ttl": "string",
```

```json
  "use_pre111_group_cn_behavior": true,
  "use_token_groups": false,
  "userattr": "cn",
  "userdn": "string",
  "userfilter": "({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})",
  "username_as_alias": false
}
```
