### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|anonymous_group_search|boolean|false|none|Use anonymous binds when performing LDAP group searches (if true the initial credentials will still be used for the initial connection test).|
|binddn|string|false|none|LDAP DN for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|bindpass|string|false|none|LDAP password for searching for the user DN (optional)|
|case_sensitive_names|boolean|false|none|If true, case sensitivity will be used when comparing usernames and groups for matching policies.|
|certificate|string|false|none|CA certificate to use when verifying LDAP server certificate, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|client_tls_cert|string|false|none|Client certificate to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|client_tls_key|string|false|none|Client certificate key to provide to the LDAP server, must be x509 PEM encoded (optional)|
|connection_timeout|string(duration)|false|none|Timeout, in seconds, when attempting to connect to the LDAP server before trying the next URL in the configuration.|
|deny_null_bind|boolean|false|none|Denies an unauthenticated LDAP bind request if the user's password is empty; defaults to true|
|dereference_aliases|string|false|none|When aliases should be dereferenced on search operations. Accepted values are 'never', 'finding', 'searching', 'always'. Defaults to 'never'.|
|discoverdn|boolean|false|none|Use anonymous bind to discover the bind DN of a user (optional)|
|groupattr|string|false|none|LDAP attribute to follow on objects returned by <groupfilter> in order to enumerate user group membership. Examples: "cn" or "memberOf", etc. Default: cn|
|groupdn|string|false|none|LDAP search base to use for group membership search (eg: ou=Groups,dc=example,dc=org)|
|groupfilter|string|false|none|Go template for querying group membership of user (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserDN, Username Example: (&(objectClass=group)(member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:={{.UserDN}})) Default: (\|(memberUid={{.Username}})(member={{.UserDN}})(uniqueMember={{.UserDN}}))|
|insecure_tls|boolean|false|none|Skip LDAP server SSL Certificate verification - VERY insecure (optional)|
|max_page_size|integer|false|none|If set to a value greater than 0, the LDAP backend will use the LDAP server's paged search control to request pages of up to the given size. This can be used to avoid hitting the LDAP server's maximum result size limit. Otherwise, the LDAP backend will not use the paged search control.|
|request_timeout|string(duration)|false|none|Timeout, in seconds, for the connection when making requests against the server before returning back an error.|
|starttls|boolean|false|none|Issue a StartTLS command after establishing unencrypted connection (optional)|
|tls_max_version|string|false|none|Maximum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|tls_min_version|string|false|none|Minimum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any configured for specific users/groups.|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|upndomain|string|false|none|Enables userPrincipalDomain login with [username]@UPNDomain (optional)|
|url|string|false|none|LDAP URL to connect to (default: ldap://127.0.0.1). Multiple URLs can be specified by concatenating them with commas; they will be tried in-order.|
|use_pre111_group_cn_behavior|boolean|false|none|In Vault 1.1.1 a fix for handling group CN values of different cases unfortunately introduced a regression that could cause previously defined groups to not be found due to a change in the resulting name. If set true, the pre-1.1.1 behavior for matching group CNs will be used. This is only needed in some upgrade scenarios for backwards compatibility. It is enabled by default if the config is upgraded but disabled by default on new configurations.|
|use_token_groups|boolean|false|none|If true, use the Active Directory tokenGroups constructed attribute of the user to find the group memberships. This will find all security groups including nested ones.|
|userattr|string|false|none|Attribute used for users (default: cn)|
|userdn|string|false|none|LDAP domain to use for users (eg: ou=People,dc=example,dc=org)|
|userfilter|string|false|none|Go template for LDAP user search filer (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserAttr, Username Default: ({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})|
|username_as_alias|boolean|false|none|If true, sets the alias name to the username|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|dereference_aliases|never|
|dereference_aliases|finding|
|dereference_aliases|searching|
|dereference_aliases|always|
|tls_max_version|tls10|
|tls_max_version|tls11|
|tls_max_version|tls12|
|tls_max_version|tls13|
|tls_min_version|tls10|
|tls_min_version|tls11|
|tls_min_version|tls12|
|tls_min_version|tls13|

This can be used to avoid hitting the LDAP server's maximum result size limit. Otherwise, the LDAP backend will not use the paged search control.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum password time-to-live.|
|password_policy|string|false|none|Password policy to use to generate passwords|
|request_timeout|string(duration)|false|none|Timeout, in seconds, for the connection when making requests against the server before returning back an error.|
|schema|string|false|none|The desired LDAP schema used when modifying user account passwords.|
|starttls|boolean|false|none|Issue a StartTLS command after establishing unencrypted connection (optional)|
|tls_max_version|string|false|none|Maximum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|tls_min_version|string|false|none|Minimum TLS version to use. Accepted values are 'tls10', 'tls11', 'tls12' or 'tls13'. Defaults to 'tls12'|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The default password time-to-live.|
|upndomain|string|false|none|Enables userPrincipalDomain login with [username]@UPNDomain (optional)|
|url|string|false|none|LDAP URL to connect to (default: ldap://127.0.0.1). Multiple URLs can be specified by concatenating them with commas; they will be tried in-order.|
|use_pre111_group_cn_behavior|boolean|false|none|In Vault 1.1.1 a fix for handling group CN values of different cases unfortunately introduced a regression that could cause previously defined groups to not be found due to a change in the resulting name. If set true, the pre-1.1.1 behavior for matching group CNs will be used. This is only needed in some upgrade scenarios for backwards compatibility. It is enabled by default if the config is upgraded but disabled by default on new configurations.|
|use_token_groups|boolean|false|none|If true, use the Active Directory tokenGroups constructed attribute of the user to find the group memberships. This will find all security groups including nested ones.|
|userattr|string|false|none|Attribute used for users (default: cn)|
|userdn|string|false|none|LDAP domain to use for users (eg: ou=People,dc=example,dc=org)|
|userfilter|string|false|none|Go template for LDAP user search filer (optional) The template can access the following context variables: UserAttr, Username Default: ({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})|
|username_as_alias|boolean|false|none|If true, sets the alias name to the username|

During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|

|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|

|eab_policy|string|false|none|Specify the policy to use for external account binding behaviour, 'not-required', 'new-account-required' or 'always-required'|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|whether ACME is enabled, defaults to false meaning that clusters will by default not get ACME support|

<h2 id="tocS_PkiConfigureAutoTidyRequest">PkiConfigureAutoTidyRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapkiconfigureautotidyrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_PkiConfigureAutoTidyRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSpkiconfigureautotidyrequest"></a>
<a id="tocspkiconfigureautotidyrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "acme_account_safety_buffer": 2592000,
  "enabled": true,
  "interval_duration": 43200,
  "issuer_safety_buffer": 31536000,
  "maintain_stored_certificate_counts": false,
  "pause_duration": "0s",
  "publish_stored_certificate_count_metrics": false,
  "revocation_queue_safety_buffer": 172800,
  "safety_buffer": 259200,
  "tidy_acme": false,
  "tidy_cert_store": true,
  "tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs": true,
  "tidy_expired_issuers": true,
  "tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle": true,
  "tidy_revocation_list": true,
  "tidy_revocation_queue": false,
  "tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations": true,
  "tidy_revoked_certs": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acme_account_safety_buffer|string(duration)|false|none|The amount of time that must pass after creation that an account with no orders is marked revoked, and the amount of time after being marked revoked or deactivated.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Set to true to enable automatic tidy operations.|
|interval_duration|string(duration)|false|none|Interval at which to run an auto-tidy operation. This is the time between tidy invocations (after one finishes to the start of the next). Running a manual tidy will reset this duration.|
|issuer_safety_buffer|string(duration)|false|none|The amount of extra time that must have passed beyond issuer's expiration before it is removed from the backend storage. Defaults to 8760 hours (1 year).|
|maintain_stored_certificate_counts|boolean|false|none|This configures whether stored certificates are counted upon initialization of the backend, and whether during normal operation, a running count of certificates stored is maintained.|
|pause_duration|string|false|none|The amount of time to wait between processing certificates. This allows operators to change the execution profile of tidy to take consume less resources by slowing down how long it takes to run. Note that the entire list of certificates will be stored in memory during the entire tidy operation, but resources to read/process/update existing entries will be spread out over a greater period of time. By default this is zero seconds.|
|publish_stored_certificate_count_metrics|boolean|false|none|This configures whether the stored certificate count is published to the metrics consumer. It does not affect if the stored certificate count is maintained, and if maintained, it will be available on the tidy-status endpoint.|
|revocation_queue_safety_buffer|string(duration)|false|none|The amount of time that must pass from the cross-cluster revocation request being initiated to when it will be slated for removal. Setting this too low may remove valid revocation requests before the owning cluster has a chance to process them, especially if the cluster is offline.|
|safety_buffer|string(duration)|false|none|The amount of extra time that must have passed beyond certificate expiration before it is removed from the backend storage and/or revocation list. Defaults to 72 hours.|
|tidy_acme|boolean|false|none|Set to true to enable tidying ACME accounts, orders and authorizations. ACME orders are tidied (deleted) safety_buffer after the certificate associated with them expires, or after the order and relevant authorizations have expired if no certificate was produced. Authorizations are tidied with the corresponding order. When a valid ACME Account is at least acme_account_safety_buffer old, and has no remaining orders associated with it, the account is marked as revoked. After another acme_account_safety_buffer has passed from the revocation or deactivation date, a revoked or deactivated ACME account is deleted.|
|tidy_cert_store|boolean|false|none|Set to true to enable tidying up the certificate store|
|tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs|boolean|false|none|Set to true to enable tidying up the cross-cluster revoked certificate store. Only runs on the active primary node.|
|tidy_expired_issuers|boolean|false|none|Set to true to automatically remove expired issuers past the issuer_safety_buffer. No keys will be removed as part of this operation.|
|tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle|boolean|false|none|Set to true to move the legacy ca_bundle from /config/ca_bundle to /config/ca_bundle.bak. This prevents downgrades to pre-Vault 1.11 versions (as older PKI engines do not know about the new multi-issuer storage layout), but improves the performance on seal wrapped PKI mounts. This will only occur if at least issuer_safety_buffer time has occurred after the initial storage migration. This backup is saved in case of an issue in future migrations. Operators may consider removing it via sys/raw if they desire. The backup will be removed via a DELETE /root call, but note that this removes ALL issuers within the mount (and is thus not desirable in most operational scenarios).|
|tidy_revocation_list|boolean|false|none|Deprecated; synonym for 'tidy_revoked_certs|
|tidy_revocation_queue|boolean|false|none|Set to true to remove stale revocation queue entries that haven't been confirmed by any active cluster. Only runs on the active primary node|
|tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations|boolean|false|none|Set to true to validate issuer associations on revocation entries. This helps increase the performance of CRL building and OCSP responses.|
|tidy_revoked_certs|boolean|false|none|Set to true to expire all revoked and expired certificates, removing them both from the CRL and from storage. The CRL will be rotated if this causes any values to be removed.|

```json
{
  "auto_rebuild": true,
  "auto_rebuild_grace_period": "12h",
  "cross_cluster_revocation": true,
  "delta_rebuild_interval": "15m",
  "disable": true,
  "enable_delta": true,
  "expiry": "72h",
  "ocsp_disable": true,
  "ocsp_expiry": "1h",
  "unified_crl": "false",
  "unified_crl_on_existing_paths": "false"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto_rebuild|boolean|false|none|If set to true, enables automatic rebuilding of the CRL|
|auto_rebuild_grace_period|string|false|none|The time before the CRL expires to automatically rebuild it, when enabled. Must be shorter than the CRL expiry. Defaults to 12h.|
|cross_cluster_revocation|boolean|false|none|Whether to enable a global, cross-cluster revocation queue. Must be used with auto_rebuild=true.|
|delta_rebuild_interval|string|false|none|The time between delta CRL rebuilds if a new revocation has occurred. Must be shorter than the CRL expiry. Defaults to 15m.|
|disable|boolean|false|none|If set to true, disables generating the CRL entirely.|
|enable_delta|boolean|false|none|Whether to enable delta CRLs between authoritative CRL rebuilds|
|expiry|string|false|none|The amount of time the generated CRL should be valid; defaults to 72 hours|
|ocsp_disable|boolean|false|none|If set to true, ocsp unauthorized responses will be returned.|
|ocsp_expiry|string|false|none|The amount of time an OCSP response will be valid (controls the NextUpdate field); defaults to 12 hours|
|unified_crl|boolean|false|none|If set to true enables global replication of revocation entries, also enabling unified versions of OCSP and CRLs if their respective features are enabled. disable for CRLs and ocsp_disable for OCSP.|
|unified_crl_on_existing_paths|boolean|false|none|If set to true, existing CRL and OCSP paths will return the unified CRL instead of a response based on cluster-local data|

```json
  "key_type": "rsa",
  "locality": [
    "string"
  ],

  "managed_key_name": "string",
  "not_after": "string",
  "not_before_duration": 30,
  "organization": [
    "string"
  ],

    "string"
  ],
  "ou": [
    "string"
  ],
  "postal_code": [
    "string"
  ],
  "private_key_format": "der",
  "province": [
    "string"
  ],
  "serial_number": "string",
  "signature_bits": 0,
  "street_address": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ttl": "string",
  "uri_sans": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|add_basic_constraints|boolean|false|none|Whether to add a Basic Constraints extension with CA: true. Only needed as a workaround in some compatibility scenarios with Active Directory Certificate Services.|
|alt_names|string|false|none|The requested Subject Alternative Names, if any, in a comma-delimited list. May contain both DNS names and email addresses.|
|common_name|string|false|none|The requested common name; if you want more than one, specify the alternative names in the alt_names map. If not specified when signing, the common name will be taken from the CSR; other names must still be specified in alt_names or ip_sans.|
|country|[string]|false|none|If set, Country will be set to this value.|
|exclude_cn_from_sans|boolean|false|none|If true, the Common Name will not be included in DNS or Email Subject Alternate Names. Defaults to false (CN is included).|
|exported|string|false|none|Must be "internal", "exported" or "kms". If set to "exported", the generated private key will be returned. This is your *only* chance to retrieve the private key!|
|format|string|false|none|Format for returned data. Can be "pem", "der", or "pem_bundle". If "pem_bundle", any private key and issuing cert will be appended to the certificate pem. If "der", the value will be base64 encoded. Defaults to "pem".|
|ip_sans|[string]|false|none|The requested IP SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list|
|key_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|key_name|string|false|none|Provide a name to the generated or existing key, the name must be unique across all keys and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|key_ref|string|false|none|Reference to a existing key; either "default" for the configured default key, an identifier or the name assigned to the key.|
|key_type|string|false|none|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec" and "ed25519" are the only valid values.|
|locality|[string]|false|none|If set, Locality will be set to this value.|
|managed_key_id|string|false|none|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_name is required. Ignored for other types.|
|managed_key_name|string|false|none|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_id is required. Ignored for other types.|
|not_after|string|false|none|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|not_before_duration|string(duration)|false|none|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|organization|[string]|false|none|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value.|
|other_sans|[string]|false|none|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|
|ou|[string]|false|none|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value.|
|postal_code|[string]|false|none|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value.|
|private_key_format|string|false|none|Format for the returned private key. Generally the default will be controlled by the "format" parameter as either base64-encoded DER or PEM-encoded DER. However, this can be set to "pkcs8" to have the returned private key contain base64-encoded pkcs8 or PEM-encoded pkcs8 instead. Defaults to "der".|
|province|[string]|false|none|If set, Province will be set to this value.|
|serial_number|string|false|none|The Subject's requested serial number, if any. See RFC 4519 Section 2.31 'serialNumber' for a description of this field. If you want more than one, specify alternative names in the alt_names map using OID 2.5.4.5. This has no impact on the final certificate's Serial Number field.|
|signature_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|street_address|[string]|false|none|If set, Street Address will be set to this value.|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the mount max TTL. Note: this only has an effect when generating a CA cert or signing a CA cert, not when generating a CSR for an intermediate CA.|
|uri_sans|[string]|false|none|The requested URI SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list.|

|exported|external|
|exported|kms|

|format|der|
|format|pem_bundle|
|key_type|rsa|
|key_type|ec|
|key_type|ed25519|
|private_key_format|""|
|private_key_format|der|
|private_key_format|pem|
|private_key_format|pkcs8|

|ou|[string]|false|none|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value.|
|permitted_dns_domains|[string]|false|none|Domains for which this certificate is allowed to sign or issue child certificates. If set, all DNS names (subject and alt) on child certs must be exact matches or subsets of the given domains (see https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.10).|
|postal_code|[string]|false|none|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value.|

|province|[string]|false|none|If set, Province will be set to this value.|

|skid|string|false|none|Value for the Subject Key Identifier field (RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.2). This value should ONLY be used when cross-signing to mimic the existing certificate's SKID value; this is necessary to allow certain TLS implementations (such as OpenSSL) which use SKID/AKID matches in chain building to restrict possible valid chains. Specified as a string in hex format. Default is empty, allowing Vault to automatically calculate the SKID according to method one in the above RFC section.|
|street_address|[string]|false|none|If set, Street Address will be set to this value.|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the mount max TTL. Note: this only has an effect when generating a CA cert or signing a CA cert, not when generating a CSR for an intermediate CA.|

|use_csr_values|boolean|false|none|If true, then: 1) Subject information, including names and alternate names, will be preserved from the CSR rather than using values provided in the other parameters to this path; 2) Any key usages requested in the CSR will be added to the basic set of key usages used for CA certs signed by this path; for instance, the non-repudiation flag; 3) Extensions requested in the CSR will be copied into the issued certificate.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alt_names|string|false|none|The requested Subject Alternative Names, if any, in a comma-delimited list. May contain both DNS names and email addresses.|
|common_name|string|false|none|The requested common name; if you want more than one, specify the alternative names in the alt_names map. If not specified when signing, the common name will be taken from the CSR; other names must still be specified in alt_names or ip_sans.|
|country|[string]|false|none|If set, Country will be set to this value.|
|exclude_cn_from_sans|boolean|false|none|If true, the Common Name will not be included in DNS or Email Subject Alternate Names. Defaults to false (CN is included).|
|format|string|false|none|Format for returned data. Can be "pem", "der", or "pem_bundle". If "pem_bundle", any private key and issuing cert will be appended to the certificate pem. If "der", the value will be base64 encoded. Defaults to "pem".|
|ip_sans|[string]|false|none|The requested IP SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list|
|issuer_name|string|false|none|Provide a name to the generated or existing issuer, the name must be unique across all issuers and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|key_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|key_name|string|false|none|Provide a name to the generated or existing key, the name must be unique across all keys and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|key_ref|string|false|none|Reference to a existing key; either "default" for the configured default key, an identifier or the name assigned to the key.|
|key_type|string|false|none|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec" and "ed25519" are the only valid values.|
|locality|[string]|false|none|If set, Locality will be set to this value.|
|managed_key_id|string|false|none|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_name is required. Ignored for other types.|
|managed_key_name|string|false|none|The name of the managed key to use when the exported type is kms. When kms type is the key type, this field or managed_key_id is required. Ignored for other types.|
|max_path_length|integer|false|none|The maximum allowable path length|
|not_after|string|false|none|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|not_before_duration|string(duration)|false|none|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|organization|[string]|false|none|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value.|
|other_sans|[string]|false|none|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|
|ou|[string]|false|none|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value.|
|permitted_dns_domains|[string]|false|none|Domains for which this certificate is allowed to sign or issue child certificates. If set, all DNS names (subject and alt) on child certs must be exact matches or subsets of the given domains (see https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.10).|
|postal_code|[string]|false|none|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value.|
|private_key_format|string|false|none|Format for the returned private key. Generally the default will be controlled by the "format" parameter as either base64-encoded DER or PEM-encoded DER. However, this can be set to "pkcs8" to have the returned private key contain base64-encoded pkcs8 or PEM-encoded pkcs8 instead. Defaults to "der".|
|province|[string]|false|none|If set, Province will be set to this value.|
|serial_number|string|false|none|The Subject's requested serial number, if any. See RFC 4519 Section 2.31 'serialNumber' for a description of this field. If you want more than one, specify alternative names in the alt_names map using OID 2.5.4.5. This has no impact on the final certificate's Serial Number field.|
|signature_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|street_address|[string]|false|none|If set, Street Address will be set to this value.|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the mount max TTL. Note: this only has an effect when generating a CA cert or signing a CA cert, not when generating a CSR for an intermediate CA.|
|uri_sans|[string]|false|none|The requested URI SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list.|
|use_pss|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to use PSS signatures when using a RSA key-type issuer. Defaults to false.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_any_name|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for any domain, regardless of allowed_domains restrictions. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_bare_domains|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for the base domains themselves, e.g. "example.com" of domains listed in allowed_domains. This is a separate option as in some cases this can be considered a security threat. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_glob_domains|boolean|false|none|If set, domains specified in allowed_domains can include shell-style glob patterns, e.g. "ftp*.example.com". See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_ip_sans|boolean|false|none|If set, IP Subject Alternative Names are allowed. Any valid IP is accepted and No authorization checking is performed.|
|allow_localhost|boolean|false|none|Whether to allow "localhost" and "localdomain" as a valid common name in a request, independent of allowed_domains value.|
|allow_subdomains|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for subdomains of domains listed in allowed_domains, including wildcard subdomains. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_token_displayname|boolean|false|none|Whether to allow "localhost" and "localdomain" as a valid common name in a request, independent of allowed_domains value.|
|allow_wildcard_certificates|boolean|false|none|If set, allows certificates with wildcards in the common name to be issued, conforming to RFC 6125's Section 6.4.3; e.g., "*.example.net" or "b*z.example.net". See the documentation for more information.|
|allowed_domains|[string]|false|none|Specifies the domains this role is allowed to issue certificates for. This is used with the allow_bare_domains, allow_subdomains, and allow_glob_domains to determine matches for the common name, DNS-typed SAN entries, and Email-typed SAN entries of certificates. See the documentation for more information. This parameter accepts a comma-separated string or list of domains.|
|allowed_domains_template|boolean|false|none|If set, Allowed domains can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated domains are also permitted.|
|allowed_other_sans|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed other names to put in SANs. These values support globbing and must be in the format <oid>;<type>:<value>. Currently only "utf8" is a valid type. All values, including globbing values, must use this syntax, with the exception being a single "*" which allows any OID and any value (but type must still be utf8).|
|allowed_serial_numbers|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed serial numbers to put in Subject. These values support globbing.|
|allowed_uri_sans|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed URIs for URI Subject Alternative Names. Any valid URI is accepted, these values support globbing.|
|allowed_uri_sans_template|boolean|false|none|If set, Allowed URI SANs can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated URI SANs are also permitted.|
|allowed_user_ids|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed user-ids to put in user system login name specified here: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1274#section-9.3.1|
|basic_constraints_valid_for_non_ca|boolean|false|none|Mark Basic Constraints valid when issuing non-CA certificates.|
|client_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for client auth use. Defaults to true. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|cn_validations|[string]|false|none|List of allowed validations to run against the Common Name field. Values can include 'email' to validate the CN is a email address, 'hostname' to validate the CN is a valid hostname (potentially including wildcards). When multiple validations are specified, these take OR semantics (either email OR hostname are allowed). The special value 'disabled' allows disabling all CN name validations, allowing for arbitrary non-Hostname, non-Email address CNs.|
|code_signing_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for code signing use. Defaults to false. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|country|[string]|false|none|If set, Country will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|email_protection_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for email protection use. Defaults to false. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|enforce_hostnames|boolean|false|none|If set, only valid host names are allowed for CN and DNS SANs, and the host part of email addresses. Defaults to true.|
|ext_key_usage|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of extended key usages. Valid values can be found at https://golang.org/pkg/crypto/x509/#ExtKeyUsage -- simply drop the "ExtKeyUsage" part of the name. To remove all key usages from being set, set this value to an empty list. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|ext_key_usage_oids|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of extended key usage oids.|
|generate_lease|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates issued/signed against this role will have Vault leases attached to them. Defaults to "false". Certificates can be added to the CRL by "vault revoke <lease_id>" when certificates are associated with leases. It can also be done using the "pki/revoke" endpoint. However, when lease generation is disabled, invoking "pki/revoke" would be the only way to add the certificates to the CRL. When large number of certificates are generated with long lifetimes, it is recommended that lease generation be disabled, as large amount of leases adversely affect the startup time of Vault.|
|issuer_ref|string|false|none|Reference to the issuer used to sign requests serviced by this role.|
|key_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|key_type|string|false|none|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec", "ed25519" and "any" are the only valid values.|
|key_usage|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of key usages (not extended key usages). Valid values can be found at https://golang.org/pkg/crypto/x509/#KeyUsage -- simply drop the "KeyUsage" part of the name. To remove all key usages from being set, set this value to an empty list. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.3.|
|locality|[string]|false|none|If set, Locality will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|max_ttl|integer(int64)|false|none|The maximum allowed lease duration. If not set, defaults to the system maximum lease TTL.|
|no_store|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates issued/signed against this role will not be stored in the storage backend. This can improve performance when issuing large numbers of certificates. However, certificates issued in this way cannot be enumerated or revoked, so this option is recommended only for certificates that are non-sensitive, or extremely short-lived. This option implies a value of "false" for "generate_lease".|
|not_after|string|false|none|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ.|
|not_before_duration|integer(int64)|false|none|The duration in seconds before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|organization|[string]|false|none|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|ou|[string]|false|none|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|policy_identifiers|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of policy OIDs, or a JSON list of qualified policy information, which must include an oid, and may include a notice and/or cps url, using the form [{"oid"="1.3.6.1.4.1.7.8","notice"="I am a user Notice"}, {"oid"="1.3.6.1.4.1.44947.1.2.4 ","cps"="https://example.com"}].|
|postal_code|[string]|false|none|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|province|[string]|false|none|If set, Province will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|require_cn|boolean|false|none|If set to false, makes the 'common_name' field optional while generating a certificate.|
|server_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for server auth use. Defaults to true. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|signature_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|street_address|[string]|false|none|If set, Street Address will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|ttl|integer(int64)|false|none|The lease duration (validity period of the certificate) if no specific lease duration is requested. The lease duration controls the expiration of certificates issued by this backend. Defaults to the system default value or the value of max_ttl, whichever is shorter.|
|use_csr_common_name|boolean|false|none|If set, when used with a signing profile, the common name in the CSR will be used. This does *not* include any requested Subject Alternative Names; use use_csr_sans for that. Defaults to true.|
|use_csr_sans|boolean|false|none|If set, when used with a signing profile, the SANs in the CSR will be used. This does *not* include the Common Name (cn); use use_csr_common_name for that. Defaults to true.|
|use_pss|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to use PSS signatures when using a RSA key-type issuer. Defaults to false.|

### Properties

|aia_path|string|false|none|Optional URI to this mount's AIA distribution point; may refer to an external non-Vault responder. This is for resolving AIA URLs and providing the {{cluster_aia_path}} template parameter and will not be used for other purposes. As such, unlike path above, this could safely be an insecure transit mechanism (like HTTP without TLS). For example: http://cdn.example.com/pr1/pki|
|path|string|false|none|Canonical URI to this mount on this performance replication cluster's external address. This is for resolving AIA URLs and providing the {{cluster_path}} template parameter but might be used for other purposes in the future. This should only point back to this particular PR replica and should not ever point to another PR cluster. It may point to any node in the PR replica, including standby nodes, and need not always point to the active node. For example: https://pr1.vault.example.com:8200/v1/pki|

<h2 id="tocS_PkiReadCrlConfigurationResponse">PkiReadCrlConfigurationResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapkireadcrlconfigurationresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_PkiReadCrlConfigurationResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSpkireadcrlconfigurationresponse"></a>
<a id="tocspkireadcrlconfigurationresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "auto_rebuild": true,
  "auto_rebuild_grace_period": "string",
  "cross_cluster_revocation": true,
  "delta_rebuild_interval": "string",
  "disable": true,
  "enable_delta": true,
  "expiry": "string",
  "ocsp_disable": true,
  "ocsp_expiry": "string",
  "unified_crl": true,
  "unified_crl_on_existing_paths": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto_rebuild|boolean|false|none|If set to true, enables automatic rebuilding of the CRL|
|auto_rebuild_grace_period|string|false|none|The time before the CRL expires to automatically rebuild it, when enabled. Must be shorter than the CRL expiry. Defaults to 12h.|
|cross_cluster_revocation|boolean|false|none|Whether to enable a global, cross-cluster revocation queue. Must be used with auto_rebuild=true.|
|delta_rebuild_interval|string|false|none|The time between delta CRL rebuilds if a new revocation has occurred. Must be shorter than the CRL expiry. Defaults to 15m.|
|disable|boolean|false|none|If set to true, disables generating the CRL entirely.|
|enable_delta|boolean|false|none|Whether to enable delta CRLs between authoritative CRL rebuilds|
|expiry|string|false|none|The amount of time the generated CRL should be valid; defaults to 72 hours|
|ocsp_disable|boolean|false|none|If set to true, ocsp unauthorized responses will be returned.|
|ocsp_expiry|string|false|none|The amount of time an OCSP response will be valid (controls the NextUpdate field); defaults to 12 hours|
|unified_crl|boolean|false|none|If set to true enables global replication of revocation entries, also enabling unified versions of OCSP and CRLs if their respective features are enabled. disable for CRLs and ocsp_disable for OCSP.|
|unified_crl_on_existing_paths|boolean|false|none|If set to true, existing CRL and OCSP paths will return the unified CRL instead of a response based on cluster-local data|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_any_name|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for any domain, regardless of allowed_domains restrictions. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_bare_domains|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for the base domains themselves, e.g. "example.com" of domains listed in allowed_domains. This is a separate option as in some cases this can be considered a security threat. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_glob_domains|boolean|false|none|If set, domains specified in allowed_domains can include shell-style glob patterns, e.g. "ftp*.example.com". See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_ip_sans|boolean|false|none|If set, IP Subject Alternative Names are allowed. Any valid IP is accepted and No authorization checking is performed.|
|allow_localhost|boolean|false|none|Whether to allow "localhost" and "localdomain" as a valid common name in a request, independent of allowed_domains value.|
|allow_subdomains|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for subdomains of domains listed in allowed_domains, including wildcard subdomains. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_token_displayname|boolean|false|none|Whether to allow "localhost" and "localdomain" as a valid common name in a request, independent of allowed_domains value.|
|allow_wildcard_certificates|boolean|false|none|If set, allows certificates with wildcards in the common name to be issued, conforming to RFC 6125's Section 6.4.3; e.g., "*.example.net" or "b*z.example.net". See the documentation for more information.|
|allowed_domains|[string]|false|none|Specifies the domains this role is allowed to issue certificates for. This is used with the allow_bare_domains, allow_subdomains, and allow_glob_domains to determine matches for the common name, DNS-typed SAN entries, and Email-typed SAN entries of certificates. See the documentation for more information. This parameter accepts a comma-separated string or list of domains.|
|allowed_domains_template|boolean|false|none|If set, Allowed domains can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated domains are also permitted.|
|allowed_other_sans|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed other names to put in SANs. These values support globbing and must be in the format <oid>;<type>:<value>. Currently only "utf8" is a valid type. All values, including globbing values, must use this syntax, with the exception being a single "*" which allows any OID and any value (but type must still be utf8).|
|allowed_serial_numbers|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed serial numbers to put in Subject. These values support globbing.|
|allowed_uri_sans|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed URIs for URI Subject Alternative Names. Any valid URI is accepted, these values support globbing.|
|allowed_uri_sans_template|boolean|false|none|If set, Allowed URI SANs can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated URI SANs are also permitted.|
|allowed_user_ids|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed user-ids to put in user system login name specified here: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1274#section-9.3.1|
|basic_constraints_valid_for_non_ca|boolean|false|none|Mark Basic Constraints valid when issuing non-CA certificates.|
|client_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for client auth use. Defaults to true. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|cn_validations|[string]|false|none|List of allowed validations to run against the Common Name field. Values can include 'email' to validate the CN is a email address, 'hostname' to validate the CN is a valid hostname (potentially including wildcards). When multiple validations are specified, these take OR semantics (either email OR hostname are allowed). The special value 'disabled' allows disabling all CN name validations, allowing for arbitrary non-Hostname, non-Email address CNs.|
|code_signing_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for code signing use. Defaults to false. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|country|[string]|false|none|If set, Country will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|email_protection_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for email protection use. Defaults to false. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|enforce_hostnames|boolean|false|none|If set, only valid host names are allowed for CN and DNS SANs, and the host part of email addresses. Defaults to true.|
|ext_key_usage|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of extended key usages. Valid values can be found at https://golang.org/pkg/crypto/x509/#ExtKeyUsage -- simply drop the "ExtKeyUsage" part of the name. To remove all key usages from being set, set this value to an empty list. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|ext_key_usage_oids|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of extended key usage oids.|
|generate_lease|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates issued/signed against this role will have Vault leases attached to them. Defaults to "false". Certificates can be added to the CRL by "vault revoke <lease_id>" when certificates are associated with leases. It can also be done using the "pki/revoke" endpoint. However, when lease generation is disabled, invoking "pki/revoke" would be the only way to add the certificates to the CRL. When large number of certificates are generated with long lifetimes, it is recommended that lease generation be disabled, as large amount of leases adversely affect the startup time of Vault.|
|issuer_ref|string|false|none|Reference to the issuer used to sign requests serviced by this role.|
|key_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|key_type|string|false|none|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec", "ed25519" and "any" are the only valid values.|
|key_usage|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of key usages (not extended key usages). Valid values can be found at https://golang.org/pkg/crypto/x509/#KeyUsage -- simply drop the "KeyUsage" part of the name. To remove all key usages from being set, set this value to an empty list. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.3.|
|locality|[string]|false|none|If set, Locality will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|max_ttl|integer(int64)|false|none|The maximum allowed lease duration. If not set, defaults to the system maximum lease TTL.|
|no_store|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates issued/signed against this role will not be stored in the storage backend. This can improve performance when issuing large numbers of certificates. However, certificates issued in this way cannot be enumerated or revoked, so this option is recommended only for certificates that are non-sensitive, or extremely short-lived. This option implies a value of "false" for "generate_lease".|
|not_after|string|false|none|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ.|
|not_before_duration|integer(int64)|false|none|The duration in seconds before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|organization|[string]|false|none|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|ou|[string]|false|none|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|policy_identifiers|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of policy OIDs, or a JSON list of qualified policy information, which must include an oid, and may include a notice and/or cps url, using the form [{"oid"="1.3.6.1.4.1.7.8","notice"="I am a user Notice"}, {"oid"="1.3.6.1.4.1.44947.1.2.4 ","cps"="https://example.com"}].|
|postal_code|[string]|false|none|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|province|[string]|false|none|If set, Province will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|require_cn|boolean|false|none|If set to false, makes the 'common_name' field optional while generating a certificate.|
|server_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for server auth use. Defaults to true. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|signature_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|street_address|[string]|false|none|If set, Street Address will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|ttl|integer(int64)|false|none|The lease duration (validity period of the certificate) if no specific lease duration is requested. The lease duration controls the expiration of certificates issued by this backend. Defaults to the system default value or the value of max_ttl, whichever is shorter.|
|use_csr_common_name|boolean|false|none|If set, when used with a signing profile, the common name in the CSR will be used. This does *not* include any requested Subject Alternative Names; use use_csr_sans for that. Defaults to true.|
|use_csr_sans|boolean|false|none|If set, when used with a signing profile, the SANs in the CSR will be used. This does *not* include the Common Name (cn); use use_csr_common_name for that. Defaults to true.|
|use_pss|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to use PSS signatures when using a RSA key-type issuer. Defaults to false.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alt_names|string|false|none|The requested Subject Alternative Names, if any, in a comma-delimited list. May contain both DNS names and email addresses.|
|common_name|string|false|none|The requested common name; if you want more than one, specify the alternative names in the alt_names map. If not specified when signing, the common name will be taken from the CSR; other names must still be specified in alt_names or ip_sans.|
|country|[string]|false|none|If set, Country will be set to this value.|
|csr|string|false|none|PEM-format CSR to be signed.|
|exclude_cn_from_sans|boolean|false|none|If true, the Common Name will not be included in DNS or Email Subject Alternate Names. Defaults to false (CN is included).|
|format|string|false|none|Format for returned data. Can be "pem", "der", or "pem_bundle". If "pem_bundle", any private key and issuing cert will be appended to the certificate pem. If "der", the value will be base64 encoded. Defaults to "pem".|
|ip_sans|[string]|false|none|The requested IP SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list|
|issuer_name|string|false|none|Provide a name to the generated or existing issuer, the name must be unique across all issuers and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|issuer_ref|string|false|none|Reference to a existing issuer; either "default" for the configured default issuer, an identifier or the name assigned to the issuer.|
|locality|[string]|false|none|If set, Locality will be set to this value.|
|max_path_length|integer|false|none|The maximum allowable path length|
|not_after|string|false|none|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|not_before_duration|string(duration)|false|none|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|organization|[string]|false|none|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value.|
|other_sans|[string]|false|none|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|

|not_after|string|false|none|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ|
|other_sans|[string]|false|none|Requested other SANs, in an array with the format <oid>;UTF8:<utf8 string value> for each entry.|
|private_key_format|string|false|none|Format for the returned private key. Generally the default will be controlled by the "format" parameter as either base64-encoded DER or PEM-encoded DER. However, this can be set to "pkcs8" to have the returned private key contain base64-encoded pkcs8 or PEM-encoded pkcs8 instead. Defaults to "der".|
|remove_roots_from_chain|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to remove self-signed CA certificates in the output of the ca_chain field.|
|serial_number|string|false|none|The Subject's requested serial number, if any. See RFC 4519 Section 2.31 'serialNumber' for a description of this field. If you want more than one, specify alternative names in the alt_names map using OID 2.5.4.5. This has no impact on the final certificate's Serial Number field.|
|signature_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The requested Time To Live for the certificate; sets the expiration date. If not specified the role default, backend default, or system default TTL is used, in that order. Cannot be larger than the role max TTL.|
|uri_sans|[string]|false|none|The requested URI SANs, if any, in a comma-delimited list.|
|use_pss|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to use PSS signatures when using a RSA key-type issuer. Defaults to false.|
|user_ids|[string]|false|none|The requested user_ids value to place in the subject, if any, in a comma-delimited list. Restricted by allowed_user_ids. Any values are added with OID 0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.1.|

<h2 id="tocS_PkiTidyRequest">PkiTidyRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapkitidyrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_PkiTidyRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSpkitidyrequest"></a>
<a id="tocspkitidyrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "acme_account_safety_buffer": 2592000,
  "issuer_safety_buffer": 31536000,
  "pause_duration": "0s",
  "revocation_queue_safety_buffer": 172800,
  "safety_buffer": 259200,
  "tidy_acme": false,
  "tidy_cert_store": true,
  "tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs": true,
  "tidy_expired_issuers": true,
  "tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle": true,
  "tidy_revocation_list": true,
  "tidy_revocation_queue": false,
  "tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations": true,
  "tidy_revoked_certs": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acme_account_safety_buffer|string(duration)|false|none|The amount of time that must pass after creation that an account with no orders is marked revoked, and the amount of time after being marked revoked or deactivated.|
|issuer_safety_buffer|string(duration)|false|none|The amount of extra time that must have passed beyond issuer's expiration before it is removed from the backend storage. Defaults to 8760 hours (1 year).|
|pause_duration|string|false|none|The amount of time to wait between processing certificates. This allows operators to change the execution profile of tidy to take consume less resources by slowing down how long it takes to run. Note that the entire list of certificates will be stored in memory during the entire tidy operation, but resources to read/process/update existing entries will be spread out over a greater period of time. By default this is zero seconds.|
|revocation_queue_safety_buffer|string(duration)|false|none|The amount of time that must pass from the cross-cluster revocation request being initiated to when it will be slated for removal. Setting this too low may remove valid revocation requests before the owning cluster has a chance to process them, especially if the cluster is offline.|
|safety_buffer|string(duration)|false|none|The amount of extra time that must have passed beyond certificate expiration before it is removed from the backend storage and/or revocation list. Defaults to 72 hours.|
|tidy_acme|boolean|false|none|Set to true to enable tidying ACME accounts, orders and authorizations. ACME orders are tidied (deleted) safety_buffer after the certificate associated with them expires, or after the order and relevant authorizations have expired if no certificate was produced. Authorizations are tidied with the corresponding order. When a valid ACME Account is at least acme_account_safety_buffer old, and has no remaining orders associated with it, the account is marked as revoked. After another acme_account_safety_buffer has passed from the revocation or deactivation date, a revoked or deactivated ACME account is deleted.|
|tidy_cert_store|boolean|false|none|Set to true to enable tidying up the certificate store|
|tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs|boolean|false|none|Set to true to enable tidying up the cross-cluster revoked certificate store. Only runs on the active primary node.|
|tidy_expired_issuers|boolean|false|none|Set to true to automatically remove expired issuers past the issuer_safety_buffer. No keys will be removed as part of this operation.|
|tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle|boolean|false|none|Set to true to move the legacy ca_bundle from /config/ca_bundle to /config/ca_bundle.bak. This prevents downgrades to pre-Vault 1.11 versions (as older PKI engines do not know about the new multi-issuer storage layout), but improves the performance on seal wrapped PKI mounts. This will only occur if at least issuer_safety_buffer time has occurred after the initial storage migration. This backup is saved in case of an issue in future migrations. Operators may consider removing it via sys/raw if they desire. The backup will be removed via a DELETE /root call, but note that this removes ALL issuers within the mount (and is thus not desirable in most operational scenarios).|
|tidy_revocation_list|boolean|false|none|Deprecated; synonym for 'tidy_revoked_certs|
|tidy_revocation_queue|boolean|false|none|Set to true to remove stale revocation queue entries that haven't been confirmed by any active cluster. Only runs on the active primary node|
|tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations|boolean|false|none|Set to true to validate issuer associations on revocation entries. This helps increase the performance of CRL building and OCSP responses.|
|tidy_revoked_certs|boolean|false|none|Set to true to expire all revoked and expired certificates, removing them both from the CRL and from storage. The CRL will be rotated if this causes any values to be removed.|

<h2 id="tocS_PkiWriteIssuerRequest">PkiWriteIssuerRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapkiwriteissuerrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_PkiWriteIssuerRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSpkiwriteissuerrequest"></a>
<a id="tocspkiwriteissuerrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "crl_distribution_points": [
    "string"
  ],
  "enable_aia_url_templating": false,
  "issuer_name": "string",
  "issuing_certificates": [
    "string"
  ],
  "leaf_not_after_behavior": "err",
  "manual_chain": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ocsp_servers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "revocation_signature_algorithm": "",
  "usage": [
    "read-only",
    "issuing-certificates",
    "crl-signing",
    "ocsp-signing"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|crl_distribution_points|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of URLs to be used for the CRL distribution points attribute. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.13.|
|enable_aia_url_templating|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to enabling templating of the above AIA fields. When templating is enabled the special values '{{issuer_id}}', '{{cluster_path}}', '{{cluster_aia_path}}' are available, but the addresses are not checked for URL validity until issuance time. Using '{{cluster_path}}' requires /config/cluster's 'path' member to be set on all PR Secondary clusters and using '{{cluster_aia_path}}' requires /config/cluster's 'aia_path' member to be set on all PR secondary clusters.|
|issuer_name|string|false|none|Provide a name to the generated or existing issuer, the name must be unique across all issuers and not be the reserved value 'default'|
|issuing_certificates|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of URLs to be used for the issuing certificate attribute. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.2.1.|
|leaf_not_after_behavior|string|false|none|Behavior of leaf's NotAfter fields: "err" to error if the computed NotAfter date exceeds that of this issuer; "truncate" to silently truncate to that of this issuer; or "permit" to allow this issuance to succeed (with NotAfter exceeding that of an issuer). Note that not all values will results in certificates that can be validated through the entire validity period. It is suggested to use "truncate" for intermediate CAs and "permit" only for root CAs.|
|manual_chain|[string]|false|none|Chain of issuer references to use to build this issuer's computed CAChain field, when non-empty.|
|ocsp_servers|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of URLs to be used for the OCSP servers attribute. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.2.1.|
|revocation_signature_algorithm|string|false|none|Which x509.SignatureAlgorithm name to use for signing CRLs. This parameter allows differentiation between PKCS#1v1.5 and PSS keys and choice of signature hash algorithm. The default (empty string) value is for Go to select the signature algorithm. This can fail if the underlying key does not support the requested signature algorithm, which may not be known at modification time (such as with PKCS#11 managed RSA keys).|
|usage|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list (or string slice) of usages for this issuer; valid values are "read-only", "issuing-certificates", "crl-signing", and "ocsp-signing". Multiple values may be specified. Read-only is implicit and always set.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_any_name|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for any domain, regardless of allowed_domains restrictions. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_bare_domains|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for the base domains themselves, e.g. "example.com" of domains listed in allowed_domains. This is a separate option as in some cases this can be considered a security threat. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_glob_domains|boolean|false|none|If set, domains specified in allowed_domains can include shell-style glob patterns, e.g. "ftp*.example.com". See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_ip_sans|boolean|false|none|If set, IP Subject Alternative Names are allowed. Any valid IP is accepted and No authorization checking is performed.|
|allow_localhost|boolean|false|none|Whether to allow "localhost" and "localdomain" as a valid common name in a request, independent of allowed_domains value.|
|allow_subdomains|boolean|false|none|If set, clients can request certificates for subdomains of domains listed in allowed_domains, including wildcard subdomains. See the documentation for more information.|
|allow_wildcard_certificates|boolean|false|none|If set, allows certificates with wildcards in the common name to be issued, conforming to RFC 6125's Section 6.4.3; e.g., "*.example.net" or "b*z.example.net". See the documentation for more information.|
|allowed_domains|[string]|false|none|Specifies the domains this role is allowed to issue certificates for. This is used with the allow_bare_domains, allow_subdomains, and allow_glob_domains to determine matches for the common name, DNS-typed SAN entries, and Email-typed SAN entries of certificates. See the documentation for more information. This parameter accepts a comma-separated string or list of domains.|
|allowed_domains_template|boolean|false|none|If set, Allowed domains can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated domains are also permitted.|
|allowed_other_sans|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed other names to put in SANs. These values support globbing and must be in the format <oid>;<type>:<value>. Currently only "utf8" is a valid type. All values, including globbing values, must use this syntax, with the exception being a single "*" which allows any OID and any value (but type must still be utf8).|
|allowed_serial_numbers|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed serial numbers to put in Subject. These values support globbing.|
|allowed_uri_sans|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed URIs for URI Subject Alternative Names. Any valid URI is accepted, these values support globbing.|
|allowed_uri_sans_template|boolean|false|none|If set, Allowed URI SANs can be specified using identity template policies. Non-templated URI SANs are also permitted.|
|allowed_user_ids|[string]|false|none|If set, an array of allowed user-ids to put in user system login name specified here: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1274#section-9.3.1|
|backend|string|false|none|Backend Type|
|basic_constraints_valid_for_non_ca|boolean|false|none|Mark Basic Constraints valid when issuing non-CA certificates.|
|client_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for client auth use. Defaults to true. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|cn_validations|[string]|false|none|List of allowed validations to run against the Common Name field. Values can include 'email' to validate the CN is a email address, 'hostname' to validate the CN is a valid hostname (potentially including wildcards). When multiple validations are specified, these take OR semantics (either email OR hostname are allowed). The special value 'disabled' allows disabling all CN name validations, allowing for arbitrary non-Hostname, non-Email address CNs.|
|code_signing_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for code signing use. Defaults to false. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|country|[string]|false|none|If set, Country will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|email_protection_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for email protection use. Defaults to false. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|enforce_hostnames|boolean|false|none|If set, only valid host names are allowed for CN and DNS SANs, and the host part of email addresses. Defaults to true.|
|ext_key_usage|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of extended key usages. Valid values can be found at https://golang.org/pkg/crypto/x509/#ExtKeyUsage -- simply drop the "ExtKeyUsage" part of the name. To remove all key usages from being set, set this value to an empty list. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|ext_key_usage_oids|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of extended key usage oids.|
|generate_lease|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates issued/signed against this role will have Vault leases attached to them. Defaults to "false". Certificates can be added to the CRL by "vault revoke <lease_id>" when certificates are associated with leases. It can also be done using the "pki/revoke" endpoint. However, when lease generation is disabled, invoking "pki/revoke" would be the only way to add the certificates to the CRL. When large number of certificates are generated with long lifetimes, it is recommended that lease generation be disabled, as large amount of leases adversely affect the startup time of Vault.|
|issuer_ref|string|false|none|Reference to the issuer used to sign requests serviced by this role.|
|key_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use. Allowed values are 0 (universal default); with rsa key_type: 2048 (default), 3072, or 4096; with ec key_type: 224, 256 (default), 384, or 521; ignored with ed25519.|
|key_type|string|false|none|The type of key to use; defaults to RSA. "rsa" "ec", "ed25519" and "any" are the only valid values.|
|key_usage|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of key usages (not extended key usages). Valid values can be found at https://golang.org/pkg/crypto/x509/#KeyUsage -- simply drop the "KeyUsage" part of the name. To remove all key usages from being set, set this value to an empty list. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.3.|
|locality|[string]|false|none|If set, Locality will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum allowed lease duration. If not set, defaults to the system maximum lease TTL.|
|no_store|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates issued/signed against this role will not be stored in the storage backend. This can improve performance when issuing large numbers of certificates. However, certificates issued in this way cannot be enumerated or revoked, so this option is recommended only for certificates that are non-sensitive, or extremely short-lived. This option implies a value of "false" for "generate_lease".|
|not_after|string|false|none|Set the not after field of the certificate with specified date value. The value format should be given in UTC format YYYY-MM-ddTHH:MM:SSZ.|
|not_before_duration|string(duration)|false|none|The duration before now which the certificate needs to be backdated by.|
|organization|[string]|false|none|If set, O (Organization) will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|ou|[string]|false|none|If set, OU (OrganizationalUnit) will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|policy_identifiers|[string]|false|none|A comma-separated string or list of policy OIDs, or a JSON list of qualified policy information, which must include an oid, and may include a notice and/or cps url, using the form [{"oid"="1.3.6.1.4.1.7.8","notice"="I am a user Notice"}, {"oid"="1.3.6.1.4.1.44947.1.2.4 ","cps"="https://example.com"}].|
|postal_code|[string]|false|none|If set, Postal Code will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|province|[string]|false|none|If set, Province will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|require_cn|boolean|false|none|If set to false, makes the 'common_name' field optional while generating a certificate.|
|server_flag|boolean|false|none|If set, certificates are flagged for server auth use. Defaults to true. See also RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.12.|
|signature_bits|integer|false|none|The number of bits to use in the signature algorithm; accepts 256 for SHA-2-256, 384 for SHA-2-384, and 512 for SHA-2-512. Defaults to 0 to automatically detect based on key length (SHA-2-256 for RSA keys, and matching the curve size for NIST P-Curves).|
|street_address|[string]|false|none|If set, Street Address will be set to this value in certificates issued by this role.|
|ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The lease duration (validity period of the certificate) if no specific lease duration is requested. The lease duration controls the expiration of certificates issued by this backend. Defaults to the system default value or the value of max_ttl, whichever is shorter.|
|use_csr_common_name|boolean|false|none|If set, when used with a signing profile, the common name in the CSR will be used. This does *not* include any requested Subject Alternative Names; use use_csr_sans for that. Defaults to true.|
|use_csr_sans|boolean|false|none|If set, when used with a signing profile, the SANs in the CSR will be used. This does *not* include the Common Name (cn); use use_csr_common_name for that. Defaults to true.|
|use_pss|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to use PSS signatures when using a RSA key-type issuer. Defaults to false.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|key_type|rsa|
|key_type|ec|
|key_type|ed25519|
|key_type|any|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dial_timeout|string(duration)|false|none|Number of seconds before connect times out (default: 10)|
|host|string|false|none|RADIUS server host|
|nas_identifier|string|false|none|RADIUS NAS Identifier field (optional)|
|nas_port|integer|false|none|RADIUS NAS port field (default: 10)|
|port|integer|false|none|RADIUS server port (default: 1812)|
|read_timeout|string(duration)|false|none|Number of seconds before response times out (default: 10)|
|secret|string|false|none|Secret shared with the RADIUS server|
|token_bound_cidrs|[string]|false|none|Comma separated string or JSON list of CIDR blocks. If set, specifies the blocks of IP addresses which are allowed to use the generated token.|
|token_explicit_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role carry an explicit maximum TTL. During renewal, the current maximum TTL values of the role and the mount are not checked for changes, and any updates to these values will have no effect on the token being renewed.|
|token_max_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The maximum lifetime of the generated token|
|token_no_default_policy|boolean|false|none|If true, the 'default' policy will not automatically be added to generated tokens|
|token_num_uses|integer|false|none|The maximum number of times a token may be used, a value of zero means unlimited|
|token_period|string(duration)|false|none|If set, tokens created via this role will have no max lifetime; instead, their renewal period will be fixed to this value. This takes an integer number of seconds, or a string duration (e.g. "24h").|
|token_policies|[string]|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies. This will apply to all tokens generated by this auth method, in addition to any configured for specific users.|
|token_ttl|string(duration)|false|none|The initial ttl of the token to generate|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of token to generate, service or batch|
|unregistered_user_policies|string|false|none|Comma-separated list of policies to grant upon successful RADIUS authentication of an unregistered user (default: empty)|

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|block_interval|string(duration)|false|none|If set, when a client reaches a rate limit threshold, the client will be prohibited from any further requests until after the 'block_interval' has elapsed.|
|inheritable|boolean|false|none|Whether all child namespaces can inherit this namespace quota.|
|interval|string(duration)|false|none|The duration to enforce rate limiting for (default '1s').|
|path|string|false|none|Path of the mount or namespace to apply the quota. A blank path configures a global quota. For example namespace1/ adds a quota to a full namespace, namespace1/auth/userpass adds a quota to userpass in namespace1.|
|rate|number(float)|false|none|The maximum number of requests in a given interval to be allowed by the quota rule. The 'rate' must be positive.|
|role|string|false|none|Login role to apply this quota to. Note that when set, path must be configured to a valid auth method with a concept of roles.|
|type|string|false|none|Type of the quota rule.|

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backup|boolean|false|none|Specifies if using PGP-encrypted keys, whether Vault should also store a plaintext backup of the PGP-encrypted keys.|
|pgp_keys|[string]|false|none|Specifies an array of PGP public keys used to encrypt the output unseal keys. Ordering is preserved. The keys must be base64-encoded from their original binary representation. The size of this array must be the same as secret_shares.|
|require_verification|boolean|false|none|Turns on verification functionality|
|secret_shares|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of shares to split the unseal key into.|
|secret_threshold|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of shares required to reconstruct the unseal key. This must be less than or equal secret_shares. If using Vault HSM with auto-unsealing, this value must be the same as secret_shares.|
